1-2-3-the-first.name: 1-2-3 el Primero
1-2-3-the-first.meaning: The leader of the loyal midwayers in the service of Gabriel at the Caligastia betrayal, later one of the four and twenty counselors (45:4.18, 77:8.2).

rejected.reason: Without the article it reads as a ranking, not a name.

606-of-satania.name: 606 de Satania
606-of-satania.meaning: The number of Urantia as the 606th inhabited world registered in the local system of Satania (43:0.1, 49:0.3).

a-b-c-the-first.name: A-B-C el Primero
a-b-c-the-first.meaning: The designation of a secondary midwayer of the first subgroup; the eight subgroups are named A-B-C the first, second, and so on (77:6.4).

rejected.reason: A roman numeral reads as a regnal number.

aaron-old-testament.name: Aarón (Antiguo Testamento)
aaron-old-testament.meaning: The Old Testament Aaron of the Golden Calf, the subject of a sermon of Peter at Rimmon (146:1.1).

aaron-the-stone-mason.name: Aarón el cantero
aaron-the-stone-mason.meaning: A stone mason recently made whole by Jesus who told a paralytic of Jesus, so that the paralytic was lowered through the roof (148:9.2); the papers imply he is the man with the withered hand healed on the Sabbath (148:7.2, 148:7.3).

rejected.reason: 'albañil' is a bricklayer; the terms already done use 'cantero' for 'stone mason'.

abaddon.name: Abadón
abaddon.meaning: The chief of staff of Caligastia, who followed him into rebellion and is chief executive of the Urantia rebels (53:1.5).

abandonters.name: abandonters
abandonters.meaning: The permanent citizens of the Uversa headquarters spheres, created by unrevealed agents of the Ancients of Days and the seven Reflective Spirits (37:9.12, 30:1.44).

rejected.reason: Adapting the ending suggests a family with 'finalitarios' that the English does not show.
Adds the sense of 'abandonar' (to leave behind), which the papers do not state.

abandonters.note: Coined name kept in the English spelling; a Spanish reader can still hear 'abandonar' in it.

abel.name: Abel
abel.meaning: The first child of Adam and Eve born in the second garden, a herder (76:2.1).

abila.name: Abila
abila.meaning: A town of the Decapolis where the apostles did personal work (138:9.3).

abimelech.name: Abimelec
abimelech.meaning: The ruler at Gerar who took Abraham's wife; Abraham later made converts among his people, who sacrificed first-born sons (93:9.3, 93:9.4).

abiram.name: Abiram
abiram.meaning: The first-born son of a petty king of Palestine, put alive in the foundation of the walls of Jericho (89:6.6).

abner.name: Abner
abner.meaning: The chief of the disciples of John the Baptist, later head of the seventy messengers and leader of the church at Philadelphia (Papers 163, 166, 171).

aborigines-australian.name: aborígenes (australianos)
aborigines-australian.meaning: The natives of Australia, cited as survivors of primitive, antisocial social conditions (68:1.6).

aborigines-indian.name: aborígenes (de la India)
aborigines-indian.meaning: The so-called aborigines of India: not representative of the early mixed peoples of India but the most inferior southern and eastern fringe, never fully absorbed by the Andites or the Aryans (79:2.2).

rejected.reason: "indios" also names the native peoples of the Americas, a wrong reading for most Latin American readers.
Fine in a sentence, but the parallel term "aborígenes (australianos)" is already set; keep the same head word.

abraham-old-testament.name: Abraham (Antiguo Testamento)
abraham-old-testament.meaning: The Hebrew patriarch who became the pupil of Melchizedek and an ancestor of Joseph (93:5.1).

abraham-the-pharisee.name: Abraham el fariseo
abraham-the-pharisee.meaning: A young, influential member of the Sanhedrin who publicly accepted Jesus' teachings and was baptized by Abner in the pool of Siloam (148:8.1).

absalom.name: Absalón
absalom.meaning: Absalom, a son of King David whose mother was a Canaanite; today he might be called a demagogue (97:9.15).

rejected.reason: The English spelling; Spanish uses the standard biblical form.

absolute.name: Absoluto
absolute.meaning: The one Absolute of infinity (three Absolutes on subinfinite levels), conceived as the impersonal reaction of the Trinity; also the Buddhist concept of the Eternal One (56:9.5, Paper 94).

rejected.reason: The neuter article makes it an abstract quality; the papers treat it as a reality parallel to 'the Trinity' (56:9.5).

absolute-buddha.name: Buda Absoluto
absolute-buddha.meaning: The Buddhist concept of the Buddha as the Eternal One of infinite existence, the Buddhist approach to Deity (Paper 94).

rejected.reason: 'Buda' is the standard Spanish form of the historical name (rule 2).

absolute-deity.name: Deidad Absoluta
absolute-deity.meaning: Deity on the absolute level; the absolute aspect of Deity, distinct from the Deity Absolute (0:1.13, 56:9).

rejected.reason: That is the form of 'Deity Absolute'; the order of the English words marks two terms.

absolute-mind-person.name: Mente Absoluta (persona)
absolute-mind-person.meaning: The Infinite Spirit as the personalization of absolute mind (3:1.8, 9:7.4).

rejected.reason: 'Intelecto' would break the 'mind = mente' family.

absolute-person.name: Persona Absoluta
absolute-person.meaning: The Eternal Son, the absolute personality, though not in the experiential sense the personalization of the Absolute (0:5.5, 56:9.5).

rejected.reason: 'Personality' and 'person' are different English words; 0:5.5 uses 'absolute personality' separately.

absolutes.name: Absolutos
absolutes.meaning: The seven Absolutes of Infinity, the eternal and co-ordinate premises of all reality (Father, Son, Spirit, Paradise, and the three potential Absolutes); 'three absolute actuals' names the Father, Son, and Spirit or the actual side against the three potential Absolutes (Paper 105, 0:11).

rejected.reason: False friend: Spanish 'actual' means 'current, present-day'.
'Actualizado' commonly means 'updated'.
'Real' also means 'royal', and as a noun a coin.

absoniters.name: absonitarios
absoniters.meaning: Beings of the absonite level, not created but eventuated (0:1.12).

rejected.reason: The same form as the adjective "absonito"; "-ario" follows "finaliters: finalitarios".
Says they make things absonite.

absonity.name: absonidad
absonity.meaning: The quality or level of the absonite, between finite and absolute, which Paradise arrivals study after divinity (0:9.2, 30:4.31).

rejected.reason: Less natural; "-idad" matches "divinity: divinidad".

achaia.name: Acaya
achaia.meaning: The Roman province in Greece where Luke wrote his Gospel in the year 82 (121:8.8).

acropolis.name: Acrópolis
acropolis.meaning: The Acropolis of Athens, under whose shadow Paul spoke to the council of the Areopagus (195:1.1).

rejected.reason: Lowercase is the common noun for any citadel; here it names the one in Athens.

act-of-god.name: Acto de Dios
act-of-god.meaning: The children of the Infinite Spirit are truly the "Act of God," as the divine Sons are the "Word of God": God speaks through the Son and acts through the Infinite Spirit (10:3.3).

rejected.reason: "Acción" reads as an activity in progress; the English is a single act, set beside "Word" (Palabra).
"Obra" means a work or product, not the act itself; it changes the pairing with "Palabra de Dios".
Legal sense of English "act of God"; the authors do not mean this. The reader must not bring the insurance or legal sense of "acto de Dios" to the term.

act-of-god.note: Keep the quotation marks of 10:3.3 in running text («Acto de Dios») so the legal sense of "acto de Dios" (force majeure) does not intrude.

actium.name: Accio
actium.meaning: Actium, the site of the battle that Augustus commemorated by the founding of Nicopolis, the "city of victory" (133:2.5).

rejected.reason: Latin form; Spanish uses "Accio" for the battle (batalla de Accio).

acts-book-of.name: Hechos, libro de los
acts-book-of.meaning: The second of three books that Luke planned on Christ and Christianity; he died in A.D. 90 just before he finished it (121:8.8).

rejected.reason: Not the Spanish title of the book.

actual.name: actual
actual.meaning: That which exists in fullness of expression, in contrast to the potential, which carries undisclosed capacity for growth (0:4.7, 115:3.16).

rejected.reason: Collides with 'realidad' (reality), of which the actual is only one phase (0:4.1, 0:4.7).
Breaks the family with 'actualizar' and also means 'cash'.
The reader must not bring 'current, present-day'. The sense is 'existing in act'.

actual.note: The packet names 'actual' as a false friend. I keep it only because the papers set 'actual' against 'potential' in a philosophical sense, which Spanish philosophy writes as 'actual / en acto'. A human must decide if readers will take it as 'current'.

actual-the.name: Actual, lo
actual-the.meaning: The triodity of actuality: the union of the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, and the Paradise Isle, which is the actual revelation of the originality of the First Source and Center (115:3.7).

rejected.reason: Masculine article reads as a person; the English names a union of three, so the neuter 'lo' fits.
Collides with 'realidad' (reality).

actual-the.note: Same false-friend risk as 'actual': 'lo actual' reads as 'what is current'. The capital helps, but a human must check it.
forcedChoices: Spanish needs an article; I chose the neuter 'lo', which the context (a union, not a person) supports.

adam.name: Adán
adam.meaning: The Material Son sent with Eve to Urantia as a biologic uplifter (51:0.1).

adam-original-of-satania.name: Adán (el original de Satania)
adam-original-of-satania.meaning: The first and original Material Son of Satania, whose name every Material Son sent as a biologic uplifter carries (51:0.1).

adam-village.name: Adam (aldea)
adam-village.meaning: A village in Perea, east of the Jordan, near which John the Baptist made his attack on Herod Antipas (135:10.2, 165:0.1).

rejected.reason: Same form as the term already done for Adam, the person.

forcedChoices: English uses one spelling for the man and the village; Spanish 'Adán' is the man, so the village keeps 'Adam' to stay distinct.

adamites.name: Adamitas
adamites.meaning: The violet race, the descendants of Adam and Eve on Urantia, who mixed with the evolutionary races to uplift them biologically.

rejected.reason: Possible adjective, but the noun form parallels 'Anditas' and 'Andonitas' already chosen.

adamson.name: Adamson
adamson.meaning: The first-born son of Adam and Eve, who with Ratta founded a center north of the second garden and became an origin of the secondary midwayers (77:5.6, 80:7.3).

rejected.reason: The name exists only in this book, so the English spelling stays; a translation hides that it is a name.

adamson.note: Adam is "Adán" in Spanish, so a reviewer can choose to keep "Adamson" (book-only name, rule 3) or adapt it. I keep it.

adamsonites.name: Adamsonitas
adamsonites.meaning: The descendants of Adamson and Ratta, who kept a high culture for almost seven thousand years at their center east of the Caspian Sea (77:5.9, 78:1.3).

aden.name: Aden
aden.meaning: Aden, a man who taught and worked in Jesus' name without being with the apostles; John forbade him, but he went on and raised up believers at Kanata (159:2.1, 159:2.4).

rejected.reason: This is the Spanish name of the city in Yemen; the term is a person, so keep the English spelling to keep the two apart.

aden.note: The person's name is spelled like the city of Adén; a reader can take it for the city. The spelling without the accent marks the difference.

adirondack-mountains.name: montes Adirondack
adirondack-mountains.meaning: The ancient Adirondack Mountains of North America, part of an east-west ridge of primitive fossil-bearing rock (58:7.4).

rejected.reason: Calque of the English; Spanish geography writes lowercase "montes" before the proper name, as in "montes Apalaches".

adjuster-expression.name: expresión del Ajustador
adjuster-expression.meaning: The expression of the indwelling Adjuster through the mortal mind and personality (Paper 110).

rejected.reason: Not natural Spanish; the hyphen compound does not exist.

adjuster-fused-mortals.name: mortales fusionados con el Ajustador
adjuster-fused-mortals.meaning: Ascending mortals whose souls have fused with their indwelling Thought Adjuster; one of three orders of fusion (40:9.1, 40:10.2).

rejected.reason: 'Fundido' also means 'melted' or 'burnt out'.

adjuster-fusion.name: fusión con el Ajustador
adjuster-fusion.meaning: The eternal union of the surviving mortal soul with the indwelling Thought Adjuster (40:9.1, Paper 110).

rejected.reason: Reads as the Adjuster fusing with something else by itself.

adjutant-mind-spirits.name: espíritus ayudantes de la mente
adjutant-mind-spirits.meaning: Seven spirits, children of the Universe Mother Spirit, that minister mind to the lower orders of intelligent life and condition organic evolution (36:5.1, 101:5.10).

rejected.reason: A calque; the hyphen compound is not natural in Spanish.
'Adjunto' means attached or an assistant rank; less clear than 'ayudante'.

rejected.form: espíritu de valor (for spirit of courage)
rejected.reason: 'Valor' also means 'value', a frequent term in the papers; 'coraje' has one sense.

rejected.form: espíritu de culto (for spirit of worship)
rejected.reason: 'Culto' is ritual or a sect; 'adoración' is the act of worship.

adjutants-of-havona-circuits.name: ayudantes de los circuitos de Havona
aliases: Ayudantes Duodécuples de los Circuitos de Havona
adjutants-of-havona-circuits.meaning: The twelve adjutants of each Circuit Spirit of Havona, before whom ascending pilgrims pass the tests of a circle to move inward (26:5.5).

rejected.form: asistentes de los circuitos de Havona
rejected.reason: The terms already done use 'ayudante' for 'adjutant' (espíritus ayudantes de la mente).

administrative-assistants.name: asistentes administrativos
administrative-assistants.meaning: Seraphim of the administrator order who are the immediate assistants of System Sovereigns and serve as agents of the system rulers (39:4.2); the papers also use the phrase for an unrevealed corps that serves Gabriel (33:4.6).

rejected.reason: 'Auxiliar' is already used for 'Aids' (Universe Aids).

administrative-assistants.note: In everyday Spanish 'asistente administrativo' is an office job title. The phrase names two different groups (39:4.2 and 33:4.6).

administrative-enactors.name: escenificadores administrativos
administrative-enactors.meaning: The seventh group of heavenly reproducers: those who depict the significance of governmental philosophy and administrative technique, the celestial dramatists of sovereignty (44:2.9, 44:2.1).

rejected.reason: "Ejecutor" means one who carries out orders or a sentence (and "ejecutores divinos" is already a term); these beings act out, they do not execute.
"intérprete" is already used for translators of meaning (racial interpreters, interpreters of ethics).
"representador" is rare, and "representar" also means to stand in for someone, as a delegate.

administrative-enactors.note: "Enactor" here means one who acts out or stages a drama; "escenificador" carries that sense. A reviewer can check this against the other heavenly reproducer groups when they are done.

administrator-seraphim.name: serafines administradores
administrator-seraphim.meaning: The fourth order of seraphim, who serve the administration of the local systems (39:4.1).

adonai.name: Adonai
adonai.meaning: Adonai, one of the names the Semites used for their Deity because they disliked to speak its name (96:1.9).

rejected.reason: A Spanish variant spelling; "Adonai" is the more common and neutral form.

adonia.name: Adonia
adonia.meaning: Adonia, the central Asian commercial metropolis of the Andites, near the present city of Ashkhabad (79:1.4).

advisory-commission-on-ethics-and-self-g.name: Comisión Consultiva de Ética y Autogobierno
aliases: Comisión Consultiva de Ética Interuniversal y Autogobierno
advisory-commission-on-ethics-and-self-g.meaning: The Paradise reserve corps of the Faithfuls of Days, called in the papers the Advisory Commission of Interuniverse Ethics and Self-government (18:7.1).

rejected.form: Comisión Asesora de Ética y Autogobierno
rejected.reason: Also correct; "Consultiva" is the more usual name for a body that gives advice, and "asesores" is kept for advisers as persons (court advisers).

rejected.form: Comisión Consultiva de Ética y Autonomía
rejected.reason: "autonomía" is independence from others; the English is the governing of oneself.

advisory-commission-on-ethics-and-self-g.note: The papers (18:7.1) give only the form "Advisory Commission of Interuniverse Ethics and Self-government"; I give that as the alias.

afghanistan.name: Afganistán
afghanistan.meaning: Afghanistan, in whose highlands Badonan, a descendant of Andon and Fonta, founded a primitive center of culture that lasted over half a million years (79:0.1).

africa.name: África
africa.meaning: The continent to which the indigo race and other Sangik peoples migrated, and where the indigo race remained (64:6).

agaman.name: Agaman
agaman.meaning: A widow of Damascus, one of the ten women whom Jesus commissioned for the ministering work of the kingdom (150:1.1).

agni.name: Agni
agni.meaning: The three-headed Aryan fire god, lord of the earth and a remnant of an earlier Trinity concept, sometimes exalted as head of the Vedic pantheon (94:1.3, 94:1.4).

agondonters.name: agondonters
agondonters.meaning: Agondonters: ascenders from isolated (quarantined) worlds, evolutionary will creatures who can believe without seeing, persevere when isolated, and triumph over insuperable difficulties even when alone; they keep this grouping into the Corps of the Mortal Finality (50:7.2).

rejected.reason: Would follow "finalitarios", but the nearest coined pattern, "abandonters", is kept unchanged in the terms already done; keep the -onters family visible.
An invented Spanish ending with no support in the terms already done.

ahab.name: Acab
ahab.meaning: A Hebrew king whom Elijah denounced for the murder of the Naboths to take their land (97:3.6, 97:9.19).

ahura-mazda.name: Ahura-Mazda
ahura-mazda.meaning: The supreme god at the head of Zoroaster's group of seven gods; this concept later degenerated into Sol Invictus of Mithraism (95:6.2, 98:5.3).

rejected.reason: A later Persian form; the papers use Ahura-Mazda.

ai.name: Hai
ai.meaning: Ai, the city whose ambush and wholesale slaughter, with only the king saved, the papers give as a picture of barbaric warfare (69:8.3).

rejected.reason: In Spanish, "ai" reads as the interjection "¡ay!"; the standard Spanish biblical form is "Hai".
Same sound as the interjection "¡ay!".

akkad.name: Acad
akkad.meaning: One of the Mesopotamian valley cities that held rule in turn after the Kish confederation broke up; it fell about 2500 B.C. (78:8.9, 78:8.10).

alabama.name: Alabama
alabama.meaning: A state of the United States, named in the geologic history as the end of an ancient rock ridge from Newfoundland (58:7.4).

alaska.name: Alaska
alaska.meaning: The northwest region of North America, named in the papers for its rock ridges and ancient volcanoes (58:7.4, 59:5.20).

alexander-brother-of-philo.name: Alejandro (hermano de Filón)
alexander-brother-of-philo.meaning: Alexander, a Jewish banker of Alexandria with whom Gonod did business; his brother was the philosopher Philo (130:3.9).

alexander-of-cyrene.name: Alejandro de Cirene
alexander-of-cyrene.meaning: Alexander, a son of Simon of Cyrene, who with his brother Rufus became a very effective teacher of the gospel in Africa (187:1.10).

alexander-the-great.name: Alejandro Magno
alexander-the-great.meaning: The Macedonian king who expanded Greece into an empire from the Adriatic to the Indus and spread Hellenistic civilization (195:1.7).

alexandria.name: Alejandría
alexandria.meaning: The Egyptian city of the great library, where Jesus lived as a child and later visited (Papers 122-123, 130).

allah.name: Alá
allah.meaning: Allah, Islam's clear-cut concept of the one and only Deity, the supreme God of the universe (95:7.6, 94:2.8).

rejected.reason: English transliteration; the standard Spanish form is "Alá".

almighty-supreme.name: Supremo Todopoderoso
almighty-supreme.meaning: The power aspect of the Supreme Being, the experiential power of God the Supreme that synthesizes in the grand universe (0:7.7).

rejected.reason: Order makes 'Todopoderoso' the name; in English 'Supreme' is the head noun.
Plainer Spanish is 'Todopoderoso'.

alpha-and-omega.name: Alfa y Omega
alpha-and-omega.meaning: A title that Jesus claimed: 'the beginning and the end, the first and the last' (128:1.10).

alpheus.name: Alfeo
alpheus.meaning: Alpheus, the father of the twin apostles James and Judas, fishermen of Kheresa (138:4.1).

rejected.reason: Not a Spanish form; "gemelos Alfeo" is already set.

alpheus-twins.name: gemelos Alfeo
alpheus-twins.meaning: James and Judas Alpheus, twin fishermen who were two of the twelve apostles of Jesus (Paper 139:10).

rejected.reason: Alpheus is a biblical name with a standard Spanish form.

alps.name: Alpes
alps.meaning: The European mountain range, used as a measure of height (59:1.8).

alvoring.name: Alvoring
alvoring.meaning: Alvoring, one of the seven nearest neighboring local universes of Nebadon in Orvonton (32:2.12).

amadon.name: Amadon
amadon.meaning: The Andonite associate of Van who stayed loyal in the Lucifer rebellion and gave his name to the 144 loyal Amadonites (67:6.3).

amadonites.name: Amadonitas
amadonites.meaning: The descendants of the Andonites who stayed loyal with Van and Amadon; a cultural and religious name more than a racial one (73:1.3, 67:6.2).

amatha.name: Amatha
amatha.meaning: Peter's mother-in-law, ill with malarial fever, cured later at sundown in the event at the Zebedee home (145:2.16).

rejected.reason: The name occurs only in this book; the rules keep the English spelling.

amathus.name: Amatus
amathus.meaning: A town east of the Jordan, on the east Jordan road that Jesus took back to Nazareth (128:1.14).

rejected.reason: The Spanish name of a different Amathus, the city in Cyprus.
Keeps the English-Latin spelling with 'th', which Spanish does not use.

amathus.note: I do not know an established Spanish form for this Perean town. A human must confirm 'Amatus' or choose another form.

amaziah.name: Amasías
amaziah.meaning: Amaziah, a king of Judah who defeated the Edomites, was defeated by his northern neighbors, and was assassinated by revolting rural folk (97:9.22).

amdon.name: Amdon
amdon.meaning: The Chaldean herder of Sumerian extraction in whose tent Melchizedek was first seen by mortal man (93:2.1).

amenemope.name: Amenemope
amenemope.meaning: An Egyptian teacher whose Book of Wisdom passed almost word for word into Hebrew Proverbs (95:4.5).

amenhotep-iii.name: Amenhotep III
amenhotep-iii.meaning: Amenhotep III, the Egyptian prince whose birth is pictured at Luxor with a second, identical child, the symbol of his ka (111:0.5).

rejected.reason: An older Greek-derived Spanish form; still used, but Egyptology in Spanish now prefers "Amenhotep".

amenhotep-iii.note: Both "Amenhotep III" and "Amenofis III" are standard in Spanish; a reviewer can choose one house form for all pharaohs.

amidist.name: amidista
amidist.meaning: Amidists: believers in Amida, God of the Paradise in the west, who hold that the soul can sojourn in Paradise before Nirvana and that salvation comes by faith in Amida (94:12.3).

rejected.reason: Spanish does not capitalize the name of a follower of a religion.

forcedChoices: Lowercase "amidista": Spanish writes the followers of a religion in lowercase (budistas, fariseos), as in the terms already done.

ammonites.name: amonitas
ammonites.meaning: An ancient people near the Hebrews; Saul was made king after their defeat (97:9.4).

rejected.reason: In Spanish that names the fossil mollusks, a separate use in 60:1.12.

amorites.name: amorreos
amorites.meaning: A confederation of backward clans of Palestine whose god was Chemosh; Melchizedek said they would weaken and be overcome by Abraham's descendants (93:6.2, 96:1.14).

rejected.reason: Not the standard Spanish biblical form.

amos-brother-of-jesus.name: Amós (hermano de Jesús)
amos-brother-of-jesus.meaning: Jesus' baby brother, who died after a week's illness with a high fever (127:3.13).

amos-john-mark-s-friend.name: Amós (amigo de Juan Marcos)
amos-john-mark-s-friend.meaning: John Mark's young friend whose parents, from too much love, refused to let him go with Jesus (177:2.2).

amos-kheresa-lunatic.name: Amós (lunático de Kheresa)
amos-kheresa-lunatic.meaning: The demented man who lived among the tombs of Kheresa and whose mind quieted in Jesus' presence; he believed the swine carried off his evil spirits (151:6.2, 151:6.6).

rejected.reason: States a possession that the text presents only as a legend (151:6.6).
Colloquial and less exact than the English word.

amos-kheresa-lunatic.note: "lunático" also means a moody or eccentric person in current Spanish; the reader must take it as "insane".

amos-prophet.name: Amós (profeta)
amos-prophet.meaning: The Hebrew prophet who proclaimed Yahweh the 'God of all nations' and was stoned to death (97:4.4).

amosad.name: Amosad
amosad.meaning: The leader under whom the Sethite priesthood was regenerated about 15,000 B.C., beginning a brilliant era of the second garden (78:5.1, 92:5.9).

anaxagoras.name: Anaxágoras
anaxagoras.meaning: Anaxagoras, a Greek philosopher who was a mechanist except that he recognized a First Cause, an Initial Mind (98:2.6).

anaxand.name: Anaxand
anaxand.meaning: A young Greek shipyard worker at Caesarea moved by Jesus' words about overcoming evil with good; later a church member and steward of Cornelius, who died while he ministered in the slaughter of the Jews (130:2.4, 130:2.5).

ancients-of-days.name: Ancianos de Días
ancients-of-days.meaning: The Trinity-origin rulers of the superuniverses, three on each capital, whom ascenders meet in the superuniverse (18:3.1).

rejected.reason: 'Antiguo' describes old things or former holders of a role, not an elder person.
The extra article is not in the English and makes it less like a title.

ancients-of-days-of-uversa.name: Ancianos de Días de Uversa
ancients-of-days-of-uversa.meaning: The three Trinity-origin rulers of Orvonton on Uversa, who confirm rulings of the Most Highs (93:10.6).

andes-mountains.name: cordillera de los Andes
andes-mountains.meaning: The South American mountain range, which rose in ancient geologic epochs (59:5.18).

andites.name: Anditas
andites.meaning: The best all-round human stock since the violet race, a blend of Adamite and Nodite remnants with the best of other races (78:4.3, 80:4.5).

andon-and-fonta.name: Andon y Fonta
andon-and-fonta.meaning: The first two human beings on Urantia, the parents of mankind (Paper 63).

rejected.reason: These names exist only in this book; the rule keeps the English spelling. 'Andonitas' keeps the same root.

andonites.name: Andonitas
andonites.meaning: The first human race, descendants of Andon and Fonta, swarthy hunters who resembled the present-day Eskimo (63:4.1, 63:5.6).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes peoples in lowercase, but this name exists only in this book and the packet keeps English capitals on coined terms.

andovontia.name: Andovontia
andovontia.meaning: The tertiary Universe Circuit Supervisor of Nebadon, concerned with spirit and morontia circuits, who isolated Urantia at the time of Caligastia's betrayal (37:8.3).

andrew.name: Andrés
andrew.meaning: Andrew, brother of Peter, the first apostle and chairman of the twelve (139:1.1).

andromeda.name: Andrómeda
andromeda.meaning: A very active sun-forming nebula outside the inhabited superuniverse, visible to the naked eye; a giant nova in it collapsed about fifty years before the writing (15:4.7, 41:8.3).

andronover.name: Andronover
andronover.meaning: The former spiral nebula whose center is the nucleus of the physical system to which our sun belongs (15:3.6, 57:3.2).

ang.name: Ang
ang.meaning: The member of the Prince's staff who presided over the council on food and material welfare (66:5.2).

angamon.name: Angamon
angamon.meaning: The leader of the Stoics at Rome, with whom Jesus had an all-night talk; later a friend of Paul and a supporter of the church at Rome (132:1.1, 132:5.1).

angelic-world.name: Mundo Angélico
angelic-world.meaning: The third transitional culture world of Jerusem, headquarters of the seraphic hosts of the system, surrounded by seven worlds of angelic training (45:1.5).

rejected.reason: Plain but loses the adjective form that matches 'Mundo Morontial'.

angels.name: ángeles
angels.meaning: The ministering spirits, the angelic hosts born of the Infinite Spirit and its associated creative Spirits (17:8.2).

anglo-saxons.name: anglosajones
anglo-saxons.meaning: The Anglo-Saxon peoples, whose forefathers were the blended Andite horsemen and blue men of the Russian plains, the ancestors of the Nordic races (80:4.5).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes this compound as one word.

forcedChoices: Lowercase: Spanish writes peoples and nationalities in lowercase.

angona.name: Angona
angona.meaning: The dark giant system whose near approach drew from the sun the matter that became the solar system (57:5.6, 57:5.13).

anna.name: Ana
anna.meaning: A Galilean poetess who lingered about the temple courts with Simeon and was an intimate of Zacharias (122:9.2).

annan.name: Annan
annan.meaning: Annan, a loyal daughter and spokesman for the Nodites, a member of the twelve-member Urantia committee that received Adam and Eve (74:2.5).
forcedChoices: "Annan" is a woman ("daughter"); a Spanish sentence must use feminine agreement: «Annan, una hija leal y portavoz de los noditas».

annas.name: Anás
annas.meaning: The former Jewish high priest, father-in-law of Caiaphas, who knew Jesus earlier and held the preliminary examination of Jesus (142:0.2, 183:5.1).

annon.name: Annon
annon.meaning: Annon, one of the well-known women among the ancestors of Mary, the mother of Jesus (122:1.2).

anova.name: Anova
anova.meaning: Anova, world number one of Satania, its oldest inhabited world, a satellite of a large dark planet lit by three neighboring suns (49:0.5).

ansie.name: Ansie
ansie.meaning: Ansie, one of the well-known women among the ancestors of Mary, the mother of Jesus (122:1.2).

antarctica.name: Antártida
antarctica.meaning: The southern continent, which rose with the other land masses from the Pacific depths (57:8.21).

antares.name: Antares
antares.meaning: Antares, the largest star in the local universe, a stellar cloud 450 times the diameter of the sun (41:3.2).

antioch.name: Antioquía
antioch.meaning: The city of Syria where Jesus lived for over two months on his Mediterranean journey and where Paul later preached (134:7.3).

rejected.reason: Without the accent it is the Colombian department; the ancient city is Antioquía.

antipatris.name: Antípatris
antipatris.meaning: A town of Palestine on Jesus' route to Jerusalem, from which people came to hear him (127:6.4, 143:0.1).

antonia-fortress.name: Antonia (fortaleza)
antonia-fortress.meaning: The Roman castle of Antonia in Jerusalem, a hated reminder of the Roman yoke (162:4.2).

anu.name: Anu
anu.meaning: Anu, a Mesopotamian god; with Bel and Ea one of the Babylonian triad, the gods of earth, sea, and sky (95:1.4).

apennines.name: Apeninos
apennines.meaning: The Apennines of Italy, whose highlands stood as islands when most of Europe was under the sea in the early mammal age (61:1.12).

aphrodite.name: Afrodita
aphrodite.meaning: The Greek form of the goddess Ishtar; in Rome she became Venus (95:1.7, 98:3.3).

apollo.name: Apolo
apollo.meaning: Apollo, the Greek and Roman god whose temple stood on the Palatine hill in Rome (132:0.2).

apostles-of-jesus.name: apóstoles de Jesús
apostles-of-jesus.meaning: The twelve men Jesus chose as his personal companions and ambassadors of the kingdom (138:0.1, 139:0.1).

rejected.reason: 'Ignorante' adds an insult; 'iletrado' keeps the sense of no formal schooling.

apostles-of-john-the-baptist.name: apóstoles de Juan el Bautista
apostles-of-john-the-baptist.meaning: The twelve leaders whom John the Baptist named as his apostles; they conferred and worked with Jesus' apostles (144:6.9, 150:5.1).

appalachian-mountains.name: montes Apalaches
appalachian-mountains.meaning: The mountain range of eastern North America, named for its rock layers and for arctic species left on its peaks after the last ice age (59:4.16, 61:7.16).

appian-way.name: vía Apia
appian-way.meaning: The Roman road from Capua to Rome on which Jesus, Gonod, and Ganid traveled (130:0.2).

aquila.name: Áquila
aquila.meaning: Aquila, a Jewish tentmaker, one of the Cynics whom Jesus met in Rome; with Priscilla he later lodged and worked with Paul in Corinth (133:3.12).

rejected.reason: Also used in Spanish Bibles, but read without the accent it is stressed on the second syllable; the accent marks the Latin stress.
The Spanish word for eagle; a wrong reading.

arabia.name: Arabia
arabia.meaning: The desert peninsula where the Salem missionaries failed through overorganization and where clans kept a hazy idea of one God (95:7.1, 95:7.3).

arabian-sea.name: mar Arábigo
arabian-sea.meaning: The Arabian Sea, crossed coastwise by Dravidian shipping by 7000 B.C. on the way to the Sumerian cities of the Persian Gulf (79:3.7).

rejected.reason: Also used, but "mar Arábigo" is the more usual Spanish name.

arabs.name: árabes
arabs.meaning: The swarthy nomadic tribes from a blend of the blue race remnant of the Persian peninsula with the yellow race, later upstepped by the violet race (64:7.11).

aram.name: Aram
aram.meaning: Aram, a river settlement near Erech, home of Noah the wine maker (78:7.5).

rejected.reason: The biblical Aram is the land of Syria; this Aram is a village near Erech. Do not add the Syria sense.

aram.note: Aram here is a Mesopotamian village, not the biblical land of Aram (Syria). It matches "Noé (vinicultor de Aram)" already done.

aramaic.name: arameo
aramaic.meaning: The common language of Palestine in Jesus' time, of which he first learned the Galilean dialect (123:3.1).

arbela.name: Arbela
arbela.meaning: Arbela, one of the cities and towns of Perea where the seventy and the apostles worked in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

archangels.name: arcángeles
archangels.meaning: Offspring of the Creator Son and the Universe Mother Spirit who serve the resurrection and survival of creatures (37:3.1).

rejected.reason: the reader must not bring the seven named archangels of tradition; this is an order of the local universe

archelais.name: Arquelaida
archelais.meaning: A new Greek city near the Jordan where Jesus and his associates went after southern Samaria (143:0.2).

rejected.reason: Closer to the Greek, but "Arquelaida" follows the usual Spanish adaptation of such names.

archeozoic.name: Arqueozoico
archeozoic.meaning: The name students give to the prelife era, from the time the planet reached its present size to the start of life, when water covered the whole surface (59:0.2, 78:7.4).

architects-of-being.name: Arquitectos del Ser
architects-of-being.meaning: The (unrevealed) Architects of Being, who formulate the plans by which life is constructed on the inhabited planets (36:0.1).

rejected.reason: "Existencia" narrows "Being" to the fact of existing; the English is wider.
The plural adds a meaning (the plans of individual beings) that the English does not state.

architects-of-being.note: "del Ser" with a capital can make a Spanish reader think of the Supreme Being; the English "Being" has the same capital, so the form keeps the English open.

architects-of-the-master-universe.name: Arquitectos del Universo Maestro
architects-of-the-master-universe.meaning: The absonite planners of the master universe, 28,011 in number, organized by space levels (31:9.1).

rejected.reason: breaks the 'master' family

architectural-spheres.name: esferas arquitectónicas
architectural-spheres.meaning: Worlds made to order, such as Salvington, Edentia, and Jerusem, lighted and energized independently of the suns (41:1.3, 43:0.2).

rejected.reason: Not standard Spanish.

arctic-ocean.name: océano Ártico
arctic-ocean.meaning: The northern ocean, which in an earlier epoch connected through the Ural depression with the Mediterranean (61:1.12).

arctic-regions.name: regiones árticas
arctic-regions.meaning: The far northern regions of the earth, used as a geologic reference (59:4.6).

ardnon.name: Ardnon
ardnon.meaning: Ardnon, the leader of the Chaldean priests who, told by the seraphim through the midway creatures, visited the newborn Jesus (119:7.6).

area-and-building-custodians.name: custodios de áreas y edificios
area-and-building-custodians.meaning: The seventh group of Morontia Companions, custodians of the material and morontia structures and abodes of the mansion worlds (48:3.15).

rejected.reason: "guardián" is already used for guardians (guardian angels, Celestial Guardians); "custodian" is "custodio" in the terms already done.
A janitor or caretaker; too low and changes the idea.

areopagus.name: Areópago
areopagus.meaning: The Areopagus, the council in Athens before which Paul spoke of "the Unknown God" (195:1.1).

areopolis.name: Areópolis
areopolis.meaning: Areopolis, one of the towns of Perea in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

arimathea.name: Arimatea
arimathea.meaning: Arimathea, a village whose citizens invited Jesus to visit them while he and the apostles were in Samaria; the home of Joseph of Arimathea (143:0.1, 189:4.2).

aristotle.name: Aristóteles
aristotle.meaning: The Greek philosopher, successor of Socrates and Plato, who taught that virtue is knowledge and goodness is health of the soul (98:2.6).

arius.name: Arrio
arius.meaning: Arius, whose persuasions at Nicaea would have triumphed but for Athanasius (195:0.18).

rejected.reason: Latin form; the standard Spanish form is "Arrio".

armageddon.name: Armagedón
armageddon.meaning: Armageddon, the headquarters of the orange race some 300,000 years ago under the leadership of Porshunta (64:6.12).

rejected.reason: Without the accent the Spanish stress is wrong.

armageddon.note: The papers use the name only as a place, the orange race's headquarters. Readers can bring the apocalyptic "final battle" sense to it; the papers do not mean that.

armenia.name: Armenia
armenia.meaning: Armenia, one of the lands through which Andrew journeyed after persecution scattered the apostles (139:1.12).

aroer.name: Aroer
aroer.meaning: Aroer, one of the towns of Perea in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

artemis.name: Artemisa
artemis.meaning: Artemis of the Ephesians, the most famous goddess of Asia Minor, a perpetuation of the ancient Anatolian mother goddess (133:6.1).

rejected.reason: Also used, but "Artemisa" is the usual Spanish form.

artists-of-odor.name: artistas del olor
artists-of-odor.meaning: The fourth group of designers and embellishers, celestial artisans who create symphonies for the delight of the children of light; the papers call the name an unfortunate comparison with chemical odors (44:6.6).

rejected.reason: "aroma" adds pleasantness; the English uses the plain word "odor" and says the comparison is unfortunate.
Same reason; "fragrance" is not the authors' word.
Ties the term to the physical sense of smell more than the English does.

artists-of-odor.note: "olor" is neutral in Spanish, but some readers can take it as a bad smell ("huele a algo").

aryans.name: arios
aryans.meaning: The Andite invaders of India, whose racial effect was strong only in the northern provinces (79:4.3).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes peoples in lowercase.

aryans.note: 'ario' carries modern racist political senses in Spanish. The papers use it in a historical sense.

ascending-mortals.name: mortales ascendentes
aliases: mortales fusionados con el Ajustador en ascenso
ascending-mortals.meaning: Mortals who survive and progress from the material worlds through the mansion worlds, the superuniverse, and Havona to Paradise (49:0.1, 47:3.12, 53:3.6).

rejected.reason: False friend: 'ascendiente' means an ancestor or an influence.
Plain, but does not work as a noun phrase in all contexts; the English 'ascendant' and 'ascending' both go to 'ascendente'.

ascending-pilgrims.name: peregrinos ascendentes
ascending-pilgrims.meaning: Ascending creatures of time who pass through the Havona universe on their way to Paradise (13:1.21).

ascending-sons-of-god.name: hijos de Dios ascendentes
ascending-sons-of-god.meaning: Creatures of evolutionary origin who climb toward Paradise, helped by the descending Sons; translated midwayers are registered among them (20:1.1, 40:3.1).

ascendington.name: Ascendington
ascendington.meaning: The seventh sacred world of the Father around Paradise, the home and rendezvous of the ascending pilgrims during their Havona life (13:1.21, 13:1.23).

ashdod.name: Asdod
ashdod.meaning: Ashdod, a town on Jesus' journey from Joppa through Jamnia to Gaza in A.D. 25 (134:7.4).

ashkhabad.name: Asjabad
ashkhabad.meaning: Ashkhabad, a present-day city of central Asia near the site of ancient Adonia (79:1.4).

rejected.reason: English transliteration.
A rarer Spanish spelling.

ashkhabad.note: Spanish spellings vary (Asjabad, Asgabat); a reviewer can check the house form for modern place names.

ashtaroth.name: Astarot
ashtaroth.meaning: Ashtaroth, a town where John found a man teaching in Jesus' name and forbade him (159:2.1).

rejected.reason: Kept for the goddess Ashtoreth; the two must stay apart.

ashtoreth.name: Astoret
ashtoreth.meaning: Ashtoreth, the name under which the cult of Ishtar invaded Palestine (95:1.7).

rejected.reason: Kept for the town Ashtaroth; the two must stay apart.
Kept for Astarte, the name among the northern tribes.

ashur.name: Asur
ashur.meaning: Ashur, the god of the Assyrians, one of the national gods Jeremiah said did not exist apart from Yahweh (97:6.2).

ashurbanipal.name: Asurbanipal
ashurbanipal.meaning: Ashurbanipal, an Assyrian king who sent more colonists to dwell in Samaria (143:4.1).

asia.name: Asia
asia.meaning: The continent that was the homeland of the human race and of the early civilizations (64:1.1, 78:1.1).

asmonean-palace.name: palacio asmoneo
asmonean-palace.meaning: The stately home of Herod in Jerusalem, which Joseph showed Jesus near the temple (125:1.5).

asoka.name: Asoka
asoka.meaning: Asoka, the low-caste Indian monarch who espoused Buddhism, built an empire, and sent more than seventeen thousand Buddhist missionaries over the known world (94:9.1).

rejected.reason: A more recent transliteration; "Asoka" follows the English and is common in Spanish.

assigned-sentinel-of-satania.name: Centinela Asignado de Satania
assigned-sentinel-of-satania.meaning: The Assigned Sentinel of the system of Satania, representative of the Supreme Executives and subordinate to the Associate Inspector (24:5.2).

assigned-sentinels.name: Centinelas Asignados
assigned-sentinels.meaning: Co-ordinating personalities and liaison representatives of the Seven Supreme Executives, personalized by the Infinite Spirit, who serve in rotation on the system capitals (24:5.1, 24:5.3).

assistant-teachers.name: instructores asistentes
assistant-teachers.meaning: The fourth group of superior seraphim, helpers and associates of the teaching counselors, linked with the educational work of the local universe, especially on the mansion worlds (39:2.7).

rejected.reason: "Maestro" is kept for "Master" in the terms already done; "teacher" is "instructor" (consejeros instructores).
"ayudante" is kept for "adjutant", and "profesor" is not the word used for teacher in the terms already done.

associate-circuit-supervisors.name: Supervisores Asociados de los Circuitos
associate-circuit-supervisors.meaning: The seven supervisors on the Paradise spheres of the Spirit who, with the Supreme Power Centers, co-ordinate the circuits that pass out to the seven superuniverses (24:1.8).

rejected.reason: Breaks the pattern of the done 'Supervisores de los Circuitos del Universo'.

associate-inspectors.name: Inspectores Asociados
associate-inspectors.meaning: Higher personalities of the Infinite Spirit who represent the Seven Supreme Executives in the local universes, one on each local universe headquarters as a close associate of the Union of Days (24:4.2).

associate-power-directors.name: directores asociados del poder
associate-power-directors.meaning: The first group of Master Physical Controllers, who assign and dispatch all orders of physical controllers as the energy needs of the realms change (29:4.15, 29:4.18).

associate-registrars.name: archivistas asociados
associate-registrars.meaning: Morontia recorders who serve with the spirit recorders in the supervision and custody of the records of the morontia creations (48:2.25, 30:2.115).

rejected.reason: 'registrador' is already used for 'recorder'; one English word, one Spanish word.

associate-registrars.note: 'registrar' is a separate English word from 'recorder' (registradores). 'archivista' is the closest free word; a reviewer must confirm it.

associate-transcendental-master-force-or.name: Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza Trascendentales Asociados
aliases: Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza Asociados
associate-transcendental-master-force-or.meaning: The second group of Master Force Organizers, whose pressure-presence and tension-trends bring space-energy from the puissant to the gravity stage (29:0.3, 42:2.12).

rejected.form: Organizadores Asociados Trascendentales Maestros de la Fuerza
rejected.reason: Splits "Maestros de la Fuerza" from "Organizadores"; the order follows "Controladores Físicos Maestros".

assuntia.name: Assuntia
assuntia.meaning: Assuntia, one of the local systems of Norlatiadek that are immediate neighbors of Satania (41:2.1).

assyria.name: Asiria
assyria.meaning: The empire to which the northern kingdom refused tribute, after which Israel was besieged and dispersed (97:9.21).

astarte.name: Astarté
astarte.meaning: Astarte, the name under which the cult of Ishtar reached the northern tribes (95:1.7).

athanasius.name: Atanasio
athanasius.meaning: Athanasius, a Greek from Egypt who at Nicaea defended the concept of the nature of Jesus against the persuasions of Arius (195:0.18).

athens.name: Atenas
athens.meaning: The Greek city where Paul spoke before the Areopagus about 'the Unknown God' (195:1.1).

atlantic-ocean.name: océano Atlántico
atlantic-ocean.meaning: The ocean between the Americas and Europe and Africa, named in the geologic history (61:3.9).

aton.name: Atón
aton.meaning: The Egyptian sun-god whose outward worship Ikhnaton kept while he led the disguised worship of the One God (95:5.7).

attis.name: Atis
attis.meaning: The son of Cybele in the Phrygian mystery cult (98:4.3).

augustus.name: Augusto
augustus.meaning: The Roman emperor who died in A.D. 14, with Tiberius as coemperor before his death (136:2.8, 133:2.5).

australia.name: Australia
australia.meaning: The southern continent that split from the early land mass and evolved in isolation.

avalon.name: Avalon
avalon.meaning: One of the nearest local universes to Nebadon (32:2.12).

rejected.reason: The Spanish form of the island of Arthurian legend; that is not this universe.

avalon.note: A reader can link 'Avalon' to the Arthurian legend; the papers use it only as the name of a local universe.

avonals-order-of.name: Avonales, orden de los
avonals-order-of.meaning: The order of Paradise Sons also called Magisterial Sons (20:1.11, 20:6.5).

rejected.reason: Keep the name, but Spanish forms the plural of a noun in -al with -es.

azariah.name: Azarías
azariah.meaning: Azariah, called Uzziah by Isaiah, the sixteen-year-old son of Amaziah put on the throne of Judah after his father's assassination (97:9.22).

baal.name: Baal
baal.meaning: The Canaanite god whose name means 'owner', a god of rain and of land ownership and fertility (97:3.3).

baal-perazim.name: Baal-Perazim
baal-perazim.meaning: Baal-Perazim, the place David named for a victory, because eighty per cent of his soldiers were Baalites (97:9.12).

baalites.name: baalitas
baalites.meaning: The northern and more settled Canaanites, aristocratic landlords who followed the Baal cult of property and fertility (97:3.3, 97:3.4).

babel.name: Babel
babel.meaning: The city that grew from the planned center named Bablot, later Bablod, and finally Babel (77:3.3).

bablot-architect.name: Bablot (arquitecto)
bablot-architect.meaning: The Nodite architect and builder of the tower that gave its name to the city later called Babel (77:3.3).

babylon.name: Babilonia
babylon.meaning: The Mesopotamian city of the temples of Bel-Marduk and of the Hebrew captivity (95:1.10).

babylonian-captivity.name: cautiverio babilónico
babylonian-captivity.meaning: The exile of the Jews in Babylon after Nebuchadnezzar took Jerusalem, which turned them firmly to monotheism (97:9).

rejected.reason: 'cautividad' is correct but less common than 'cautiverio'.

babylonians.name: babilonios
babylonians.meaning: The people of Babylon, who enlarged the story of man's creation to teach descent directly from the gods (74:8.6).

badonan.name: Badonan
badonan.meaning: A great-great-grandson of Andon, among whose tribes in the northwestern Indian highlands a center of culture persisted (64:3.1).

badonan-tribes.name: tribus de Badonan
badonan-tribes.meaning: The descendants of Badonan in the highlands northwest of India who kept traditions of Andon and from whose improved stock the Neanderthal race came (64:2.4, 64:3.5).

rejected.reason: Makes an adjective the English does not use.

baganda-tribes.name: tribus baganda
baganda-tribes.meaning: The Baganda tribes of Africa, which have only recently emerged from the mana level of prayer (91:0.5).

rejected.reason: Spanish usually leaves African ethnic names unchanged after "tribus".

balkans.name: Balcanes
balkans.meaning: The Balkans, one of the two routes (with the Ukraine) by which the Andonites entered Europe after 3000 B.C. (80:9.6).

baltic.name: Báltico
baltic.meaning: The Baltic sea and coast, a route by which Andonites from Siberia entered Europe and a source of the amber trade of the Nordics (80:4.2, 80:9.4).

baluchistan.name: Baluchistán
baluchistan.meaning: The highland region through which Andites moved from the Iranian grazing lands into India (79:1.1, 79:2.4).

barabbas.name: Barrabás
barabbas.meaning: The murderer whom Pilate released instead of Jesus at the demand of the crowd (185:5.4).

barak.name: Barac
barak.meaning: Barak, who with Deborah defeated Sisera at Taanach (126:1.2).

barnabas.name: Bernabé
barnabas.meaning: Barnabas, a Greek convert of the pupils of Rodan, associated with Stephen in Jerusalem (194:4.11).

bartholomew.name: Bartolomé
bartholomew.meaning: The father of the apostle Nathaniel, who died shortly after Pentecost, after which Nathaniel went to Mesopotamia and India (139:6.9).
bartholomew.note: Church tradition identifies the apostle Nathaniel with Bartholomew; the papers make Bartholomew his father. The form must not be read as the apostle.

bartimeus.name: Bartimeo
bartimeus.meaning: Bartimeus, an elderly beggar of Jericho, blind from youth, whose sight Jesus restored (171:5.1, 171:5.3).

bashan.name: Basán
bashan.meaning: Bashan, the land of King Og, whose raid by the Hebrews the papers name as brutal (69:8.3).

basques.name: vascos
basques.meaning: The Basques, with the Berbers one of two surviving branches of the blue race, though much mixed with the Saharans (80:9.11).
forcedChoices: Lowercase: Spanish writes peoples in lowercase.

batanea.name: Batanea
batanea.meaning: The region east of Galilee near whose borders Matthew Levi had his customs office (138:2.4).

bathsheba.name: Betsabé
bathsheba.meaning: The wife of the Hittite whom King David took as a wife (97:9.10).

bautan.name: Bautan
bautan.meaning: Bautan, a pupil in Gautama's school at Benares who told his teacher the Salem traditions of the Melchizedek covenant with Abraham (94:7.5).

bay-of-bengal.name: golfo de Bengala
bay-of-bengal.meaning: The Bay of Bengal, where Dravidian shipping ventured as far as the East Indies by 7000 B.C. (79:3.7).

rejected.reason: Calque; Spanish geography names this body of water "golfo de Bengala".

beauty.name: belleza
beauty.meaning: With truth and goodness one of the three divine values; the harmony and unity of reality that creatures perceive and that leads to worship (2:7, 56:10).

rejected.reason: Mostly physical attractiveness; narrower.

bedouins.name: beduinos
bedouins.meaning: The Bedouins, desert tribes whose tribal god Yahweh Moses adopted, and who believed nature spirits made the sand whirls (96:4.3, 85:4.2).

beelzebub.name: Belcebú
beelzebub.meaning: The leader of the disloyal secondary midwayers who allied themselves with Caligastia (53:1.5, 77:7.4).

beeroth.name: Beerot
beeroth.meaning: Beeroth, a town on Jesus' last tour through Palestine as a private individual, from Beersheba to Dan (134:7.5).

beersheba.name: Beerseba
beersheba.meaning: A town in the south of Palestine where Jesus stayed a week, and the southern limit of the believer centers (134:7.4, 134:7.5, 190:1.8).

rejected.reason: English spelling; the standard Spanish form of this historical town is Beerseba.

beirut.name: Beirut
beirut.meaning: Beirut, the coast city where Jesus visited the Syrian believer Malach (156:3.1).

beit-adis.name: Beit Adis
beit-adis.meaning: Beit Adis, the village near the rock cavern where Jesus lived during his forty days (136:4.14).

beit-jenn.name: Beit Jenn
beit-jenn.meaning: Beit Jenn, a village in the foothills of Mount Hermon where Jesus set up his headquarters in August A.D. 25 (134:8.1).

bel.name: Bel
bel.meaning: A Mesopotamian god, one of the seven chief deities and of the Babylonian triad with Ea and Anu, gods of earth, sea, and sky (95:1.4, 97:6.2).

bel-marduk.name: Bel-Marduk
bel-marduk.meaning: The more centralized god concept to which the Mesopotamians reduced their gods, with temples in Babylon (96:0.1, 95:1.10).

belgium.name: Bélgica
belgium.meaning: The European country, partly under water 10 million years ago and later the site of Liege, the most northerly Danubian settlement (61:4.2, 80:8.4).

benares.name: Benarés
benares.meaning: The city in India where Gautama founded his school and from which he sent students out in groups of sixty (94:7.5).

rejected.reason: Modern official name; the English uses the older name.

bengal.name: Bengala
bengal.meaning: A region of India where many people worship a meteor that fell in A.D. 1880; its bay is also named (85:1.2, 79:3.7).

berbers.name: bereberes
berbers.meaning: A North African people who, with the Basques, represent the survival of two branches of the blue race, much mixed with the Saharans (80:9.11).

rejected.reason: Also valid, but the form without the accent is more common in Latin America.

bering-strait-land-bridge.name: puente terrestre del estrecho de Bering
bering-strait-land-bridge.meaning: The land link between North America and Asia, over which the early lemurs and later peoples migrated (62:1.2).

bernice.name: Berenice
bernice.meaning: The mother of Justa; Jesus stayed in their house just north of Sidon (156:2.2).

rejected.reason: English spelling; Spanish has a standard form of this name.

bestowal.name: otorgamiento
bestowal.meaning: The act in which a Paradise Son gives himself to live as a creature (often as a mortal) on a world of his domain, and also any divine gift given (20:5.6, 20:6.5, 93:9.11).

rejected.reason: Not every bestowal is in mortal flesh, and the English uses 'incarnate' as a separate word.
Ordinary sense is a donation of money or organs.
Not natural Spanish; the reflexive verb 'otorgarse' carries the self-giving.

forcedChoices: keep 'otorgamiento' from the done term 'Pentecostés (otorgamiento del Espíritu de la Verdad)': Rule 4: one English word, one Spanish word. Note that 'otorgamiento' has a legal or administrative ring in ordinary use; the reader must take it as self-giving.

beth-marion.name: Beth-Marion
beth-marion.meaning: A Phoenician woman at Bethsaida who became so fanatical that she almost drowned when she tried to walk on the water (148:8.4).

rejected.reason: The name is known only from this book, so the English spelling stays.

beth-meon.name: Bet-meón
beth-meon.meaning: One of the cities of Perea where the seventy, Jesus, and the twelve worked in the Perean mission of A.D. 30 (165:0.1).

rejected.reason: A biblical place; Spanish has a standard form with Bet-, as in Bet-seán.

beth-nimrah.name: Bet-nimra
beth-nimrah.meaning: One of the towns of Perea where the seventy, Jesus, and the twelve worked in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

rejected.reason: A biblical place; the Spanish pattern uses Bet-.

beth-peor.name: Bet-peor
beth-peor.meaning: One of the towns of Perea where the seventy, Jesus, and the twelve worked in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

rejected.reason: A biblical place; the Spanish pattern uses Bet-.

beth-shean.name: Bet-seán
beth-shean.meaning: The ancient Hebrew city that became Scythopolis, the chief Greek city of the Decapolis, which Jesus visited with Joseph (124:3.6).

rejected.reason: Also used, but less close to the English form.

beth-zur.name: Bet-sur
beth-zur.meaning: The home town of Ezda, the orphan boy who kept the herds of John the Baptist (135:3.1).

rejected.reason: A biblical place; the Spanish pattern uses Bet-.

bethany-beyond-jordan.name: Betania más allá del Jordán
aliases: Betania al otro lado del Jordán
bethany-beyond-jordan.meaning: The place across the Jordan where Jesus and the apostles stayed for some weeks of teaching (141:7.2).

bethany-near-jerusalem.name: Betania (cerca de Jerusalén)
bethany-near-jerusalem.meaning: The village near Jerusalem, home of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary, where Jesus first stayed with them in his youth (125:2.7).

bethel.name: Betel
bethel.meaning: A town in Samaria on the route from Nazareth to Jerusalem by Jacob's well (124:6.1).

bethesda-pool.name: Betesda (estanque)
bethesda-pool.meaning: A hot-spring pool outside a Jerusalem gate, with five porches, where the sick waited for healing and Jesus spoke to them on a Sabbath (147:3.1, 147:3.6).

rejected.reason: "piscina" today suggests a swimming pool; "estanque" matches the form already used for Siloam.

bethlehem-galilee.name: Belén (Galilea)
bethlehem-galilee.meaning: A Galilean town, not the Judean Bethlehem, where Joseph worked and the apostles later did personal work (123:3.8, 138:9.3).

bethlehem-judea.name: Belén (Judea)
bethlehem-judea.meaning: The town in Judea, the City of David, where Jesus was born.

bethphage.name: Betfagé
bethphage.meaning: A hamlet a short distance northwest of Bethany, off the main road, where the colt was found and where Jesus and Thomas stayed with friends (172:3.6, 168:3.7, 191:0.13).

rejected.reason: The papers spell it Bethpage, but this is the historical village; the standard Spanish form is Betfagé.

bethsaida.name: Betsaida
bethsaida.meaning: The fishing harbor near Capernaum, home of several apostles and a center of Jesus' work (129:1.2, 150:1.1).

bethsaida-julias.name: Betsaida-Julias
bethsaida-julias.meaning: A city near the park where about five thousand gathered before the feeding (152:2.4, 157:2.1).

bildad.name: Bildad
bildad.meaning: The second of Job's friends, whose counsel held that God cannot be unjust and that Job's suffering proves sin (148:6.5, 148:6.9).

bithynia.name: Bitinia
bithynia.meaning: A region of Asia Minor through which Matthew preached and baptized after he left Jerusalem (139:7.10).

black-forest-mountains.name: montes de la Selva Negra
black-forest-mountains.meaning: European mountains whose formation began in the Carboniferous epoch, with the Vosges and the Urals (59:5.12).

black-friday.name: Viernes Negro
black-friday.meaning: The most holy day of the Phrygian mysteries, the "day of blood" that commemorated the self-inflicted death of Attis (98:4.7).

rejected.reason: In Spanish this English form means the modern shopping day.
Translates the gloss "day of blood", which the text gives separately.

black-friday.note: "Viernes Negro" also names a modern shopping day or a market crash; the context of the Attis cult must carry the sense.

black-sea.name: mar Negro
black-sea.meaning: The sea between Europe and Asia whose regions supplied iron ore to Andite metalworkers (80:6.3).

blackfoot-indians.name: indios pies negros
blackfoot-indians.meaning: A North American tribe among whom many later descendants of Onamonalonton survive (64:6.7).

blue-race.name: raza azul
blue-race.meaning: One of the six colored Sangik races of Urantia, which spread in Europe and later mixed with the Andites and Adamites.

bon.name: Bon
bon.meaning: The member of the Prince's staff who directed the board of animal domestication and utilization (66:5.4).

borneans.name: borneanos
borneans.meaning: The people of Borneo, who still kill a slave to go with his dead master on the ghost journey (87:2.8).

rejected.reason: Correct but a phrase, not a name.

bosora.name: Bosora
bosora.meaning: One of the cities of Perea where the seventy, Jesus, and the twelve worked in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

rejected.reason: Can be read as a different, better-known city; the English form is kept.

brahma.name: Brahma
brahma.meaning: The first member of the Hindu Trimurti, conceived as self-created out of the Brahman (infinity), identified with fate, and a deity-father principle that could have founded a concept of the Universal Father (94:4.4, 94:1.4, 94:1.5).

rejected.reason: The English has no diacritic; the plain form is standard in Spanish.
A different term in the glossary (the infinity from which Brahma is self-created).

brahman.name: Brahman
brahman.meaning: The Hindu concept of the Absolute, the infinite IT IS, the Universal Self existing static and potential through all eternity, never conceived as a personality (94:3.3).

rejected.reason: The personal creator god of Hinduism, a different concept.

brahmanas.name: Brahmanas
brahmanas.meaning: Later Hindu scriptures compiled with the Upanishads, when the Brahmanic priests sought true reality and depersonalized the concept of God (94:2.6).

rejected.reason: Means the priests (Brahmans), not the scriptures.

brahmanism.name: brahmanismo
brahmanism.meaning: The religious philosophy of India under the Brahman priests, which came near the idea of the indwelling Adjuster but held that no human individuality exists apart from the indwelling Universal One (94:3.6).

breath-giver.name: Dador del Aliento
aliases: Dador del Aliento a los hombres y a los animales
breath-giver.meaning: The name of the deity that Onagar led the Andonic tribes to worship, the 'Breath Giver to men and animals' (63:6.1, 45:4.3, 64:1.7).

rejected.reason: Changes the image; the English names breath, not life.
Reads as a description, not as a name; the English uses a title.
'Donante' has the sense of a blood or organ donor.

breath-giver.note: 'Dador' is correct but slightly formal; a reviewer can check that it reads naturally as a divine title.

brenner-pass.name: paso del Brennero
brenner-pass.meaning: The Alpine pass by which the Nordics traded amber with the Danubians (80:9.4).

bretons.name: bretones
bretons.meaning: The people of Brittany, survivors of the original Andonite inhabitants of western Europe mixed with Mediterranean stock (80:9.14).

bright-and-morning-stars.name: Resplandecientes Estrellas Matutinas
bright-and-morning-stars.meaning: The first order of Universe Aids, one in each local universe, the first-born of its native creatures and its chief executive; Gabriel is the one of Nebadon (37:1.9).

rejected.reason: 'Brillantes' is already 'Brilliant' in 'Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas'; one English word has one translation.
Repeats 'Brillantes' and reads awkwardly.
A common name of the planet Venus, and of Lucifer in tradition.

forcedChoices: The English 'Bright and Morning' joins two qualifiers with 'and'; a literal 'y' reads awkwardly in Spanish, so both qualify 'Estrellas' without the conjunction, parallel to 'Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas'.

brilliant-evening-stars.name: Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas
brilliant-evening-stars.meaning: Superangels of the local universe who serve as liaison officers of Gabriel, some created and some ascendant (37:2.1).

rejected.reason: the ordinary name of the planet Venus
also reads as Venus

brilliant-evening-stars-chief.name: Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas (jefe)
aliases: jefe de las Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas
brilliant-evening-stars-chief.meaning: The head of the Brilliant Evening Stars in the local universe, who has custody of and dispatches all personal communications (39:2.17).
forcedChoices: Spanish "jefe" is masculine; the English "chief" has no gender. I keep the masculine as the unmarked form.

british-columbia.name: Columbia Británica
british-columbia.meaning: A Canadian province where, 70 million years ago, Cambrian rocks were thrust fifteen miles over Cretaceous layers (60:3.14).

british-isles.name: Islas Británicas
british-isles.meaning: The island group of northwestern Europe that includes Great Britain and Ireland (historical geography, standard Spanish form).

rejected.reason: Excludes Ireland; it is only the alias form.

brittany.name: Bretaña
brittany.meaning: A region of western France where older Andonite stock kept some identity and old sun-worship superstitions persist among the Bretons (80:4.6, 80:9.14).

rejected.reason: Great Britain is a different place; a reader can confuse plain "Bretaña" with it, so the alias "Bretaña francesa" helps where the context is weak.

broadcast-directors.name: directores de difusiones
broadcast-directors.meaning: Thought conservers among the celestial artisans who supervise, censor, edit, adapt, and translate the broadcasts of Paradise, the superuniverses, and the local universes (44:4.9, 44:4.10).

rejected.reason: "broadcasts" is already "difusiones" in the glossary.

broadcast-receivers.name: receptores de difusiones
broadcast-receivers.meaning: The fifth group of primary seconaphim, who receive a special class of broadcast messages and synchronize the reflective vision of the Ancients of Days with them (28:4.12, 29:4.29).

rejected.reason: "transmisores" is already the form for energy transmitters; "difusiones" is the done form for broadcasts.
Names a radio set, a device, not a being.

broadcasters-superior-seraphim.name: difusores (serafines superiores)
broadcasters-superior-seraphim.meaning: Seraphic recorders among the superior seraphim who send out records and essential information (39:2.9).

rejected.reason: ties the term to radio technology
technical sense of a device or a currency issuer

broadcasters-tertiary-supernaphim.name: difusores (supernafines terciarios)
broadcasters-tertiary-supernaphim.meaning: The tertiary supernaphim of the third Circuit Spirit, master technicians who receive and send the broadcasts of the central creation and direct the space reports of Deity phenomena on Paradise (26:3.6).

rejected.reason: "broadcasters" is already "difusores" for the superior seraphim; one word, one translation.

broadcasts-celestial.name: difusiones (celestiales)
broadcasts-celestial.meaning: The communications sent from Paradise, the superuniverses, and the local universes, received on the capitals and displayed to all beings, such as the stream of space reports (44:4.9, 46:3.1).

rejected.reason: Correct, but 'broadcasters' is already 'difusores'; the family keeps one root.
Also means a release of money or of gases.

broadcasts-celestial.note: 'difusión' is also a general word for spreading news. The context shows a broadcast.

bronze-age.name: Edad del Bronce
bronze-age.meaning: The cultural period of bronze tools that overlapped the New Stone Age, associated with mother worship in Scandinavia (80:9.13).

rejected.reason: Less usual; 'Edad del Bronce' is the standard Spanish name of the period.

brotherhood-of-man.name: fraternidad de los hombres
brotherhood-of-man.meaning: The relationship of all persons as brothers that follows from the fatherhood of God, preached together with it in the gospel (193:0.4, 140:10.9).

rejected.reason: In Spanish the singular can read as the brotherhood of one man.
'Hermandad' also means a guild or confraternity; 'brotherhood' is already 'fraternidad' in 'espíritus de la fraternidad'.
Changes the noun 'man' to an adjective and loses 'el hombre'.

brotherhood-of-united-midwayers.name: Fraternidad de los Seres Intermedios Unidos
brotherhood-of-united-midwayers.meaning: The united corps of primary and secondary midwayers on Urantia, in whose name the narrator of the Jesus papers writes (121:8.14, 77:8.1).

rejected.form: Hermandad de los Seres Intermedios Unidos
rejected.reason: 'brotherhood' is already 'fraternidad' in 'espíritus de la fraternidad'; one word keeps one translation.

brown-race.name: raza parda
brown-race.meaning: The blend of the red and yellow races that held the islands off the Asiatic coast (64:7.16, 78:3.8, 94:5.6).

rejected.reason: 'moreno' commonly means dark-haired or tanned.
'marrón' is not used in all regions for skin color.

buddha.name: Buda
buddha.meaning: The title given to Gautama; Jesus said Buddha was better than Buddhism, a great man and prophet who lost sight of his spiritual Father (92:5.12, 132:7.4).

buddha-sakyamuni.name: Buda, Sakyamuni
buddha-sakyamuni.meaning: A later title of Gautama given by his disciples, after "the enlightened one" and "the Buddha" (94:8.2, 94:11.3).

rejected.reason: A valid spelling, but the English writes Sakyamuni.

buddhism.name: budismo
buddhism.meaning: The religion that grew from the teachings of Gautama Buddha (94:8.1, 94:11.1).

burma.name: Birmania
burma.meaning: The region where Indian and Chinese cultures blended and the green race persisted most (79:2.4, 79:6.2).

bushmen.name: bosquimanos
bushmen.meaning: A small people of southern Africa with a primitive culture (66:5.30).

caesarea.name: Cesarea
caesarea.meaning: The coastal city built by Herod, the Roman capital of Palestine.

caesarea-philippi.name: Cesarea de Filipo
caesarea-philippi.meaning: The city in the north of Palestine where Jesus and the apostles stayed and taught for two weeks (155:2.1).

rejected.reason: Less usual than 'Cesarea de Filipo'.

caiaphas.name: Caifás
caiaphas.meaning: The acting high priest and son-in-law of Annas, before whom Jesus was tried (183:5.1).

cain.name: Caín
cain.meaning: The son of Eve who killed Abel, later repented and received an Adjuster (76:2.8).

caleb.name: Caleb
caleb.meaning: With Joshua, one of the only two of the hosts out of Egypt who lived to enter the promised land, according to the Scriptures (166:3.2).

calebites.name: calebitas
calebites.meaning: A non-Hebrew nomadic group that formed part of David's kingdom of Judah at Hebron (97:9.7).

caledonian-mountains.name: montes Caledonianos
caledonian-mountains.meaning: A great mountain range raised about 290 million years ago, from Ireland through Scotland to Spitzbergen (59:3.3).

rejected.reason: Less used; Spanish geology says "caledoniano".

california.name: California
california.meaning: The region on the western coast of North America.

caligastia.name: Caligastia
caligastia.meaning: The Planetary Prince of Urantia who joined the Lucifer rebellion and was deposed (67:6.5 context).

caligastia-one-hundred.name: cien de Caligastia
caligastia-one-hundred.meaning: The corporeal members of the Planetary Prince's staff, fifty men and fifty women, who came to Urantia in material bodies (66:2.3, 66:4.2).

rejected.reason: Is a military staff; the papers mean a corps of assistants and teachers.
The English writes 'one hundred' in lowercase.

caligula.name: Calígula
caligula.meaning: The Roman emperor at whose court Selta, the writer of a Jewish apocalyptic text, served (176:2.8).

callirrhoe.name: Calírroe
callirrhoe.meaning: One of the towns of Perea where the seventy, Jesus, and the twelve worked in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

cambrian.name: Cámbrico
cambrian.meaning: The geologic period of fifty million years of early marine life that geologists name the Cambrian (59:1.20, 59:1.15, 60:3.14).

rejected.reason: Not the standard Spanish geologic term.

cana.name: Caná
cana.meaning: The Galilean town where Jesus turned water into wine (138:8.5).

canaanites.name: cananeos
canaanites.meaning: The non-Hebrew inhabitants of Palestine with whom the Israelites united and intermarried to form the Hebrew nation, and whose tribal worship included Yahweh and the golden calves (97:9.1, 97:9.13, 96:1.12).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes the names of peoples in lowercase, as with 'filisteos' already in the glossary.

canada.name: Canadá
canada.meaning: The present North American country, where the oldest fossil-bearing rock layer comes to the surface (58:7.4).

cano.name: Cano
cano.meaning: The brilliant leader of the friendly Nodites near the Garden who met Eve in secret and believed in the Serapatatia plan (75:3.7, 75:3.8).
cano.note: Spanish "cano" is an adjective for gray hair. The capital marks the name, but a reader can notice the common word.

cape-horn.name: cabo de Hornos
cape-horn.meaning: The southern tip of South America, the end of the mountain range that runs from Alaska (60:3.2, 60:3.12).

capernaum.name: Cafarnaúm
capernaum.meaning: The fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee, Jesus' headquarters in his public work (Papers 129-150).

rejected.reason: Less common; 'Cafarnaúm' is the usual Spanish form.

capetown.name: Ciudad del Cabo
capetown.meaning: A city of South Africa that the papers contrast with the crude culture of the Bushmen to the north (66:5.30).

capitolias.name: Capitolias
capitolias.meaning: One of the cities of Perea where the seventy, Jesus, and the twelve worked in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

capitolium.name: Capitolio
capitolium.meaning: The Capitoline hill in Rome with the temple of Jupiter, Juno, and Minerva, where Jesus often went to ponder the bondage of ignorance of the Romans (132:0.2).

rejected.reason: Latin form; Spanish has a standard form.

cappadocia.name: Capadocia
cappadocia.meaning: A region of Asia Minor through which Matthew preached and baptized after he left Jerusalem (139:7.10).

capua.name: Capua
capua.meaning: An Italian city where Jesus and his companions stopped three days before going on the Appian Way to Rome (130:8.6, 130:0.2).

carboniferous.name: Carbonífero
carboniferous.meaning: The geologic period of the coal age, the fern-forest age of frogs; its active stage began 200 million years ago (58:7.10, 59:5.10, 59:5.13).

caribbean-region.name: región del Caribe
caribbean-region.meaning: The Caribbean area, which was highly elevated in early geologic ages (59:1.5, 59:2.2).

carpathians.name: Cárpatos
carpathians.meaning: European highlands that stood above the water as islands when most of Europe was submerged (61:1.12).

carrara-marble.name: mármol de Carrara
carrara-marble.meaning: Marble that comes from limestone laid down in the southern Alps by a sea invasion in the early reptilian age (60:1.4).

carthage.name: Cartago
carthage.meaning: The city of northern Africa near an old Andite colony, visited by Jesus and Ganid (80:7.11, 130:0.2, 130:6.6).

caspian-sea.name: mar Caspio
caspian-sea.meaning: The inland sea whose southeastern region Jesus reached as conductor of a caravan from April A.D. 24 for a year (134:2.1).
caspian-sea.note: The packet summary gives the dates as 'April 24 to April 25 CE'; 134:2.1 says the trip began on April 1, A.D. 24, and lasted a full year.

caspin.name: Caspin
caspin.meaning: One of the towns of Perea where the seventy, Jesus, and the twelve worked in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

catskill-mountains.name: montes Catskill
catskill-mountains.meaning: Mountains on the west bank of the Hudson River, one of the largest geologic monuments of the Devonian floods 240 million years ago (59:4.15).

caucasians.name: caucásicos
caucasians.meaning: The generalized homogeneity of the so-called white races, which comes from Andite inheritance; the papers call it Caucasoid (78:4.4, 81:4.14).

rejected.reason: Not the usual Spanish adjective; "caucásico" is common, "caucasoide" is the technical form for Caucasoid.

caucasians.note: "caucásico" also means 'of the Caucasus region'; the context of race must decide.

cedes.name: Cedes
cedes.meaning: A believer at Antioch who made a brief record of Jesus' life in A.D. 78, one of Luke's sources (121:8.9).

celestial-artisans.name: artesanos celestiales
celestial-artisans.meaning: Recruited artists and artisans of the morontia and lower spirit realms, organized in seven divisions (Paper 44).

celestial-guardians.name: Guardianes Celestiales
celestial-guardians.meaning: Twice-trinitized sons, co-ordinates of the High Son Assistants, commissioned to the courts of the Ancients of Days (22:1.12).
celestial-guardians.note: "guardianes" is also used in "ángeles guardianes" and "guardianes del destino"; the capitals separate this order.

celestial-musicians.name: músicos celestiales
celestial-musicians.meaning: Celestial artisans who produce celestial harmony by the manipulation of spirit forces (44:1.2).

celestial-overseers.name: Superintendentes Celestiales
celestial-overseers.meaning: A recruited corps of over three million volunteers in Nebadon who serve as educational advisers and inspectors of the local universe school system (37:6.1, 30:2.146).

rejected.reason: "Supervisores" already renders "Supervisors" (Supreme Center Supervisors); one English word, one Spanish word.
The papers use "inspectors" as a description of their work (37:6.1), not as the name.
Archaic or regional in most countries.

celestial-recorders.name: Registradores Celestiales
celestial-recorders.meaning: Ascendant seraphim who make all superuniverse records in duplicate, a spirit original and a semimaterial copy (25:6.1, 25:6.5).

celsus.name: Celso
celsus.meaning: A host of Jesus and the apostles at Caesarea-Philippi (157:3.7).

celta.name: Celta
celta.meaning: The daughter of a Roman centurion, one of the women Jesus commissioned for the ministering work of the kingdom (150:1.1).

rejected.reason: Changes the name; rule 3 keeps the spelling.

celta.note: In Spanish "celta" is the common word for a Celt; the capital letter and the context must show it is a personal name.

cenozoic.name: Cenozoico
cenozoic.meaning: The mammalian era of the last fifty million years, the recent-times era (59:0.6, 61:0.2, 61:1.10).

rejected.reason: The English uses the noun alone; 'el Cenozoico' is the standard noun form.

census-directors.name: Directores del Censo
census-directors.meaning: Higher personalities of the Infinite Spirit, with headquarters on the superuniverse capitals, who keep the record of will creatures (24:0.10, 24:2.3).

central-america.name: América Central
central-america.meaning: The region where a mixed race, mainly red with yellow, orange, and blue elements, founded lasting civilizations (64:7.5, 79:5.8).

central-universe.name: universo central
central-universe.meaning: Havona, the eternal and perfect creation of a billion worlds around the Isle of Paradise (0:0.5).

ceylon.name: Ceilán
ceylon.meaning: The island south of India reached by the least progressive Saharan group and where Buddhism became established (80:2.2, 92:6.16, 94:9.1).

rejected.reason: The modern name; the English uses the historical name.

ch-in-shih-huang-ti.name: Ch'in Shih Huang Ti
