ch-in-shih-huang-ti.meaning: A Chinese emperor whose imperial efforts against the Confucian doctrines failed (94:6.11).

rejected.reason: The modern pinyin form; the glossary keeps the older romanization (Sinkiang, Honan).

ch-in-shih-huang-ti.note: A reviewer must decide between the book's Wade-Giles form and the pinyin form now common in Spanish.

chaldeans.name: caldeos
chaldeans.meaning: Eastern Semites near Ur, among the most advanced of them, and star worshipers who saw themselves as children of the sky father and the earth mother (96:2.1, 85:5.1).

chang.name: Chang
chang.meaning: A Chinese merchant in Corinth whom Jesus told to worship only God, his true spirit ancestor (133:4.9).

charax.name: Cárax
charax.meaning: The port where Jesus parted from Gonod and Ganid, who sailed for India (130:0.3, 133:9.4).

rejected.reason: 'ch' reads as a Spanish 'ch' sound.

chazan-of-nazareth-synagogue.name: jazán de la sinagoga de Nazaret
chazan-of-nazareth-synagogue.meaning: The officer of the synagogue who taught the children of Nazareth, Jesus' teacher (123:5.3, 123:5.5).

rejected.reason: English spelling; Spanish has an adapted form.
The later sense of the word; here he is the teacher of the school.

chazan-of-nazareth-synagogue.note: In modern use the word means the cantor of the synagogue; the papers use the older sense of school officer.

chedorlaomer.name: Quedorlaomer
chedorlaomer.meaning: The enemy over whom Abraham won a victory, after which Abraham offered a conventional sacrifice (93:4.14).

chemosh.name: Quemos
chemosh.meaning: The god of the Amorites, whose actuality the Hebrews conceded but held subordinate to Yahweh (96:1.14).

cherubim-and-sanobim.name: querubines y sanobines
cherubim-and-sanobim.meaning: Paired assistants of the seraphim, the cherubim energy positive and the sanobim energy negative, near the morontia level (38:7.2, 38:7.3, 38:7.6).

rejected.reason: the family seraphim→serafines, cherubim→querubines needs the same Spanish plural
the reader must not bring the image of winged infants; these are working assistants

forcedChoices: masculine gender for querubín and sanobín: Spanish nouns need a gender; the papers write 'her' for some angels, but the noun stays masculine

chicago.name: Chicago
chicago.meaning: The U.S. city, used to show the value of sunlight, and, per the packet, the city that the papers call "the city of this visitation" (58:2.1, 113:2.7).
chicago.note: 58:2.1 names Chicago; 113:2.7 says "the city of this visitation" without naming it. The identification of the two comes from the entity data, not from the text.

chief-of-mystery-monitors.name: jefe de los Monitores de Misterio
chief-of-mystery-monitors.meaning: The being who presides over the college of Personalized Adjusters on Divinington and advises Master Spirit Number One (Paper 107).

rejected.reason: 'Misteriosos' describes them as secretive; the English uses 'Mystery' as a name element.

chief-of-nebadon-archangels.name: jefe de los arcángeles de Nebadon
aliases: Jefe de los Arcángeles de Nebadon
chief-of-nebadon-archangels.meaning: The head of the archangels of Nebadon, who called the council of the resurrection after Jesus' burial and asked for custody of his body, and who presented Paper 33 (189:0.1, 189:2.1, 33:8.7).

rejected.reason: Changes the structure; the English names the chief of a group.

chief-of-nebadon-voices.name: jefe de las Voces de Nebadon
aliases: Jefe de las Voces de Nebadon
chief-of-nebadon-voices.meaning: The primary seconaphim chief who, on request, presents the Michael seconaphim of record so that the Ancients of Days perceive the voice and attitude of Michael of Nebadon (28:4.6).
forcedChoices: "jefe" is masculine; the English "chief" has no gender and seconaphim are angels. The masculine is the generic form.

chief-of-urantia-cherubim.name: jefe de los querubines de Urantia
chief-of-urantia-cherubim.meaning: The chief of the cherubim on Urantia, who sat on the advisory council of the planetary receivers (114:1.4).

chief-of-urantia-seraphim.name: jefe de los serafines de Urantia
chief-of-urantia-seraphim.meaning: The supernaphim who commands the seraphic hosts on Urantia, a post that rotates (114:6.20, 113:0.1).

chief-supernaphim.name: supernafín jefe
chief-supernaphim.meaning: The original pattern angel, the first angel of Paradise, who presides over all three orders of supernaphim (27:2.1).

rejected.reason: Reads as an office over the supernaphim, not as one supernaphim who is chief.

forcedChoices: The English "supernaphim" serves as singular here; Spanish needs the singular "supernafín" for one being.

chiefs-of-assignment.name: jefes de asignación
chiefs-of-assignment.meaning: Primary supernaphim who assign service on Paradise, for example a supernaphim to command the seraphim of a reclaimed isolated world (27:0.2, 27:2.2).

rejected.reason: "destino" is reserved for destiny (guardianes del destino).

china.name: China
china.meaning: The land of eastern Asia where the yellow race built a stable civilization (79:5-8).

china-seas.name: mares de China
china-seas.meaning: The seas whose dangers the Buddhist teachers faced as they carried their faith over Asia (94:9.2).

chinese.name: chinos
chinese.meaning: The people of China, mainly of the yellow race, with a long and stable civilization (79:8.1).

chorazin.name: Corazín
chorazin.meaning: A town of Galilee where Jesus and later his evangelists met the most general rejection of the gospel (146:4.6, 155:2.2).

christ.name: Cristo
christ.meaning: 'The anointed one'; the title given to Jesus and used for Michael after his bestowal, as in Christ Michael (128:7.10, 196:2.1).

christian-church-early.name: iglesia cristiana primitiva
aliases: naciente culto del cristianismo de Pablo
christian-church-early.meaning: The church that grew after Pentecost under Peter and Paul and that became a religion about Jesus, mixed with Greek and pagan elements (194:4.0, 195:0.1, 196:2.1).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes adjectives of religion in lowercase; the English capital on 'Christian' is a rule of English, not a coined term.
'Temprana' is a calque of 'early'; 'primitiva' is the plain Spanish word for the first period.

christianity.name: cristianismo
christianity.meaning: The religion about Jesus that grew after him, with more of his gospel than any other faith but with additions he did not teach (195:0.1, 196:2.1).

christmas.name: Navidad
christmas.meaning: The Christian festival whose lavish gift-giving and tree perpetuate older customs (69:5.13, 85:2.5).

rejected.reason: Regional and dated.

chronoldeks.name: chronoldeks
chronoldeks.meaning: Master Physical Controllers grouped with the frandalanks, dependable living indicators of time (29:4.11, 28:6.11).

rejected.reason: Shows the time root, but breaks the rule to keep coined names as spelled, as with 'frandalanks'.

churches.name: iglesias
churches.meaning: Religious institutions; the papers set the visible church, a social organization, against the true church, the invisible spiritual brotherhood of Jesus (195:10.11, 195:10.14).

chuza.name: Cusa
chuza.meaning: A member of Herod Antipas's official family, his steward, husband of Joanna, who told Herod that Jesus did not meddle in earthly rule (154:0.2, 150:1.1).

rejected.reason: Older Spanish Bible spelling; "Cusa" is the more common current form. Both are in use.

cicero.name: Cicerón
cicero.meaning: The Roman orator; a people that produced him and Vergil was ripe for Paul's Hellenized Christianity (195:2.6).

cincinnati-island.name: isla de Cincinnati
cincinnati-island.meaning: A Devonian landmass in North America; the land southeast of it stayed above water while much of western Europe was submerged (59:4.8).
cincinnati-island.note: The papers name it only once. The summary places it in Europe, but the text places only the submerged lands in Europe.

circuit-regulators.name: reguladores de circuitos
circuit-regulators.meaning: Morontia power supervisors who co-ordinate physical and spiritual energy, regulate its flow into the planetary morontia circuits, and act as living morontia dynamos (48:2.13, 48:2.14, 30:2.109).

rejected.reason: The English has no article; these circuits are many and planetary, not a known set.
'controladores' is used for 'controllers' elsewhere in the glossary.

circuits.name: circuitos
circuits.meaning: The paths of presence, energy, and communication that bind creation, such as the personality circuit of the Father and the mind circuit of the Conjoint Actor (0:6.1).

citizenship-registrars.name: archivistas de la ciudadanía
citizenship-registrars.meaning: Officials of the representative government of Jerusem who compute the mota status of citizens and assign their suffrage qualifications (45:7.7).

rejected.reason: "recorders" is already "registradores"; "registrars" is "archivistas" in the glossary.

city-of-judah.name: Ciudad de Judá
city-of-judah.meaning: The town in the hills four miles west of Jerusalem where Elizabeth lived, Mary visited her, and John the Baptist was born (122:2.6, 122:2.7).

rejected.reason: The English capitalizes 'City' as part of the name.

claudia-procula.name: Claudia Prócula
claudia-procula.meaning: The wife of Pontius Pilate, who heard of Jesus through her maid and after Pilate's death became known for spreading the gospel (185:1.7).

claudius.name: Claudio
claudius.meaning: A wealthy Roman slaveholder who freed one hundred and seventeen slaves after an evening with Jesus (132:4.5).

claudus.name: Claudus
claudus.meaning: A discouraged young man on Malta who, after his talk with Jesus, became a Cynic preacher and later preached Christianity in Rome, Naples, and Spain (130:8.1).

rejected.reason: Merges him with Claudius, a different person.

clement.name: Clemente
clement.meaning: Clement of Alexandria, taught by Pantaenus in the early schools that kept much of Jesus' teachings (195:3.10).

cleopas-of-emmaus.name: Cleofás de Emaús
cleopas-of-emmaus.meaning: A man of Emmaus, brother of Jacob, to whom Jesus appeared on the road from Jerusalem in his seventh morontia appearance (190:5.2, 190:5.3).

cloa.name: Cloa
cloa.meaning: One of the remarkable women among the ancestors of Mary, the mother of Jesus (122:1.2).

clopas.name: Clopás
clopas.meaning: The husband of Mary, the sister of Jesus' mother, who stood near the cross (187:3.2, 188:1.7).

rejected.reason: Already the form for Cleopas of Emmaus, a different person.

co-ordinate-creator-sons.name: Hijos Creadores Coordinados
co-ordinate-creator-sons.meaning: The Creator Sons considered as a corps of equal rank among themselves, through whom the Eternal Son functions in the local universes (6:2.2, 7:2.4, 7:5.10).

rejected.reason: Closer to 'of equal rank', but it breaks the rule that 'co-ordinate' is 'coordinar' and its family.
The chosen form can read as 'coordinated by someone'; the English means 'of the same order or rank'. A reviewer must decide.

co-ordinate-trinity-origin-beings.name: Seres Coordinados Originados en la Trinidad
co-ordinate-trinity-origin-beings.meaning: A Paradise group of Trinity-origin beings that includes the Trinity Teacher Sons, three groups of superuniverse administrators, and the Inspired Trinity Spirits (19:0.1).

rejected.form: Seres Coordinadores Originados en la Trinidad
rejected.reason: Says they co-ordinate others; the English adjective means of co-ordinate (equal) rank.
Loses 'origin'.

forcedChoices: 'Coordinados' from the done term 'co-ordinate: coordinar': The English adjective 'co-ordinate' means of equal rank or order, but Spanish 'coordinado' commonly reads as 'organized' or 'co-ordinated'; a human must check this.

co-ordinators-and-liaison-directors.name: coordinadores y directores de enlace
co-ordinators-and-liaison-directors.meaning: Morontia Companions who facilitate morontia intercourse and prevent confusion as instructors of social conduct and morontia progress (48:3.11).

college-of-high-ethics.name: Colegio de Alta Ética
college-of-high-ethics.meaning: The highest course of training in universe administration, given on the Melchizedek home world and presided over by the original Father Melchizedek (35:3.22).

college-of-wisdom.name: Colegio de la Sabiduría
college-of-wisdom.meaning: The high college on Salvington at the top of the Teacher Sons' long course of training (20:8.3).

colorado.name: Colorado
colorado.meaning: The North American region named for its Morrison fresh-water fossil beds and for the Grand Canyon of the Colorado River (60:2.5, 58:7.5).

colorado-river.name: río Colorado
colorado-river.meaning: The North American river whose Grand Canyon shows primitive fossil-bearing rocks in several layers (58:7.5).

combined-controllers.name: controladores combinados
combined-controllers.meaning: Highly mechanical Morontia Power Supervisors, one at the center of each administrative unit of a morontia world, sensitive to physical, spiritual, and morontial energies (48:2.19, 30:2.112).

complements-of-rest.name: complementos del descanso
complements-of-rest.meaning: Secondary supernaphim on the inner Havona circuit who work with the instigators of rest to prepare pilgrims for Paradise (26:4.9, 27:1.1).

rejected.reason: 'reposo' leans to physical stillness; 'descanso' is the plain word.

complements-of-rest.note: 'complemento' can read as an add-on item; here it means a colleague who completes a pair.

compound-manipulators.name: manipuladores compuestos
compound-manipulators.meaning: Celestial artisans who work with the functional association of physical, mindal, and spiritual energies and seek the universe presence of God the Supreme (44:5.5).

rejected.reason: Reads as chemical compounds and closes the English adjective.
Commentary; adds words the English does not have.

compound-manipulators.note: The English "compound" can describe the manipulators or the energy they work with; the Spanish keeps the same ambiguity.

concept-recorders.name: registradores de conceptos
concept-recorders.meaning: Thought recorders who preserve concept pictures and idea patterns by a permanent method unknown on material worlds (44:4.5).

conductors-of-worship.name: conductores de la adoración
conductors-of-worship.meaning: Primary supernaphim on Paradise who lead the outbursts of worship and teach ascenders how to worship so that they reach full satisfaction in less time (27:7.3, 27:7.4).

rejected.reason: "director" already renders "director" (directors of conduct).
"guías" already renders "guides" (Graduate Guides, Trinity guides).

conductors-of-worship.note: Spanish "conductor" most often means a driver. Here it must read as one who leads.

confucianism.name: confucianismo
confucianism.meaning: The moral teaching that grew from Confucius, which held that earthly order should mirror the order of heaven and placed the God concept below the Way of Heaven (94:6.10, 131:9.1).

confucius.name: Confucio
confucius.meaning: The sixth-century B.C. Chinese teacher who compiled the sayings of ancient sages and put morality in place of magic (92:5.12, 94:6.9).

conjoint-creator.name: Creador Conjunto
conjoint-creator.meaning: A title of the Infinite Spirit, the Third Person, who creates jointly with the Father and the Son and is the source of mind and manipulator of energy (9:3.5, 9:5.4, 9:5.5).

rejected.reason: Loses the 'conjoint' root that the papers also use in 'Conjoint Actor'.

connecticut.name: Connecticut
connecticut.meaning: A state of the United States where the great eastern-Connecticut fault appeared in the early reptilian age, one side sinking two miles (60:1.7).
connecticut.note: The summary dates the fault to the Cretaceous; the text puts it in the early reptilian age section (60:1).

constantine.name: Constantino
constantine.meaning: The Roman emperor won to Christianity after Christian leaders compromised further with paganism (195:0.10).

constellation-centers.name: Centros de las Constelaciones
constellation-centers.meaning: The fifth order of Supreme Power Centers: ten in each constellation, energy projectors to its one hundred local systems (29:2.6, 29:2.17).

rejected.reason: Rare adjective.

constellation-fathers.name: Padres de las Constelaciones
constellation-fathers.meaning: The reigning Most High of a constellation, the presiding member of its three Vorondadek rulers, who reigns ten thousand standard years (35:6.1, 43:3.2).

constellations.name: constelaciones
constellations.meaning: The administrative divisions of a local universe, each of one hundred local systems, ruled by the Most Highs (43:0.2, Paper 43).

rejected.reason: The ordinary sense of 'constelación' is a visible star pattern; the reader must not bring that sense. The same is true of the English, so the plain word stays.

consuls-universe.name: cónsules (del universo)
consuls-universe.meaning: Representatives of constellations to one another and to the universe headquarters, appointed by legislative decree, often Vorondadek Sons (33:6.4, 35:5.5).

consummator-of-universe-destiny.name: Consumador del Destino del Universo
consummator-of-universe-destiny.meaning: An unrevealed agent who probably consummates destiny, an act probably involved with the Supreme and the Ultimate in the Trinity Absolute (106:7.3).

rejected.reason: Not current Spanish; "universal" is kept for "universal".
The reader must take it as "one who brings to completion", not "consumidor" (consumer).

contact-personalities.name: personalidades de contacto
contact-personalities.meaning: The few (fewer than a score) reservists who are conscious of their role as points of contact between superhuman beings and mortals, and the midwayers who serve these contacts (114:7.8, 77:8.8).

rejected.reason: Reads as an office 'contact person'; and 'person' is a different English word.

corinth.name: Corinto
corinth.meaning: The capital of the Roman province of Achaia, visited by Jesus on his return from Rome (133:2.5).

cornelius.name: Cornelio
cornelius.meaning: A Roman centurion of Caesarea who became a believer through Peter and whose steward was Anaxand (130:2.5).

corporeal-staffs-of-planetary-princes.name: personal corpóreo de los Príncipes Planetarios
corporeal-staffs-of-planetary-princes.meaning: The one hundred ascendant volunteers who came with a Planetary Prince in material bodies as his visible helpers; on Urantia they were Caligastia's staff (77:1.2, 77:2.2, 66:4.10).

rejected.reason: The terms already done use "cuerpo" for "staff" (Van, del cuerpo del Príncipe), but "cuerpo corpóreo" repeats itself and "cuerpo" also means the body. "personal" avoids it.
Military sense.

corporeal-staffs-of-planetary-princes.note: Conflict with the earlier term "Van (del cuerpo del Príncipe)", where staff = "cuerpo". A human must decide which word "staff" takes everywhere.

corps-of-conjoint-trinitized-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trinitizados Conjuntos
corps-of-conjoint-trinitized-finaliters.meaning: One of the seven finaliter corps, located on Vicegerington, into which Havona natives are also received (31:1.5, 30:2.135).

rejected.reason: Decides that 'conjoint' modifies 'trinitized'; the English leaves it open.
Coins a new word and also closes the reading.

forcedChoices: Spanish agreement makes 'Conjuntos' grammatically modify 'Finalitarios'. A reader can still take it as 'jointly trinitized'; the done term 'Creador Conjunto' supports 'Conjunto' for 'Conjoint'.

corps-of-havona-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios de Havona
corps-of-havona-finaliters.meaning: One of the seven finaliter corps, a possible supreme destiny for Havona natives (31:1.5, 30:2.136).

corps-of-light-and-life.name: Cuerpo de Luz y Vida
corps-of-light-and-life.meaning: The corps on Paradise in which the ascendant mortals of time now serve temporarily; their final destiny is not known (31:3.2).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de la Luz y la Vida
rejected.reason: "light and life" is already "luz y vida" without articles.

corps-of-mortal-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Mortales
corps-of-mortal-finaliters.meaning: The corps that is the present known destination of the ascending Adjuster-fused mortals, with other groups also assigned to it (31:0.1, 107:2.7).

rejected.reason: Kept as the alias for 'Corps of the Finality' because it pairs with 'finalitario', but Spanish 'finalidad' usually means 'purpose', not 'final state'. A human reviewer must decide; an alternative is 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'.

corps-of-paradise-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios del Paraíso
corps-of-paradise-finaliters.meaning: The second of the seven finaliter corps in the Uversa register (30:2.133, 31:10.3).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios del Paraíso
rejected.reason: Kept for the general 'Paradise Corps of the Finality'.
Breaks the pattern 'Paradise X' = 'X del Paraíso' in the done terms.

corps-of-paradise-finaliters.note: The English aliases for this term list 'Paradise Corps of the Finality' and 'finaliter corps', but the papers use those for all seven corps (22:8.6). The papers name this corps only in two lists, so its exact membership is implied, not stated.

corps-of-perfection.name: Cuerpo de Perfección
corps-of-perfection.meaning: The local universe corps that Spirit-fused ascenders, who never become finaliters, finally join (37:5.3, 37:5.4).

rejected.reason: Possible, but the done terms use "de Perfección" without the article (Hijos Trinitizados de Perfección).

corps-of-permanent-citizens.name: cuerpo de ciudadanos permanentes
corps-of-permanent-citizens.meaning: The resident orders of beings who form the stable population of administrative worlds, such as the Material Sons on Jerusem and the susatia on Salvington (37:9.7, 37:9.12, 76:6.3).

corps-of-seraphic-completion.name: Cuerpo de Culminación Seráfica
corps-of-seraphic-completion.meaning: The corps of seraphim who traversed the circles of Seraphington, attained Paradise, and received the embrace of the Eternal Son (39:9.1).

rejected.reason: exists but is rare and stiff
suggests an ending or a stop, not an attainment

corps-of-transcendental-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trascendentales
corps-of-transcendental-finaliters.meaning: One of the seven Paradise finaliter corps, the corps related to transcendental service, to which Havona natives are also admitted (31:0, 31:8).

corps-of-trinitized-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trinitizados
corps-of-trinitized-finaliters.meaning: The finality corps that appears to be the supreme destiny of most creature-trinitized sons, one of the seven Paradise Corps of the Finality (22:8.6, 26:11.2).

rejected.reason: The article is not in the English and breaks the pattern of 'Cuerpo de Finalitarios Mortales'.

corps-of-unrevealed-sons-of-destiny.name: Cuerpo de Hijos del Destino No Revelados
corps-of-unrevealed-sons-of-destiny.meaning: The seventh of the finaliter corps, whose nature the papers do not reveal (31:10.8, 30:2.138).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de Hijos No Revelados del Destino
rejected.reason: Splits "Hijos del Destino"; the agreement of "No Revelados" with "Hijos" already shows what is unrevealed.

forcedChoices: "No Revelados" must agree in gender and number; it agrees with "Hijos", which is the reading of the English.

cosmic-consciousness.name: conciencia cósmica
cosmic-consciousness.meaning: Awareness of the realities of the universe beyond the material and local outlook; the term itself is not defined in the papers.

rejected.reason: Also valid; 'conciencia' is the more common spelling across Latin America.
The reader must not bring this; the sense is awareness.

cosmic-mind.name: mente cósmica
cosmic-mind.meaning: The sevenfold mind of time and space, a subabsolute manifestation of the mind of the Third Source and Center, ministered by the Seven Master Spirits to the superuniverses (0:6.1, 16:6).

rejected.reason: Collides with 'Universal Mind' (Mente Universal).

council-of-equilibrium.name: Consejo del Equilibrio
council-of-equilibrium.meaning: The high commissioners of power, sent by the Seven Master Spirits from the Associate Master Force Organizers, who direct the Master Physical Controllers and read the master frandalanks (29:4.2, 57:1.4).

council-of-perfection.name: consejo de perfección
council-of-perfection.meaning: A council on Paradise to which superuniverse conciliators are translated, and from which they emerge as a co-ordinating corps of the Infinite Spirit (25:3.16).

rejected.reason: The English has no article; the article would suggest an abstract named Perfection.

council-of-planetary-princes.name: consejo de los Príncipes Planetarios
aliases: consejo de sistema de los gobernantes de mundos
council-of-planetary-princes.meaning: The system council of world rulers, the Planetary Princes and resident governors general, over which the System Sovereign presides at the system headquarters (45:2.4, 114:3.4).

council-of-seven.name: consejo de siete
council-of-seven.meaning: The council of the red man, after the teaching of Onamonalonton, whose rule was unanimous (70:5.4).

rejected.reason: Suggests seven known persons, which the English does not say.

council-of-seventy.name: consejo de setenta
council-of-seventy.meaning: A council at the constellation headquarters, selected from evolutionary beings, analogous to the twenty-four counselors (50:2.2).

rejected.reason: Can be confused with "the seventy" messengers of Jesus' time.

counselors-and-advisers.name: consejeros y asesores
counselors-and-advisers.meaning: The sixth order of secondary supernaphim, who counsel Paradise pilgrims and also comfort those who fail in their first effort at Deity attainment (26:4.8, 26:10.2).

rejected.reason: 'consultor' suggests a paid business consultant.

counselors-and-advisers.note: The same English phrase is used as plain words for the Unions of Days (18:6.1); there it is not the name of an order.

court-advisers.name: asesores de los tribunales
court-advisers.meaning: Supreme seraphim attached to all orders of adjudication who see that charges against mortals are stated in justice and adjudicated in mercy, often as defenders of mortals (39:1.7, 39:1.8).

rejected.reason: 'corte' also means a royal court, a sense the English does not intend.
'consejero' is the glossary form for 'counselor', and 'adviser' is 'asesor' (counselors and advisers: consejeros y asesores).

court-of-gentiles.name: atrio de los gentiles
court-of-gentiles.meaning: The outer court of the Jerusalem temple open to gentiles (125:4.3, 162:4.3).

rejected.reason: 'corte' is a royal or judicial court.

court-of-israel.name: atrio de Israel
court-of-israel.meaning: A court of the Jerusalem temple from which steps led down to the court of the women (162:4.3).

court-of-priests.name: atrio de los sacerdotes
court-of-priests.meaning: The court of the Jerusalem temple, below the rock ledge in front of the temple, where the altar stood and sacrifices were made (125:1.4, 162:4.4).

rejected.reason: "corte" means a royal court or a law court, not an open area of a building.

court-of-women.name: atrio de las mujeres
court-of-women.meaning: The court of the Jerusalem temple below the court of Israel, lit by great candelabras at the feast of tabernacles, where John made his Nazarite cleansing sacrifices (162:4.2, 162:4.3, 135:2.1).

rejected.reason: False friend: 'corte' is a royal court or a tribunal, not an enclosed yard.
Correct but domestic; 'atrio' is the usual word for the courts of the temple.

court-of-women.note: Translators must use 'atrio' for the other temple courts too (court of Israel, court of the gentiles) so the set stays consistent.

courtesy-colonies.name: colonias de cortesía
courtesy-colonies.meaning: Groups of visiting beings who reside on headquarters worlds by courtesy, such as star students, celestial artisans, and reversion directors (46:5.30, 18:5.2, 37:10).

rejected.reason: Interprets the term instead of keeping the English word 'courtesy'.

crab-nebula.name: nebulosa del Cangrejo
crab-nebula.meaning: An irregular nebula that began about nine hundred years ago, with its mother sphere still a lone star near its center (41:8.4).

craftworkers-of-color.name: artífices del color
craftworkers-of-color.meaning: Designers and embellishers among the celestial artisans who make the ten thousand color tones of spirit reflection give out messages of harmonious beauty (44:6.3).

rejected.reason: "artisans" is already "artesanos"; "craftworkers" needs a different word.

creative-mother-spirits.name: Espíritus Madre Creativos
creative-mother-spirits.meaning: The local universe Mother Spirits seen in their creative partnership with the Creator Sons (Paper 34, 39:1.2 'Creative Spirit').

rejected.reason: 'Creadores' is fixed for 'Creator' (Hijos Creadores); 'Creative' is a different English word.
The reader must not bring the artistic or marketing sense; it means 'creating'.

creative-spirits.name: Espíritus Creativos
creative-spirits.meaning: The local universe Mother Spirits, Creative Daughters of the Infinite Spirit, who create and administer with the Creator Sons (8:5.3, 39:1.2).

rejected.reason: Merges 'Creative' with 'Creator'; the papers keep the two words apart.

creator-sons.name: Hijos Creadores
creator-sons.meaning: The makers and rulers of the local universes, Paradise Sons of the order of Michael, born of the Father and the Eternal Son (21:0.1, 32:0.1).

rejected.reason: 'Michael' is here the name of an order of Sons; the Spanish name 'Miguel' brings in the archangel and a common personal name. See michael-of-nebadon.

creature-trinitized-sons.name: hijos trinitizados por criaturas
creature-trinitized-sons.meaning: Sons brought into being by the trinitizing union of two high creatures, such as finaliters and Paradise-Havona personalities, as distinct from those trinitized by Deity (22:0.5, 22:7.8).

rejected.reason: Singular suggests one creature; trinitization needs two (22:7.8).
Calque of the English hyphen; not natural Spanish.

creatures.name: criaturas
creatures.meaning: Any created being, as distinct from the Creator; finite realities 'always have beginnings — they are created', and the creature stands in relation to the Universal Creator (0:1.11, 1:4.5, 3:4.7).

rejected.reason: Too broad; loses the 'created' sense that the papers stress.
Ordinary senses the reader must not bring: a small child, a monster or beast. The papers mean only 'created being'.

cretaceous.name: Cretácico
cretaceous.meaning: The geological period of flowering plants and the decline of the great reptiles (60:3).

rejected.reason: Less common in current Spanish geology.

crete.name: Creta
crete.meaning: The island settled about 12,000 B.C. by a brilliant tribe of Andites skilled in crafts (80:7.2).

crispus.name: Crispo
crispus.meaning: The chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, whom Jesus and Ganid met (133:3.1).

cro-magnons.name: Cromañones
cro-magnons.meaning: The vigorous European people from the blend of Andites with the blue race, the biologic foundation of the modern European races (80:3.3, 80:5.7).

rejected.reason: Spanish has the adapted form "cromañón".

cro-magnons.note: Spanish usually writes "cromañón" in lowercase; the capital follows rule 1 and the other race names (Andonitas). A human can decide.

custodians-of-knowledge.name: custodios del conocimiento
custodians-of-knowledge.meaning: Primary supernaphim who are living libraries on Paradise, in whom the facts of the universes are recorded and who classify knowledge into seven grand orders (27:5.1, 27:5.5, 26:3.5).

rejected.reason: 'guardián' is used for 'guardian' in the done terms; 'custodian' is 'custodio' (Trinitized Custodians).

custodians-of-records.name: Custodios de los Registros
custodians-of-records.meaning: Senior chief recorders among the tertiary supernaphim of Havona, chosen as permanent keepers of the formal archives of Paradise, in contrast to the living records held by the custodians of knowledge (25:5.1, 25:6.5).

rejected.reason: "guardián" already renders "guardian"; "Custodians" is "Custodios" in Trinitized Custodians.
The English says records, not archives; "archivos" is kept for "archives" in 25:5.1.

cuthites.name: cuteos
cuthites.meaning: A people whose descendants Sargon of Assyria settled in central Palestine in place of the deported Israelites (143:4.1).

rejected.reason: Too close to the Cutites, a different people.

cutites.name: Cutitas
cutites.meaning: One of the groups that occupied the first garden after Adam left it (73:7.1).

rejected.reason: Already the form for the Cuthites.

cutites.note: The papers name them once; they must not be merged with the Cuthites.

cybele.name: Cibeles
cybele.meaning: The Phrygian goddess, mother of Attis, whose cult the papers list among the mystery cults (98:4.3, 98:5.5).

cymboyton.name: Cymboyton
cymboyton.meaning: The wealthy merchant of Urmia who, with his three sons, built the temple of religion there (134:3.2).

cynicism-religion.name: cinismo (religión)
cynicism-religion.meaning: The doctrine of the Cynics, which the papers say had formerly been more a religion than a philosophy, drawn largely from remnants of Melchizedek's teachings and preached to common people (121:4.4).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes the names of schools and religions in lowercase, as in "budismo" in the terms already done.
Loses the noun that the English uses; the papers stress that it was more a religion than a school.

cynicism-religion.note: Ordinary Spanish "cinismo" means shamelessness or contempt for others. The reader must take it here as the ancient school only; the qualifier "(religión)" helps.

cynics.name: cínicos
cynics.meaning: Wandering preachers of faith and trust in God who kept the Salem teachings in a fairly pure form in Roman Europe and were later absorbed into early Christianity (98:0.2, 98:3.9, 121:4.4).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes members of a school in lowercase, as with "fariseos".
The papers call them preachers more than philosophers (98:3.9); adding "filósofos" narrows the sense.

cynics.note: Ordinary "cínico" means a shameless or scornful person. Context must show the ancient school.

cyprus.name: Chipre
cyprus.meaning: The Mediterranean island settled by Mesopotamians about 5000 B.C. (80:7.10) and visited by Jesus (130:0.3).

cyrene.name: Cirene
cyrene.meaning: The city of northern Africa, home of Simon who carried Jesus' crossbeam (187:1.10, 130:6.6).

cyrus.name: Ciro
cyrus.meaning: A figure in the traditions of the infant set adrift and preserved by the gods, with Sargon, Moses, and Romulus (89:7.3).

dabaritta.name: Dabaritta
dabaritta.meaning: A town of Galilee visited on the second preaching tour, October to December A.D. 28 (149:0.1).

dagon.name: Dagón
dagon.meaning: The god of the Philistines, named by Jeremiah among the national gods that did not exist (97:6.2).

dakota-black-hills.name: Black Hills de Dakota
dakota-black-hills.meaning: The Black Hills region of Dakota in North America, named as the eastward limit of the Pacific invasion of the western continent in the later reptilian age (60:2.4).

rejected.reason: A literal rendering that Spanish readers do not use for this real place; the English proper name is the usual form.

dalamatia.name: Dalamatia
dalamatia.meaning: The headquarters city of the Planetary Prince Caligastia on Urantia, near the Persian Gulf, later submerged (66:3).

daligastia.name: Daligastia
daligastia.meaning: A secondary Lanonandek Son, the associate-assistant of the Planetary Prince Caligastia and head of the ten councils, who joined the rebellion (66:2.2, 67:2.1).

damascus-gate.name: puerta de Damasco
damascus-gate.meaning: The north gate of Jerusalem by which Jesus was led to Golgotha and to which the frightened women ran from the tomb (187:1.4, 189:4.7).

dan-city.name: Dan (ciudad)
dan-city.meaning: The northern town of Palestine also called Caesarea-Philippi (134:7.5, 155:2.1).

dan-prince-s-staff.name: Dan (del cuerpo del Príncipe)
dan-prince-s-staff.meaning: The member of the Prince's staff who led the advisers on the conquest of predatory animals (66:5.7).

daniel.name: Daniel
daniel.meaning: The Hebrew prophet who understood that 'the Most High rules in the kingdom of men' (43:3.4).

danube.name: Danubio
danube.meaning: The European river whose valley was a route of entry for some Andites and for the Danubian Andonites moving north (80:4.1, 80:8.4).

danubians.name: danubianos
danubians.meaning: Andonite farmers and herders who entered Europe through the Balkans and moved north up the Danube valley, making pottery (80:8.4, 80:9.3).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes the names of peoples in lowercase.

daphne.name: Dafne
daphne.meaning: Daphne, the figure of Greek myth whose name the grove at Antioch carries; the papers name her only in 'the grove of Daphne' (133:8.1).

rejected.reason: The English spelling; Spanish has a standard form for this classical name.

daphne.note: The papers do not describe Daphne herself; the packet summary (a naiad, daughter of Ladon) is not in the text.

daphne-grove-of.name: bosque de Dafne
daphne-grove-of.meaning: A notorious shrine of shame at Antioch that Gonod and Ganid visited and that Jesus refused to visit (133:8.1).

rejected.reason: Closer to 'grove' in size, but less natural for a sacred grove at a shrine; 'bosque' is the plain usual word.
Gives the meaning instead of the name; the English names the grove, not the shrine.

dark-gravity-bodies.name: cuerpos oscuros de gravedad
dark-gravity-bodies.meaning: The enormous dark masses beyond the seventh Havona circuit that neither reflect nor absorb light and hide Havona from view (14:1.14, 12:1.10).

rejected.reason: Natural, but "de gravedad" keeps the word "gravedad" used in the other terms.

dark-islands-of-space.name: islas oscuras del espacio
dark-islands-of-space.meaning: Dead suns and other large masses without light and heat that hold neighboring systems in gravity balance (15:6.11, 15:5.11).

david-king.name: David (rey)
david-king.meaning: The king of Israel who made Jerusalem his capital (97:9).

david-zebedee.name: David Zebedeo
david-zebedee.meaning: David Zebedee, brother of James and John, who ran the messenger service of Jesus' ministry (163:0.1).

dawn-mammals.name: mamíferos del alba
dawn-mammals.meaning: The small, large-brained animals that walked mostly on their hind legs, which suddenly appeared from the North American lemur stock and gave rise to the mid-mammals (61:6.1, 62:4.7).

rejected.reason: A general description, not the coined name.
A real scientific term for a different group.

daynals-order-of.name: Daynales, orden de los
daynals-order-of.meaning: The Trinity Teacher Sons, Paradise Sons who are the true teachers of ascending personalities and whose missions lead a world toward light and life (20:9.4, 20:10.4).

dead-book-of-the.name: Muertos, Libro de los
dead-book-of-the.meaning: The Egyptian collection of magical charm texts, first inscribed on coffins, that was gathered and preserved as protection for the dead (95:2.5).

rejected.reason: 'Difuntos' is more formal and is not the usual Spanish name of this Egyptian text.

dead-sea.name: mar Muerto
dead-sea.meaning: The sea of Palestine by which Engedi lies (135:1.1).

deborah.name: Débora
deborah.meaning: The woman who ruled the Hebrews and, with Barak, defeated Sisera at Taanach, while the cruelty of war continued under her (70:1.17, 126:1.2).

decapolis.name: Decápolis
decapolis.meaning: The region of cities east of the Jordan where Jesus and his followers made a mission (157:2.2, 128:3.2).

deccan.name: Decán
deccan.meaning: The southern plateau of India, into which the Andites slowly moved southward about 15,000 B.C. (79:2.4).

rejected.reason: English spelling; Spanish geography uses Decán.

december-25th.name: 25 de diciembre
december-25th.meaning: December 25, the date of the annual festival of Mithras, the most elaborate observance of the Mithraic cult (98:5.4).

rejected.reason: English word order and a capital on the month; Spanish writes the day first and the month in lowercase.

deity.name: Deidad
deity.meaning: Divine reality as it functions on diverse levels, personal or not, divinely co-ordinated (0:1.1, 16:0.1).

rejected.reason: The papers use 'divinity' as a separate term for the quality of Deity (Foreword section 'Deity and Divinity').

deity-absolute.name: Absoluto de la Deidad
deity-absolute.meaning: The potential that the Father's free will segregated from total infinite reality, within which all divinity activities take place; the Qualified Absolute (0:10.1, 0:11.6).

rejected.reason: Not natural Spanish; reads as a typing error.
That is the form of 'Absolute Deity', a different term; the two must stay distinct.

deity-trinitized-sons.name: Hijos trinitizados por la Deidad
deity-trinitized-sons.meaning: The first group of Trinitized Sons of God, unrevealed in the papers (22:0.2, 22:0.5).

rejected.reason: Calque of the English compound.
'Deity' and 'God' are distinct terms (Deidad, Dios).

deity-ultimate.name: Deidad Última
deity-ultimate.meaning: A designation of God the Ultimate, Deity on the second level of unifying divinity expression as overcontroller of the master universe (0:1.10, 0:9.1).

rejected.reason: Would mirror 'Absoluto de la Deidad', but that term names a distinct Absolute; this term only names God the Ultimate.
Both English forms name the same being, so one Spanish form is acceptable; a reviewer should confirm.

deliverer.name: Libertador
deliverer.meaning: One who delivers a people, as in the Jewish hope of a Messiah-deliverer; the papers say Jesus was not the expected deliverer of the Jews but the world's deliverer (121:2.7, 122:4.2, 136:1.1).

rejected.reason: "Savior" is a different English word; the papers keep deliverance and salvation apart (97:8.3).
Adds the idea of ransom, which the English does not carry.

denmark.name: Dinamarca
denmark.meaning: The land that rose from the sea and was the military headquarters of the northern Andites for three thousand years (80:2.4, 80:5.2).

descending-sons-of-god.name: Hijos de Dios descendentes
descending-sons-of-god.meaning: Sons of God of high divine origin who serve on the worlds of time and space to help the ascending sons of God in their Paradise climb (20:1.1).

rejected.reason: 'Descendiente' means offspring or descendant, not one who goes down.

designers-and-embellishers.name: diseñadores y embellecedores
designers-and-embellishers.meaning: A group of the celestial artisans who create works of beauty for morontia and spirit beings (44:0.11).

deuteronomy.name: Deuteronomio
deuteronomy.meaning: The book of the Hebrew scriptures whose scribe portrayed the Great Choice between good and evil, and from which Jesus read in the synagogue (97:8.3, 150:8.8).

devonian.name: Devónico
devonian.meaning: The geological period of the age of fishes, with wide seas (59:4.5).

devouress.name: Devoradora
devouress.meaning: In Egyptian belief, the hell to which a soul found wanting in the judgment hall of Osiris was consigned (95:2.9).

rejected.reason: The English uses the feminine suffix -ess; the masculine loses it.
Adds words that the English name does not have.

forcedChoices: The feminine 'Devoradora' follows the English '-ess' ending.

dilmat.name: Dilmat
dilmat.meaning: The Egyptian name for the ancient Nodite settlement on the Persian Gulf near the earlier city of Dilmun (77:4.8).

rejected.reason: That is the form for Dilmun, a different name in the same paragraph.

dilmun.name: Dilmún
dilmun.meaning: The later Nodite city near the Persian Gulf; the Sumerians gave its name to all three Nodite centers (77:4.8).

rejected.reason: Spanish stress needs the accent.

diogenes-of-athens.name: Diógenes de Atenas
diogenes-of-athens.meaning: The Greek philosopher to whom the Cynics traced their philosophy (121:4.4).

rejected.reason: The papers say 'of Athens'; a translation must not correct the text.

dion.name: Dión
dion.meaning: One of the towns in Perea where the seventy and Jesus and the apostles worked during the Perean mission that began January 3, A.D. 30 (165:0.1).

rejected.reason: That form is kept for the separate English entry Dium (159:0.2), so the two names stay distinct as in the English.
Without the accent, Spanish readers stress it wrongly; the accent gives the usual pronunciation.

dionysus.name: Dioniso
dionysus.meaning: The Greek god whose nature worship flourished among the mystery cults of the Mediterranean lands (98:2.10).

rejected.reason: In Spanish this is mainly a man's given name; 'Dioniso' is the usual name of the god.
The Roman name; the English uses the Greek one.

directors-of-assignment.name: directores de asignación
directors-of-assignment.meaning: A body of 144 supreme seraphim, elected by the angels, that is the highest angelic council on any sphere and co-ordinates seraphic service and assignment (39:1.16, 39:2.17).

rejected.reason: 'Destino' is the term for 'destiny'; 'assignment' is a different word.
Reads as a personnel office; it also breaks the family with 'jefes de asignación'.

directors-of-conduct.name: directores de la conducta
directors-of-conduct.meaning: Primary supernaphim who teach new arrivals on Paradise the proper usages of conduct there and guide them so that they avoid confusion (27:4.1, 27:4.3).

discerners-of-spirits.name: Discernidores de Espíritus
discerners-of-spirits.meaning: Secondary seconaphim attached to the Universal Censors who, by inherent spiritual insight, present unerring portraits of the soul and motives of a being (28:5.20).

rejected.reason: 'Discerniente' is an adjective (discerning), not an agent noun.
Changes the idea: they discern and present; the Censors judge.

dium.name: Dium
dium.meaning: One of the Decapolis cities where the apostles and evangelists worked during the tour of August 18 to September 16 (159:0.2).

rejected.reason: Used for the separate English entry Dion (165:0.1); the English keeps two spellings, so the Spanish must keep two.

dium.note: Dion and Dium can be the same historical city, but the English gives two names; a reviewer can check whether one form is wanted.

dives.name: Dives
dives.meaning: The rich man in the old Nazarite parable of the rich man and the beggar Lazarus, which Peter recited and on which Jesus never consented to comment (169:3.2, 169:3.3).

rejected.reason: A traditional Spanish nickname for the rich man from the Gospel story, not the name that the papers give.
A description, not the personal name the text uses.

divine-builders.name: constructores divinos
divine-builders.meaning: One of the groups of celestial artisans, working in seven groups, who build the spirit cities, homes, and other structures of the celestial realms (44:0.8, 44:3.1).

rejected.reason: Correct but more literary; 'constructores' is the plain word.

divine-counselors.name: Consejeros Divinos
divine-counselors.meaning: An order of Trinity-origin beings who are the counsel of the Paradise Trinity to the superuniverses and sit with Perfectors of Wisdom and Universal Censors (19:0.1, 22:1.13).

rejected.reason: 'Asesor' reads as a hired technical adviser; 'consejero' carries counsel and wisdom.

divine-executioners.name: ejecutores divinos
divine-executioners.meaning: The quasi-material fourth members of a conciliating commission, who carry out the decisions of the commission (25:2.8, 25:3.5, 29:4.15).

rejected.reason: 'verdugo' is only the one who puts a person to death; the papers mean the one who executes decisions.
'ejecutante' is mainly a musical performer.

divine-executioners.note: 'ejecutor' can also suggest one who kills; the context (executing decisions) supports the sense 'one who carries out'.

divinington.name: Divinington
divinington.meaning: The first sacred world of the Father near Paradise, the 'bosom of the Father' and Paradise rendezvous of the Thought Adjusters (13:1.4).

divinity.name: divinidad
divinity.meaning: The unifying quality of Deity as creatures comprehend it: truth, beauty, and goodness; love, mercy, and ministry in personality; justice, power, and sovereignty on impersonal levels (0:1.2, 0:1.15, 0:1.17).

rejected.reason: 'Deidad' is the term for Deity; 'divinity' is its quality, so the two forms must differ.
In everyday Spanish 'una divinidad' is a god or goddess, and 'divinidad' can mean 'something lovely'. The reader must not bring either sense.

doings-of-kings-of-israel.name: Hechos de los Reyes de Israel
aliases: Los Hechos de los Reyes de Israel
doings-of-kings-of-israel.meaning: A book of Hebrew records that the priests of the Babylonian exile destroyed after they prepared their sacred history of Israel (97:8.1).

rejected.form: Crónicas de los Reyes de Israel
rejected.reason: Confuses it with the biblical books of Chronicles; the papers describe a lost book.

rejected.form: Obras de los Reyes de Israel
rejected.reason: 'Obras' also means buildings or written works, a wrong reading.

doings-of-kings-of-israel.note: 'Hechos' is also the word in 'Hechos, libro de los' (Acts). The full title keeps them apart, but a reviewer can check it.

doings-of-kings-of-judah.name: Hechos de los Reyes de Judá
aliases: Los Hechos de los Reyes de Judá
doings-of-kings-of-judah.meaning: A book of Hebrew records that the priests of the Babylonian exile destroyed after they prepared their sacred history of Israel (97:8.1).

rejected.form: Crónicas de los Reyes de Judá
rejected.reason: Confuses it with the biblical books of Chronicles; the papers describe a lost book.

don.name: Don
don.meaning: The Russian river whose grazing lands, with the Volga's, formed the northern route of the Andites into northwestern Europe (80:4.1).
don.note: "don" is a Spanish title of respect; use "río Don" where the context does not show a river.

dorcas.name: Dorcas
dorcas.meaning: The woman at whose home Gadiah held a memorable argument with Peter (130:1.3).

rejected.reason: A different name for the biblical figure; the papers say Dorcas.

dothan.name: Dotán
dothan.meaning: The hills where Joseph's brothers sold him into Egyptian slavery, which Jesus could see from the hill of Simeon near Nazareth (126:1.2).

rejected.reason: The English spelling; Spanish has a standard biblical form.

dravidians.name: drávidas
dravidians.meaning: The mixed people of India that came from Andite conquerors blending with native stock (79:3.1).

dual-origin-beings.name: seres de origen dual
dual-origin-beings.meaning: Beings who originate in any two of the Paradise Deities, or who are created by any two beings descended from them (30:1.29).

rejected.reason: Also natural, but 'dual' matches 'triune' as a parallel classification term.

dyaks.name: dayak
dyaks.meaning: A present-day people who evolved only the most primitive religious practices (92:6.1).

rejected.reason: The English plural; Spanish writes peoples in lowercase and does not use the English -s.
A less usual Spanish form.

dyaus-pitar.name: Dyaus pitar
dyaus-pitar.meaning: The Vedic lord of heaven, one of the triune leaders of the Aryan pantheon with Indra and Agni (94:1.3).

rejected.reason: The English writes 'pitar' in lowercase; keep the English capitals.

ea.name: Ea
ea.meaning: A Mesopotamian god, one of the Babylonian triad of Bel, Ea, and Anu, the gods of earth, sea, and sky (95:1.4).

east-indies.name: Indias Orientales
east-indies.meaning: The islands of southeast Asia, reached by Andite groups and by Dravidian shipping (78:5.6, 79:3.7).

easter-island.name: isla de Pascua
easter-island.meaning: The Pacific island that was long a religious and administrative center of one of the lost Andite-modified groups (78:5.7).

rejected.reason: The native name; the English uses the European name.

eastern-ghats.name: Ghats Orientales
eastern-ghats.meaning: The mountain range of India through which three great rivers of the Deccan flow to the sea, along which Dravidian centers of culture were located (79:3.6).

rejected.reason: Correct but less usual in Spanish geography.

ebal.name: Ebal
ebal.meaning: A mountain that Jesus could see from the hill of Simeon, connected with the traditions of Abraham, Jacob, and Abimelech (126:1.2).

eber.name: Eber
eber.meaning: The officer of the Sanhedrin sent to arrest Jesus, who refused and defended him before the rulers (162:2.6, 162:2.9).

ecclesiastes.name: Eclesiastés
ecclesiastes.meaning: The Old Testament book whose frank pessimism was a worldly wise reaction to overoptimistic beliefs in Providence (97:8.2).

edenic-league.name: liga edénica
edenic-league.meaning: The federation into which Adam joined the companies of his system of group control throughout Eden (74:5.5).

rejected.reason: Acceptable, but the English uses the adjective 'Edenic'.
The English writes 'league' in lowercase.

edentia.name: Edentia
edentia.meaning: The headquarters world of the constellation Norlatiadek, seat of the Most Highs (43:0.1).

edomites.name: edomitas
edomites.meaning: A neighbor tribe that paid tribute to David and later revolted under Amaziah (97:9.14, 97:9.22).

edrei.name: Edrei
edrei.meaning: A city of the Decapolis where Thomas and his associates labored and where Jesus taught the principles for those who preach truth (159:0.2, 159:3.1).

egypt.name: Egipto
egypt.meaning: Egypt, the land of the Nile valley and its ancient civilization (95:2.1).

eightfold-path.name: Óctuple Sendero
eightfold-path.meaning: The Buddhist philosophy of right views, aspirations, speech, conduct, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, and contemplation, linked to the doctrine of suffering and the escape from it (94:8.8).

rejected.reason: Literal and not the usual Spanish name; 'Camino' also belongs to other terms (Camino del Padre).
Adds 'Noble', which the English does not have.

el.name: El
el.meaning: The name for the composite Deity that devout Semites used when they tried to worship all the evolving ideas of divinity, which also included other Bedouin nature gods (96:1.7).
el.note: In Spanish 'El' at the start of a sentence looks like the article 'el' with a capital. Translators must make the name clear from the context.

el-elyon.name: El Elyon
el-elyon.meaning: The Most High God of heaven, the term for Melchizedek's doctrine of Deity after his time at Salem (96:1.4, 96:4.2).

el-shaddai.name: El Shaddai
el-shaddai.meaning: A Hebrew concept of God derived from Egyptian and Melchizedek teachings, the Egyptian concept of the God of heaven (96:1.5, 142:3.5).

elam.name: Elam
elam.meaning: The region east of the Euphrates where the eastern or Elamite Nodites settled (77:4.4).

elamites.name: elamitas
elamites.meaning: The eastern Nodites of Elam, headed by Enoch son of Cain, who kept peace with the Adamites and became largely Sangik while keeping a civilization above the surrounding barbarians (76:2.9, 77:4.4).

rejected.reason: Elam is a historical land; Spanish writes peoples in lowercase, as in 'edomitas'.

elealah.name: Eleale
elealah.meaning: One of the towns in Perea where the seventy and Jesus and the apostles worked during the Perean mission (165:0.1).

rejected.reason: The English spelling; Spanish has a standard biblical form without the final h.

eleusinian-mysteries.name: misterios eleusinos
eleusinian-mysteries.meaning: A mystery cult that grew up within the Olympian pantheon as a Greek version of the worship of fertility (98:2.10).

rejected.reason: The English writes 'mysteries' in lowercase.

elihu.name: Eliú
elihu.meaning: The prophet of Ur and priest of the Salem believers whose teaching of salvation by faith was the most cheering message heard in the Levant since Melchizedek (96:7.7).

rejected.reason: The English spelling; Spanish has a standard biblical form.

elijah-mark.name: Elías Marcos
elijah-mark.meaning: The father of John Mark, at whose Jerusalem home Jesus ate the Last Supper with the apostles (183:2.1).

elijah-prophet.name: Elías (profeta)
elijah-prophet.meaning: The Hebrew prophet who denounced Ahab for the murder of Naboth and defended the old land mores against the Baalim (97:9.19).

eliphaz.name: Elifaz
eliphaz.meaning: The first of Job's friends, a false comforter who taught that only the wicked suffer (148:6.4, 148:6.9).

elisha.name: Eliseo
elisha.meaning: Elijah's faithful associate, who took up his work and kept the light of truth alive in Palestine (97:2.2, 97:2.3).

elizabeth-mother-of-john-the-baptist.name: Isabel (madre de Juan el Bautista)
elizabeth-mother-of-john-the-baptist.meaning: The wife of Zacharias and mother of John the Baptist, a relative of Mary, who with Zacharias believed Jesus would be the Messiah (122:8.4).

rejected.reason: Used in some Bible versions; Isabel is the common Spanish name.

elizabeth-of-tiberias.name: Isabel de Tiberíades
elizabeth-of-tiberias.meaning: The daughter of a wealthy Jew of Tiberias and Sepphoris, one of the women Jesus commissioned (150:1.1).
elizabeth-of-tiberias.note: Same first name as Isabel, the mother of John the Baptist; the place name keeps them apart.

ellanora.name: Ellanora
ellanora.meaning: A young woman of Panoptia who took the leadership of the human races in the Lucifer rebellion, so that no one on that world joined the rebels (53:7.1).

elman.name: Elman
elman.meaning: The Syrian believer physician who supervised the sick at the Bethsaida encampment and organized the kingdom's first hospital (148:0.1, 148:2.1).

eloah.name: Eloah
eloah.meaning: The singular of Elohim, the name under which the three-in-one God concept of the Sumerian-Chaldean groups was worshiped in Egypt (96:1.8).

elohim.name: Elohim
elohim.meaning: The name under which a three-in-one God concept, a Trinity, was worshiped; Jesus never claimed to be Elohim in the flesh, only the revelation of the Father (96:1.8, 169:4.9).

emergency-council-of-edentia.name: consejo de emergencia de Edentia
emergency-council-of-edentia.meaning: The council made up of all personalities assigned to Norlatiadek because of the Satania upheaval, presided over by a Vorondadek Son, the Most High director (43:5.14).

rejected.reason: 'Urgencia' is also correct, but 'emergencia' is the plain word in most of Latin America.

emmaus.name: Emaús
emmaus.meaning: A village about seven miles west of Jerusalem, home of the brothers Cleopas and Jacob, on whose road Jesus made his seventh morontia appearance (190:5.1, 190:5.2).

emotion-designers.name: diseñadores de emociones
emotion-designers.meaning: The celestial artisans who enhance and conserve feeling, and preserve the sentiments of morontia and the emotions of divinity for study and inspiration (44:6.5).

rejected.reason: Reads as designers who are emotional, a wrong sense.
Acceptable; the plural reads more naturally for a group that preserves many feelings.

en-gannim.name: En-ganim
en-gannim.meaning: A place between Geba and Endor where Jesus stopped on his last private tour through Palestine in A.D. 25 (134:7.5).

rejected.reason: The English double n; Spanish biblical forms use one n.

endantum.name: Endantum
endantum.meaning: The headquarters of the fifth constellation of Nebadon, where Michael made his sixth bestowal as a morontia mortal (119:6.3, 119:6.6).

endor.name: Endor
endor.meaning: A town in Galilee where Joseph worked and where Jesus rested from the crowds and told the story of King Saul and the witch of Endor (123:3.8, 146:7.1).

enemy.name: enemigo
enemy.meaning: 'The enemy of the kingdom', against whom Jesus warned the apostles because he would try to draw them away (138:7.3).

rejected.reason: The English writes 'enemy' in lowercase.
The paragraph does not name the enemy; to name him in the translation closes what the text leaves open.

enemy.note: The packet summary says the enemy is Caligastia. 138:7.3 does not name him. Keep the plain word.

energy.name: energía
energy.meaning: An all-inclusive term for spiritual, mindal, and material realms; physical energy denotes all phases and forms of phenomenal motion, action, and potential (0:6.2, 0:6.3).

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) energy as only a physical quantity
rejected.reason: The reader must not limit it to physics; 0:6.2 applies it to spirit and mind.

energy-manipulators.name: manipuladores de energía
energy-manipulators.meaning: The celestial artisans, and also living physical controllers, who study and handle physical, mind, and spiritual energies (44:5.4, 41:2.4).

rejected.reason: The done list uses 'manipuladores de energía mental' and 'manipuladores de energía espiritual'.

energy-transformers.name: transformadores de energía
energy-transformers.meaning: Among the more personal orders of the Master Physical Controllers, created by the Supreme Power Directors and Center Supervisors; they command on inhabited worlds when no associate power director is present (29:4.23).

rejected.reason: Reads as an adjective of a device.

energy-transformers.note: A reader can take 'transformadores' as electrical devices; the context shows they are living beings.

energy-transmitters.name: transmisores de energía
energy-transmitters.meaning: Living beings of the Master Physical Controllers who relay energy and can receive and transmit intelligence but cannot start a communication (67:6.9, 39:5.14).

engedi.name: Engadi
engedi.meaning: A place by the Dead Sea where the Nazarite colony under Abner lived, often visited by John the Baptist (135:2.3, 135:2.4).

rejected.reason: Spanish has its own established form for this biblical place.

england.name: Inglaterra
england.meaning: England, which with Scotland and Wales fought until they gave their sovereignties to the United Kingdom (134:6.3).

english-channel-land-bridge.name: puente terrestre del canal de la Mancha
english-channel-land-bridge.meaning: The land connection between England and France during most of the ice age, by which the Andonites reached England (64:1.5, 64:2.6).

rejected.reason: The glossary already uses 'puente terrestre' (Bering Strait land bridge).

english-language.name: lengua inglesa
english-language.meaning: The language into which the revelators were authorized to translate the papers, and whose limits they note (0:0.1, 42:2.1).

enoch.name: Enoc
enoch.meaning: The son of Cain and Remona who became head of the Elamite Nodites, the first Urantia mortal to fuse with his Thought Adjuster during life in the flesh, now one of the four and twenty counselors (76:2.9, 45:4.13); the so-called Book of Enoch bears his name (126:3.8).

enos.name: Enós
enos.meaning: The son of Seth who founded the new order of worship in the second garden (76:3.4).

rejected.reason: Without the accent Spanish readers stress it wrongly; the biblical form has the accent.

ensa.name: Ensa
ensa.meaning: The minor sector of one hundred local universes, with capital Uminor the third, in which Nebadon lies (15:14.7, 18:5.5).

enta.name: Enta
enta.meaning: One of the remarkable women among the ancestors of Mary, the mother of Jesus (122:1.2).

eocene.name: Eoceno
eocene.meaning: The 'so-called Eocene period' of the early mammals, when North America was connected by land with every continent except Australia (61:1.14).

ephesus.name: Éfeso
ephesus.meaning: The capital of the Roman province of Asia, with the temple of Artemis; Jesus visited it with Gonod and Ganid, and John Zebedee later settled and died there (133:6.1, 139:4.15).

ephraim.name: Efraín
ephraim.meaning: The hill country where Israelite consciousness began, and a name for the northern kingdom of Israel (97:9.2, 97:9.11, 97:9.21).

epicurean-teacher-in-corinth.name: maestro epicúreo de Corinto
epicurean-teacher-in-corinth.meaning: The Epicurean teacher in Corinth whom Jesus told to discern the greater things of the spirit that come from the realization of God's presence in the heart (133:4.5).

rejected.reason: 'Instructor' is for the coined orders (Instructores de los Mundos Morada); for a Greek philosophy teacher it reads stiffly.
Suggests a school post that the text does not give.

epicurean-teacher-in-corinth.note: 'Maestro' in lowercase is a plain word; 'Maestro' with a capital is the title of Jesus. A reviewer can check this in context.

epicureanism.name: epicureísmo
epicureanism.meaning: The Greek school of thought dedicated to the pursuit of happiness, which helped free the Romans from fatalism and fought superstition (121:4.2, 98:6.2).

rejected.reason: In common Spanish "epicúreo" also means a lover of pleasure; the papers say the better Epicureans were not sensual. Keep it as the name of the school.

epistle-of-first-john.name: Primera Epístola de Juan
epistle-of-first-john.meaning: The epistle that John wrote himself as a covering letter for the Gospel that Nathan wrote under his direction (121:8.10).

rejected.reason: Copies the English word order and is not natural Spanish.

epochal-revelations.name: revelaciones epocales
epochal-revelations.meaning: Revelation of truth presented to a world by a celestial agency, group, or personality, in contrast to autorevelation by the indwelling Adjuster (101:4.3, 92:3.5).

rejected.reason: Can read as "revelations typical of a period" (period style).
"trascendental" is reserved for transcendental.

epochal-revelations.note: Family "revelation": root "revelación" (autorrevelación for autorevelation). "epocal" is in the dictionary but uncommon; it reads as a term, as the English does.

erech.name: Erec
erech.meaning: An ancient Mesopotamian valley city that contended for supremacy with Sumer, Akkad, Kish, Ur, and Susa, near which Noah's settlement Aram lay (78:8.9, 78:7.5).

rejected.reason: The modern archaeological name; the English uses the biblical name.
The 'ch' reads as Spanish 'ch'; 'Erec' is the usual Spanish biblical form.

error.name: error
error.meaning: An intellectual mistake, a misconception that suggests lack of intellectual keenness, with no moral guilt in itself (67:1.4, 67:1.5).

rejected.reason: Too casual for the defined term.

esdraelon.name: Esdrelón
esdraelon.meaning: The broad fertile plain south of Nazareth stretching toward Mount Gilboa and Samaria (123:5.13, 97:9.5).

rejected.reason: A different name; the English uses Esdraelon and also names Jezreel separately.
Less usual Spanish spelling.

eskimos.name: esquimales
eskimos.meaning: Descendants of the Urantia aborigines who crossed from Greenland into North America some eighty thousand years ago (64:7.18).

essenes.name: esenios
essenes.meaning: A Jewish religious sect from the Maccabean revolt that lived as a brotherhood in monasteries, did not marry, held all things in common, and taught about angels (137:7.8, 164:3.4).

esta.name: Esta
esta.meaning: A young woman of Nazareth whom James, brother of Jesus, married (128:5.7).
esta.note: 'Esta' is also a Spanish demonstrative ('this'); the capital helps, but the reader can stumble.

esther.name: Ester
esther.meaning: The Jewish heroine of Israel's deliverance, remembered at Purim and named among women of the religious life of Israel (123:3.5, 150:3.1).

eternal-son.name: Hijo Eterno
eternal-son.meaning: The Second Source and Center, the perfect expression of the Father's first absolute thought, the Word-God (6:0.1, 8:0.1).

eternals-of-days.name: Eternos de Días
eternals-of-days.meaning: The Supreme Trinity Personalities who each rule one Havona world, divine equals of the Ancients of Days (18:2.2, 18:4.6).

rejected.reason: Follows "Ancianos de Días" and "Uniones de Días" in the terms already done.

eternity.name: eternidad
eternity.meaning: Timeless existence, the everlasting now, in which potential infinity is inseparable (0:11.12, 13:1.9).

rejected.reason: Means endless duration in time, which is the opposite of timelessness.

ethical-sensitizers.name: Sensibilizadores Éticos
ethical-sensitizers.meaning: Supervisor seraphim who foster creature appreciation of the morality of interpersonal relationships, and act as counselors and exchange teachers (39:3.7).

rejected.reason: Suggests that they make ethics sensitive, not creatures.
'Concienciar' is mostly used in Spain and suggests campaigns.

ethics.name: ética
ethics.meaning: The principles of right relations between persons, growing from the facts of origin; ethics is progressive, unlike static traditional morality.

rejected.reason: The papers distinguish ethics from morality.

etruscan-priesthood.name: sacerdocio etrusco
etruscan-priesthood.meaning: The rapidly spreading Etruscan priesthood, with its new gods and temples, that the Salem missionaries in Italy could not overcome and that was organized into the Roman state religion (98:3.2).

euphrates-river.name: río Éufrates
euphrates-river.meaning: One of the two rivers of Mesopotamia.

europe.name: Europa
europe.meaning: The continent of Europe, settled by the blue man and later by the Andites (80:4.5, 80:5.8).

evangelists.name: evangelistas
evangelists.meaning: The preachers of the gospel trained by the apostles under Jesus, some later ordained as the seventy messengers of the kingdom (148:1.4, 149:0.2).

rejected.reason: Loses the link with "evangelio" (gospel).

evangelists.note: Same Spanish word as in "evangelistas seráficos" (seraphic evangels) in the terms already done. The adjective "seráficos" separates them, but a human must check the overlap.

evangels-of-destiny.name: evangelistas del destino
evangels-of-destiny.meaning: The hosts trained in the Melchizedek College of Spiritual Endowment who go out to proclaim spiritual liberty and divine sonship to the remote worlds of the universe (35:3.21).

rejected.reason: 'Evangelio' is the message (gospel), not the messenger.
Breaks the family with 'Evangelistas de la Luz' and 'evangelistas seráficos'.

evangels-of-light.name: Evangelistas de la Luz
evangels-of-light.meaning: Any celestial personality assigned for a time to a finaliter corps without taking the finaliter oath; they resume their former status after it (31:7.1, 31:7.2).

rejected.reason: "evangelio" is the message, not the messenger.
Not a Spanish word.

evangels-of-light.note: "evangel" is already "evangelista" in "seraphic evangels"; that same word also translates human "evangelists". The rule of one word, one translation forces "Evangelistas" here.

eve.name: Eva
eve.meaning: The Material Daughter who came with Adam to Urantia to uplift the races (40:2.2).

eventod.name: Eventod
eventod.meaning: The name by which Michael was known on Uversa in his fifth bestowal, as an ascending spirit mortal who lived there eleven years (119:5.2).

eventuated-transcendental-beings.name: seres trascendentales eventuados
eventuated-transcendental-beings.meaning: Transcendental beings who neither create nor are created but are eventuated, functioning on absonite levels (0:1.12, 31:8).

rejected.reason: "eventual" means "possible" or "temporary".

eventuation.name: eventuación
eventuation.meaning: The coming into being of absonite realities and beings, neither creation nor evolution; they "simply are" (0:1.12, 0:9.1, 0:9.2).

rejected.reason: The Spanish adjective "eventual" means "possible" or "temporary"; the reader must not carry it into "eventuar".
Has the Christian sense of the coming of Christ.
Means an event, not a mode of coming into being.

eveson.name: Eveson
eveson.meaning: The second son of Adam and Eve, a masterly leader and administrator and his father's great helper (76:3.3, 74:6.2).

evil.name: mal
evil.meaning: The partial or unknowing transgression of divine law, the misadaptation of immaturity, which becomes sin only when chosen knowingly (67:1.4, 67:1.5, 132:2.1).

rejected.reason: Means wickedness of character, which is closer to sin; kept only as an alias.
The reader must not bring the sense of a personal or cosmic power of evil, nor illness ("un mal").

excursion-and-reversion-supervisors.name: supervisores de excursión y reversión
excursion-and-reversion-supervisors.meaning: Morontia Companions who accompany ascenders on the longer trips to the system headquarters and the surrounding transition worlds, and plan and supervise all such tours (48:3.14).

rejected.reason: Closes the sense of 'reversion'; the glossary already gives 'reversión' (reversion directors: directores de reversión).
Loses the coined pair of the English.

excursion-and-reversion-supervisors.note: The papers do not define 'reversion' in this title; it can mean the return from a trip or a link with the reversion (recreation) directors. The form keeps both readings open.

exodus.name: Éxodo
exodus.meaning: The Book of Exodus, from which Jesus read the first text, from the law, in the synagogue at Capernaum (145:2.2).

experientials.name: experienciales
experientials.meaning: Realities that come to be through experience and growth, as the Supreme and the Ultimate are; the opposite of existential (0:1.14, 0:4.9, 0:7.5).

rejected.reason: Means "by experiment" or "trial"; a false friend.
Psychological and regional; the English is a coined term.

experts-of-communication.name: expertos en comunicación
experts-of-communication.meaning: Energy-manipulator artisans, twelve of whom serve Urantia, who know the laws of transmittal and interference for all space messages except those of Gravity and Solitary Messengers (44:5.7).

rejected.reason: Copies the English 'of'; Spanish says 'expertos en'.
Changes 'experts' to 'technicians', a word that the paragraph uses only as a description.

extension-school-instructors.name: instructores de escuelas de extensión
extension-school-instructors.meaning: Teachers from the next higher residential world of the ascendant career who keep a preparatory school on the world just below (30:3.8, 30:2.153).

rejected.reason: Reads as an outreach program of a school system.

extension-school-instructors.note: "extensión" in Spanish education can suggest university outreach courses; the papers mean a school of the next world extended down to the world below.

ezda.name: Ezda
ezda.meaning: An orphan boy of Beth-zur whom John the Baptist adopted and who cared for John's herds (135:3.1, 135:4.1).

ezekiel.name: Ezequiel
ezekiel.meaning: A Hebrew prophet who taught personal responsibility, proclaimed deliverance through the service of devotion, and foretold a new spirit within man (97:8.3, 145:2.7).

ezra-disciple-of-john.name: Esdras (discípulo de Juan)
ezra-disciple-of-john.meaning: A disciple of John the Baptist who rejected Jesus as the Deliverer, left with many disciples, and founded a sect that believed in John but not in Jesus (137:2.2).

rejected.reason: Breaks the family with 'Esdras de Nazaret', which is already done.

ezra-of-alexandria.name: Esdras de Alejandría
ezra-of-alexandria.meaning: The father of Susanna, one of the women who went to anoint the body of Jesus (189:4.4).

ezra-of-nazareth.name: Esdras de Nazaret
ezra-of-nazareth.meaning: A wealthy merchant and trader of Nazareth, father of Rebecca, who fell in love with Jesus (127:5.1).

rejected.reason: The glossary already uses 'Esdras' (Rebeca, hija de Esdras).

ezra-of-syracuse.name: Esdras de Siracusa
ezra-of-syracuse.meaning: The backslidden Jew who kept the tavern at Syracuse, whom Jesus helped back to the faith and who later helped build the first Christian church there (130:8.2).

ezra-prophet.name: Esdras (profeta)
ezra-prophet.meaning: The prophet who promised the Jews prosperity by adherence to the law (97:8.3).

ezraeon.name: Ezraeon
ezraeon.meaning: A friend of Joseph and Mary whose boat took them from Alexandria to Joppa in August, 4 B.C. (123:0.4).
ezraeon.note: The packet types this term as a place, but 123:0.4 shows that Ezraeon is a person, the owner of the boat.

fad.name: Fad
fad.meaning: The member of the Prince's staff who presided over the faculty on dissemination and conservation of knowledge, made the first alphabet of twenty-five characters, and sponsored learning by doing (66:5.9, 66:7.6).

fair-havens.name: Buenos Puertos
fair-havens.meaning: A place on Crete where Jesus drew a slave girl away from a drunken man who attacked her, which Ganid never forgot (130:5.4).

rejected.reason: Spanish readers know this Cretan harbor by its translated name.
Literal, but not the usual Spanish name of the place.

faith.name: fe
faith.meaning: The living, personal trust by which a person grasps the truth of sonship with God; the assurance of sonship is the experience of faith (140:10.9, 193:0.4, 196:3.34).

rejected.reason: The papers set belief apart from faith; 'creencia' is the word for belief.
Is trust in general and collides with 'espíritus de la confianza'.

faithful-of-days-of-edentia.name: Fiel de Días de Edentia
faithful-of-days-of-edentia.meaning: The Trinity Son of Paradise on Edentia who represents Immanuel and counsels the Most Highs of the constellation only when asked (43:4.2, 18:7.3).

rejected.reason: The terms already done use "de Días" without the article (Ancianos de Días, Uniones de Días).

faithfuls-of-days.name: Fieles de Días
faithfuls-of-days.meaning: Trinity-origin personalities, seventy million in number, who are the Paradise advisers to the rulers of the constellations (18:7.1).

rejected.reason: Breaks the pattern of 'Ancianos de Días' and 'Uniones de Días'.

family-commission-of-twelve.name: Comisión Familiar de los Doce
family-commission-of-twelve.meaning: The commission of twelve, chosen from the higher orders of universe personalities, that Gabriel sent to Urantia to investigate Jewish family life and nominate bestowal families for Michael (122:0.2).

rejected.form: Comisión de la Familia de Doce
rejected.reason: Reads as a commission about a family of twelve people.

rejected.form: Comisión de Doce sobre la Familia
rejected.reason: Clear, but it changes the order and the shape of the English name.

fanoving.name: Fanoving
fanoving.meaning: One of the nearest local universes to Nebadon in the superuniverse of Orvonton (32:2.12).

fantad.name: Fantad
fantad.meaning: The leader of the green race in its cultural revival 350 000 years ago, one of the four and twenty counselors (64:6.17, 45:4.9).

faroes.name: islas Feroe
faroes.meaning: The islands by which one group of Salem missionaries went to the Andonites of Iceland (93:7.2).

fate.name: Hado
fate.meaning: The power that the Greeks kept above Zeus, which prevented a true monotheism, since a God of final value must himself be the arbiter of fate (98:1.3).

rejected.reason: 'Destino' is the term for 'destiny', and 98:1.3 sets fate and destiny apart.
Also means 'but' as a conjunction, a wrong reading in a sentence.
The Greek proper name; the English uses a common word with a capital.

father-absolute.name: Padre-Absoluto
father-absolute.meaning: The Universal Father as the creator of the central universe and Father of all Creators, absolute in liberty of action (4:4.4, 10:3.8, 4:4.9).

rejected.reason: Without the hyphen it reads as a description ('the absolute father'); the English hyphen marks a name, like 'Father-Infinite'.

father-brahma.name: Padre-Brahma
father-brahma.meaning: The emerging Vedic concept of Brahma as the source of all gods, not wholly in disharmony with the Salem teaching of one God (94:1.5).

rejected.reason: Drops the hyphen and the English word order.

father-fused-mortals.name: mortales fusionados con el Padre
father-fused-mortals.meaning: Mortals who fuse with their Thought Adjuster, a fragment of the Universal Father; the same as Adjuster-fused mortals (40:9.1, 22:6.1).

father-guides.name: Guías Padre
father-guides.meaning: Secondary supernaphim, the older and most experienced superaphic ministers, who tutor pilgrim souls on the third circle of Havona and keep schools of wisdom there (26:4.7, 26:9.1).

rejected.reason: Says that they guide toward or belong to the Father, a reading that the English leaves open.
Says that they are fatherly in manner, which also closes what the English leaves open.

father-guides.note: The apposition 'Guías Padre' follows 'Espíritus Madre' and 'Hijos Miguel' and keeps the English sense open.

father-infinite.name: Padre-Infinito
