father-infinite.meaning: A name sometimes given to the Infinite, the actual value-level of the true infinity of the free will of the Universal Father (0:3.24, 0:3.25).

rejected.reason: Without the hyphen it reads as a plain title with an adjective, not the compound concept.

father-melchizedek.name: Padre Melquisedec
father-melchizedek.meaning: The first Melchizedek of Nebadon, who with the Creator Son and Creative Spirit brought the order into being and acts for Gabriel in his absence (93:1.2).

father-s-business.name: asuntos del Padre
father-s-business.meaning: The work of the Father that Jesus was to begin, in the message of the Salvington messenger: 'It is time that you began to be about your Father's business' (124:6.15).

rejected.reason: Has a commercial sense that the English does not intend.
Narrows 'business' to a single work; the English is broader.

forcedChoices: 'asuntos' in the plural: Spanish needs a count noun here, and the plural reads naturally as 'affairs'.

father-s-house.name: casa del Padre
father-s-house.meaning: Paradise as the eternal residence of the Father (11:3.3), and in Jesus' words the home to which the lost return (159:5.16) and which holds many mansions (30:4.17).

father-s-prayer.name: oración del Padre
father-s-prayer.meaning: The prayer that Hap's group taught the Dalamatians (66:5.14).

rejected.reason: Closes a reading; the English "Father's prayer" does not say to whom or whose, and "del Padre" keeps that open.

father-s-way.name: Camino del Padre
father-s-way.meaning: The moral law of seven commands that Hap gave the early races in Dalamatia (66:7.8).

rejected.reason: Keeps only the sense 'manner'; 'camino' carries both 'path' and 'way of life'.
Adds a word the English does not use.

forcedChoices: English 'way' is both 'path' and 'manner'; 'camino' keeps both readings better than another word.

fatherhood-of-god.name: paternidad de Dios
fatherhood-of-god.meaning: The truth that God is the Father of all persons, which the gospel of the kingdom proclaims with the sonship of man (193:0.4).

rejected.reason: Means sponsorship or godfathership, a different relationship.

fatherlikeness.name: semejanza con el Padre
fatherlikeness.meaning: Likeness to the Father; success in the quest of the Infinite is directly proportional to its achievement, which comes by living the will of God (106:9.11).

rejected.reason: Means 'fatherhood', a different term (paternidad de Dios).
Means fatherly manner, not likeness to the Father.

finaliter-corps.name: cuerpo de finalitarios
finaliter-corps.meaning: Any of the corps into which beings who attain Paradise are mustered; the papers speak of seven such corps (19:6.3, 30:4.31, 31:10.20).

rejected.reason: Grammatical, but 'finalitario' as an adjective is less clear than the noun phrase.
Reads as 'the last body'.

finaliter-corps.note: The English uses both 'finaliter corps' and 'finality corps' (30:4.31). 'cuerpo de la finalidad' is listed as an alias for the second English form.

finaliters.name: finalitarios
finaliters.meaning: Ascenders who complete the Paradise ascension and enter the Corps of the Finality, the present known destination of Adjuster-fused mortals (31:0.1, 107:2.7).

rejected.reason: Means a finalist in a contest.
Means those who finish or end a thing.

finaliters-world.name: mundo de los finalitarios
finaliters-world.meaning: The system world on which finaliters are received and where half the planet holds the probation nursery for children of surviving mortals (45:6.7, 45:6.8, 47:1.4).

rejected.reason: The English names the world after the finaliters, not after the abstract finality.
Reads as 'the last world'; loses the link to the finaliters.

finns.name: finlandeses
finns.meaning: A Nordic people who believed that most trees were occupied by kind spirits (85:2.4).

rejected.reason: Correct but less usual; it can also mean the wider Finnic peoples.

first-cause.name: Primera Causa
first-cause.meaning: God as science reaches him by reason: the origin of all causes; revelation shows that this First Cause and the God of salvation are one Deity (4:4.7, 101:2.3, 101:2.7, 118:4.1).

rejected.reason: Also correct, but the plain word order matches the English and reads naturally in all regions.

first-epistle-of-peter.name: Primera Epístola de Pedro
first-epistle-of-peter.meaning: Peter's letter that shows his vigorous style, later altered by a disciple of Paul (139:2.12).

first-experiential-trinity.name: primera Trinidad experiencial
first-experiential-trinity.meaning: The union of the Supreme Creators, the Supreme Being, and the Architects of the Master Universe, also called the Trinity Ultimate (106:3.2, 31:9.14, 0:12.3).

rejected.reason: 'Experimental' means 'trial' or 'test'.

flavius.name: Flavio
flavius.meaning: A Greek Jew, proselyte of the gate, whose art-filled house in Jerusalem received Jesus (142:4.1).

florissant-fossil-beds.name: yacimientos fósiles de Florissant
florissant-fossil-beds.meaning: The fossil beds of Colorado that belong to the later years of the recent flood stage of the mammalian era (61:2.4).

rejected.reason: A literal copy of 'beds'; 'yacimientos' is the plain Spanish word.

force.name: fuerza
force.meaning: A broad term like energy, for spiritual, mindal, and material realms; in physics, cosmic force means energies from the Unqualified Absolute not yet responsive to Paradise gravity (0:6.2, 0:6.5).

foreword.name: Prólogo
foreword.meaning: The opening paper of definitions and limits of terms, which the authors call a definitive guide for the papers that follow, not a finished statement in itself (0:0.4).

rejected.reason: Usually a short note about the book; this part defines terms and is a whole paper.
Suggests a general overview, not a set of definitions.

formosa.name: Formosa
formosa.meaning: The island in East Asia that small groups of Andites reached, with Japan and the East Indies (78:5.6).

rejected.reason: The modern name; the English uses the older name.

fortant.name: Fortant
fortant.meaning: The bestowal director of Satania, number 319,847 of the secondary Lanonandek reserves, who directs the universe activities moved to Jerusem since Michael's bestowal (45:3.7).

fortune.name: Fortune
fortune.meaning: A fearful youth whom Jesus met in Crete and who later led the Christians of Crete and worked with Titus (130:6.5).

rejected.reason: The name of a Roman goddess and a common noun (luck); it changes the personal name.
A guess at a Latin original that the papers do not give.

fortune.note: The papers give only the English form. A reviewer can decide if a historical Latin form exists.

foundation-of-spiritual-progress.name: Fundación del Progreso Espiritual
foundation-of-spiritual-progress.meaning: An institution on a neighboring planet that supervises spiritual teachers who visit families, supported by voluntary gifts (Paper 72).

rejected.reason: Adds a purpose that the English 'of' does not state.

fountain-gate.name: puerta de la Fuente
fountain-gate.meaning: The gate of Jerusalem near Siloam to which the water procession went at the Feast of Tabernacles (162:4.4).

rejected.reason: In lowercase, 'fuente' can read as any fountain; the capital marks the name of the gate.

four-and-twenty-counselors.name: veinticuatro consejeros
four-and-twenty-counselors.meaning: A commission of twenty-four ascended Urantians on Jerusem, Michael's personal agents and advisory-control body for Urantia (45:4, 76:6.3).

rejected.reason: Spanish has no archaic 'four and twenty' order; it reads as an error.

forcedChoices: plain 'veinticuatro': Spanish cannot keep the archaic English numeral order.

fourth-creatures-cherubim.name: cuartas criaturas (querubines)
fourth-creatures-cherubim.meaning: Every fourth cherubim and sanobim, quasi-material and near the morontia level, useful in borderland work (38:7.6, 38:7.7).

rejected.reason: reads as an odd adjective; the ordinal precedes in Spanish

fourth-creatures-havona-servitals.name: cuartas criaturas (Servitales de Havona)
aliases: cuartas criaturas de los Servitales de Havona
fourth-creatures-havona-servitals.meaning: Every fourth Havona Servital, a semiphysical being nearer to the physical power directors, able to discern both spirit and material beings (25:1.3, 44:0.17).

rejected.reason: Unnatural word order in Spanish.

fourth-creatures-universal-conciliators.name: cuartas criaturas (Conciliadores Universales)
fourth-creatures-universal-conciliators.meaning: The quasi-material member of each conciliating commission, the Divine Executioner, almost visible to mortals (25:2.5, 25:2.8).

foxhall-peoples.name: pueblos de Foxhall
foxhall-peoples.meaning: Early Andonite peoples of England, whose survivors became the present-day Eskimos (64:2.7).

frandalanks.name: frandalanks
frandalanks.meaning: The most numerous Master Physical Controllers, created in thirty divisions, which act as living gauges of presence, pressure, and velocity of force-energy (29:4.36, 29:4.37).

rejected.reason: Adapting a name that exists only in this book breaks rule 3.

free-will.name: libre albedrío
free-will.meaning: The capacity of a personal creature to choose within its limits, the mark of will creatures that makes moral decision and survival possible (5:6, 112:5, 118:6).

rejected.reason: Shows the family root "voluntad" but is less natural as the name of the faculty; kept as the alias "voluntad libre" where the text stresses the will.

fridays.name: viernes
fridays.meaning: Friday, long regarded as an unlucky day, an example of days of the week treated as fetishes (88:1.6).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes days of the week in lowercase.

fruit-vendor-of-messina.name: vendedor de fruta de Mesina
fruit-vendor-of-messina.meaning: A small boy at Messina from whom Jesus bought fruit and whom he encouraged; the boy later followed Mithraism and then the Christian faith (130:8.3).

rejected.reason: 'Frutero' also means a fruit bowl in many countries.

fusion.name: fusión
fusion.meaning: The eternal union of the surviving soul with a divine spirit fragment, of the Father (Adjuster), the Son, or the Spirit; a creature is fused with only one (40:9.1, 40:10.10).

rejected.reason: Too general; loses the coined term.
The reader must not bring the physical sense of 'fusión' to this term.

gabriel.name: Gabriel
gabriel.meaning: The Bright and Morning Star, first creation of the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit and chief executive of Nebadon (33:4.1).

rejected.reason: 'Lucero' is the planet Venus and is a traditional name for Lucifer; that sense is the opposite of what the authors mean.

gad.name: Gad
gad.meaning: One of the reputed tribes, with Reuben and Gilead, that traditionally lived in the regions east of the Jordan (128:1.14).

gadara.name: Gadara
gadara.meaning: A town of the Decapolis where Thomas Didymus once worked as a carpenter and stone mason, and where the apostles did personal work (138:2.5, 138:9.3).

gadda.name: Gadda
gadda.meaning: One of the towns in Perea where the seventy and Jesus and the apostles worked during the Perean mission (165:0.1).

galantia.name: Galantia
galantia.meaning: The ascendant associate of Gavalia, first of the ascendant Brilliant Evening Stars, with headquarters on Jerusem (37:2.6, 46:5.25).
galantia.note: The packet summary says "she", but 37:2.6 uses "he" in a sentence where it can refer to Gavalia or to Galantia. Translators must not add a gender that the text does not give; use forms without gender where possible.

galaxies.name: galaxias
galaxies.meaning: Vast star systems; in outer space they swing around Paradise in orderly procession, separated by quiet zones, and 375 million new ones will be seen by future telescopes (11:7.7, 12:2.3).

rejected.reason: The papers use 'nebulae' as a separate word; a galaxy is not a nebula.

galilee.name: Galilea
galilee.meaning: The northern province of Palestine where Jesus did much of his ministry; Sepphoris and later Tiberias were its capitals (129:1.2).

gamala.name: Gamala
gamala.meaning: A city visited on the second preaching tour of Galilee (149:0.1).

gamaliel.name: Gamaliel
gamaliel.meaning: A leading Jerusalem rabbi who advised the authorities to leave Jesus' followers alone (194:4.10, 126:5.3).

ganges.name: Ganges
ganges.meaning: The great river of India whose delta formed largely in the last fifty thousand years (59:6.9, 79:2.1).

ganid.name: Ganid
ganid.meaning: The young Indian son of Gonod whom Jesus tutored on their journey through the Mediterranean world (130:0.3, 133:1.1, 133:3.5).

garden-of-eden.name: Jardín del Edén
garden-of-eden.meaning: The headquarters of Adam and Eve on a Mediterranean peninsula, later submerged.

rejected.reason: Collides with the done term 'Paraíso'.

gardens-of-eden.name: Jardines del Edén
gardens-of-eden.meaning: The garden homes and culture centers of the Material Sons on inhabited worlds, named for Edentia (51:3.2, 51:6.1).

gardens-of-god.name: jardines de Dios
gardens-of-god.meaning: The name of the constellation headquarters worlds for their botanic artistry, and the vast natural park on half of Edentia (43:1.7, 43:6.1).

gautama-siddhartha.name: Gautama Siddhartha
gautama-siddhartha.meaning: The Indian teacher whose teachings contained far more truth than survives in the modern cults that bear his name (94:7.8).

rejected.reason: Changes the order and the spelling of the English form.

gavalia.name: Gavalia
gavalia.meaning: The first-born and head of the Brilliant Evening Stars of Nebadon, author of the paper on Michael's seven bestowals (37:2.6, 119:0.1).

gaza.name: Gaza
gaza.meaning: A coastal city of Palestine on Jesus' route south to Beersheba (134:7.4).

gehenna.name: Gehena
gehenna.meaning: The open burial pits south of Jerusalem where bodies of the crucified were thrown (188:0.2, 188:1.5).
gehenna.note: In Spanish "Gehena" also has the religious sense of hell; in the papers it is a physical place.

genghis-khan.name: Gengis Kan
genghis-khan.meaning: The Mongol leader of A.D. 1200, last great showing of Andite military genius in central Asia, whose return his tribesmen still await (79:1.9, 92:5.6).

gennesaret.name: Genesaret
gennesaret.meaning: A region on the Sea of Galilee where Jesus rested with the apostles and held conferences with them (152:5.5, 152:6.1).

gentiles.name: gentiles
gentiles.meaning: The non-Jewish peoples of the time of Jesus, morally somewhat below the Jews but with natural goodness in which the gospel could grow (121:4.1, 128:2.5).

rejected.reason: Adds a religious judgment; the English means only non-Jewish.

gerar.name: Gerar
gerar.meaning: A place south of Salem where Abraham went after Melchizedek left, and where he hid his identity (93:9.2, 93:9.3).

gerasa.name: Gerasa
gerasa.meaning: A city of the Decapolis on Jesus' routes between Galilee and Jerusalem (128:3.2, 152:7.1).

germany.name: Alemania
germany.meaning: The present European country, named in the papers for its geological deposits and racial history (59:4.8, 60:1.4).

gethsemane.name: Getsemaní
gethsemane.meaning: A park near Jerusalem beyond the brook Kidron, beside which Jesus and the apostles camped and where he was arrested (182:0.1).

gibraltar-isthmus.name: istmo de Gibraltar
gibraltar-isthmus.meaning: The land bridge between Spain and Africa that protected the western Mediterranean basin until an earthquake broke it and caused the greatest loss of life by flood in history (80:1.1, 80:2.4, 61:3.8).

gilboa.name: Gilboa
gilboa.meaning: The mountain in northern Palestine where the Philistines defeated Saul; the pilgrims from Nazareth passed its base on the road to Jerusalem (97:9.13, 124:6.4).

rejected.reason: Older Spanish spelling; less common today than Gilboa.

gileadites.name: galaaditas
gileadites.meaning: The tribe east of the Jordan whom Saul defended against the Ammonites (97:9.3).

gischala.name: Giscala
gischala.meaning: A Galilean town where the apostles worked (138:9.3).

god.name: Dios
god.meaning: God, the Universal Father, First Source and Center and the eternal God who dwells on Paradise (0:0.5, 1:0.1).

god-the-absolute.name: Dios el Absoluto
god-the-absolute.meaning: The experiential Deity whose actualization would follow the unification of the Absolute Trinity: the realization of absolute divinity (0:10.1).

rejected.reason: Reads as a description ('the absolute God') and breaks the pattern 'Dios el Espíritu', 'Dios el Supremo'.

god-the-sevenfold.name: Dios el Séptuple
god-the-sevenfold.meaning: The seven-level association of Deity, from the Creator Sons up to the Universal Father, that makes up for the limits of creatures and integrates the perfecting with the perfect (105:6.5, 0:9.1).

rejected.reason: Breaks the pattern of the done terms 'Dios el Absoluto' and 'Dios el Espíritu'.
'Septenario' means a seven-day period or a set of seven.

god-the-spirit.name: Dios el Espíritu
god-the-spirit.meaning: The Infinite Spirit, Third Person of the Paradise Trinity (8:0.4, 13:1.10).

rejected.reason: Drops the article and reads as a description ('God, who is spirit') instead of the name.

god-the-supreme.name: Dios el Supremo
god-the-supreme.meaning: The personal spirit reflection of the triune Paradise Deity in Havona, the first experiential Deity, unifying with the Almighty Supreme as the Supreme Being (0:7.1, 0:7.7).

god-the-ultimate.name: Dios el Último
god-the-ultimate.meaning: Personal Deity that functions on the absonite level of supertime and transcended space, eventuating from the divinity potentials of the master universe; the second experiential Deity after God the Supreme (0:9.1, 0:9.2, 0:9.5).

rejected.reason: Implies only an end point in time, against 0:9.5 (he has no end).
Without the article it reads as 'the last God'; the pattern 'Dios el X' follows Dios el Supremo and Dios el Absoluto.

forcedChoices: masculine 'el Último': The English refers to God the Ultimate with 'he' as with God the Supreme (0:7.1, 117:7.4).

godheads.name: Deidades
godheads.meaning: The three persons of the Paradise Trinity, distinct and separate in their spiritual relations with creatures, though one from the universe standpoint (5:3.1, 161:1.7).

rejected.reason: "divinidad" is already the form for divinity, a quality, not a person.
Interprets; the English has a distinct noun.
Literal and wrong; reads as heads of a body.

godheads.note: Same form as "Paradise Deities" (Deidades del Paraíso) and the plural of Deity. 5:3.1 uses both words for the same three persons, but a human must decide if Godhead needs its own form.

gods-and-goddesses.name: dioses y diosas
gods-and-goddesses.meaning: The many deities of human religions, such as the Greek family of gods and goddesses that grew from Hellenic invaders' concepts (98:1.2).

golden-calves.name: becerros de oro
golden-calves.meaning: The golden (and silver) calves that symbolized Yahweh, the Bedouin herders' concept of the spirit of the Sinai volcano (96:4.3, 96:1.12, 146:1.1).

rejected.reason: 'becerro de oro' is the fixed Spanish expression.

golgotha.name: Gólgota
golgotha.meaning: The official crucifixion site of Jerusalem, north of the city beyond the Damascus gate, where Jesus was crucified (187:1.4, 188:0.3).

rejected.reason: A different name; the English uses Golgotha.

gomorrah.name: Gomorra
gomorrah.meaning: The city destroyed with Sodom by natural causes, shortly before Melchizedek ended his bestowal (93:6.7, 93:8.1).

gonod.name: Gonod
gonod.meaning: A citizen of India, father of Ganid, who traveled with Jesus to Rome and taught him about India and China (130:0.4, 130:0.6).

goodness.name: bondad
goodness.meaning: With truth and beauty one of the three divine values through which creatures grasp divinity; the moral and spiritual quality of God that creatures seek and recognize (2:7, 56:10).

rejected.reason: Only kindness toward others; narrower than goodness.
The reader must not reduce it to "niceness" or mild kindness.

gospel.name: evangelio
gospel.meaning: The good news Jesus proclaimed: the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man, the kingdom received by faith (194:3.8, 170:0.1).

rejected.reason: A correct gloss, but not a single term; 'evangelio' is the plain word.
Capital reads as a book of the New Testament; the English uses lowercase for the message.

graduate-guides.name: Guías de Graduados
graduate-guides.meaning: Higher Personalities of the Infinite Spirit who conduct the training school of Havona and guide each ascending pilgrim through the circuits; some are translated Havona Servitals (24:6.4, 25:1.7).

rejected.reason: Reads as guides who themselves graduated; the English 'Graduate Guides' can mean guides of graduates (the pilgrims who graduate from the superuniverses).
Too academic and modern.

forcedChoices: 'de Graduados': English leaves open whether 'graduate' describes the guides or the pilgrims; Spanish must choose. The pilgrims arrive as graduates of the superuniverse schools (25:1.7). A reviewer must check.

grand-universe.name: gran universo
grand-universe.meaning: The seven evolving superuniverses together with the central universe of Havona, the now organized and inhabited creation (0:0.6).

rejected.reason: After the noun, "grande" is only a size description, not a name.

grandfanda.name: Grandfanda
grandfanda.meaning: The first mortal pilgrim of time to reach Havona, from planet 341 of system 84 in constellation 62 of local universe 1,131 in superuniverse one (24:6.8, 7:5.8).

gravity.name: gravedad
gravity.meaning: The sole control of energy-matter, and by extension the drawing circuits of personality, spirit, mind, and material gravity (0:6.11).

rejected.reason: The reader must not bring this; the sense is a drawing force.

gravity-messengers.name: Mensajeros de la Gravedad
gravity-messengers.meaning: Personal messengers able to transcend time and space, under the jurisdiction of Grandfanda and assigned to the primary Corps of the Finality (31:2.1, 23:3.2).

great-spirit.name: Gran Espíritu
great-spirit.meaning: The deity concept of the American red men, revived by Onamonalonton and kept from the Dalamatian teachings (64:6.7, 92:4.5).

rejected.reason: After the noun 'grande' means physical size; 'Gran' before the noun gives the sense of greatness.

greater-road.name: Camino Mayor
greater-road.meaning: The Mahayana, the 'Great Road' to salvation of the Chinese and north Indian Buddhists, in contrast with the Hinayana or 'Lesser Road' of the south (94:9.5, 94:12.2).

rejected.reason: A different image; the English says 'road'.
Possible, but 'camino' is the plain word for 'road'.

greater-road.note: 'Camino' is also the glossary form of 'Way' (Father's Way: Camino del Padre). The contexts differ, but a reviewer can check the overlap. 'Lesser Road' must then be 'Camino Menor'.

greece.name: Grecia
greece.meaning: Ancient Greece and its culture and philosophy (98:1.1, 195:1.1).

greeks.name: griegos
greeks.meaning: The ancient Greek people, teachers, artists, traders, and colonizers of the Mediterranean (80:7, 98:1-2).

green-race.name: raza verde
green-race.meaning: One of the six Sangik races, among the less able primitive groups, weakened by migrations in many directions (64:6.17).

gregorian-calendar.name: calendario gregoriano
gregorian-calendar.meaning: The present leap-year calendar of 365¼ days, which the revelators use to give time (57:0.1, 14:1.12).

rejected.reason: Alone it can read as a calendar for one leap year; keep it with "actual" as an alias.

guardian-angels.name: ángeles guardianes
guardian-angels.meaning: Seraphim assigned to individual mortals or groups of mortals, who minister to them in life and keep the identity of the surviving soul until the resurrection (Paper 113).

rejected.reason: A natural devotional set phrase, but it brings a popular image of a child's protector; 'guardianes' also matches 'serafines guardianes'.
Liturgical tone and less common across Latin America.

guardians-of-destiny.name: guardianes del destino
guardians-of-destiny.meaning: Personal seraphim assigned to a mortal who reaches the third circle or makes the supreme decision, who keep the soul's survival values after death and can go with the mortal to Paradise (113:6.1, 113:7.5).

rejected.reason: Popular religious term with a different idea.

gulf-of-mexico.name: golfo de México
gulf-of-mexico.meaning: The gulf formed when Mexico emerged 310 million years ago, a refuge of marine life (59:2.7, 59:6.9).

gulf-stream.name: corriente del Golfo
gulf-stream.meaning: The Atlantic ocean current, which in the Cambrian age flowed over central North America and warmed Greenland, and which the papers use as an image of a localized energy current (59:1.17, 29:2.15).

guru-nanak.name: Gurú Nanak
guru-nanak.meaning: The fifteenth-century leader who synthesized Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism into Sikhism (92:5.8, 92:5.15).

hades.name: Hades
hades.meaning: The Greek place for weak souls, and the place of torment in Jesus' parable of the rich man (86:4.8, 169:3.2).

hammurabi.name: Hammurabi
hammurabi.meaning: The Mesopotamian ruler at whose rise the Sumerians were absorbed, who used burning as a punishment (78:8.10, 70:10.14).

han-empire.name: Imperio han
han-empire.meaning: The Chinese empire, the great world power of the East in the times of Jesus (134:5.1).

hanavard.name: Hanavard
hanavard.meaning: Primary Lanonandek Son number 67, high counselor and acting chairman of the executive council of Satania (45:3.8, 45:3.10).

hap.name: Hap
hap.meaning: The member of Caligastia's corporeal staff who led the college of revealed religion, stayed loyal with Van, and gave the early races the moral code called 'The Father's Way' (66:7.8, 67:4.1).

harmony-supervisors.name: Supervisores de la Armonía
harmony-supervisors.meaning: Tertiary supernaphim of the first circuit who co-ordinate all work in Havona so that everything moves smoothly (26:3.4, 28:5.16).

havona.name: Havona
havona.meaning: The eternal central universe of perfect worlds that surrounds Paradise (0:0.5, 14:0.1).

havona-centers.name: Centros de Havona
havona-centers.meaning: Supreme Power Centers, one million in the central universe, each supervising a thousand Havona worlds (29:2.12).

havona-graph-method.name: método gráfico de Havona
havona-graph-method.meaning: A Havona method by which intelligence co-ordinators assimilate in one hour what mortal telegraphy needs a thousand years to record; its nature is beyond human comprehension (26:3.8, 27:6.4).

rejected.reason: "grafo" is a mathematical term; the papers do not say what the graph is.

havona-graph-method.note: The papers do not explain the method. "gráfico" keeps the English word open, but it can suggest a chart.

havona-natives.name: nativos de Havona
aliases: habitantes de los mundos de Havona
havona-natives.meaning: The beings created by the Trinity who are the native inhabitants of the billion worlds of the central universe (14:4, 37:9.12).

rejected.reason: Brings an ethnic and social sense.

havona-pilgrims.name: peregrinos de Havona
havona-pilgrims.meaning: Ascending mortals who reach the central universe and pass inward through the seven circuits of Havona toward Paradise (Paper 26, 24:6.4).

rejected.reason: 'romero' is a pilgrim to a local shrine and a herb; folk sense.

havona-servitals.name: Servitales de Havona
havona-servitals.meaning: Beings created by the Master Spirits with the Supreme Power Directors, who serve in Havona and the superuniverses, and some of whom become Graduate Guides (25:1.3, 25:1.7).

rejected.reason: Too generic; the coined '-al' form reads as a term.

hebrew-language.name: lengua hebrea
hebrew-language.meaning: The language of the Hebrews, who had no general written form until they learned an alphabet from the Philistines (74:8.9).

hebrews-book-of.name: Hebreos, Libro de
hebrews-book-of.meaning: The New Testament book that saw Melchizedek's mission and that, with James, shows the religion of Jesus more than Paul's (93:9.11, 196:2.1).

rejected.reason: The usual Spanish title, but the papers say "Book". A reviewer can prefer it.

henotheism.name: henoteísmo
henotheism.meaning: The stage of belief between polytheism and monotheism in which one god is held supreme while other gods are believed to exist as subordinate (96:1.2, 96:1.14).

henselon.name: Henselon
henselon.meaning: A local universe near Nebadon, the only one in Orvonton that lost more Lanonandek Sons (32:2.12, 35:9.8).

herod-antipas.name: Herodes Antipas
herod-antipas.meaning: Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, who killed John the Baptist (135:12.1).

herod-archelaus.name: Herodes Arquelao
herod-archelaus.meaning: The son of Herod and brother of Antipas who ruled Judea, whom Joseph feared, and whose futile attempt to gain the kingdom of Judea underlies the parable of the pounds (123:0.5, 171:8.2).

herod-the-great.name: Herodes el Grande
herod-the-great.meaning: The former king, father of Herod Antipas, whose Maccabean palace in Jerusalem Antipas used (185:4.1).

herodians.name: herodianos
herodians.meaning: A purely political party that wanted freedom from direct Roman rule by a return of the Herodian dynasty (137:7.10, 148:7.3).

herodias.name: Herodías
herodias.meaning: The unlawful wife of Herod Antipas who hated John the Baptist and had her daughter ask for his head (135:12.2, 135:12.6).

heshbon.name: Hesbón
heshbon.meaning: The Perean town where Jesus met Abner for the last time (171:3.2).

hierapolis.name: Hierápolis
hierapolis.meaning: The city where Philip was crucified and buried and where his daughter Leah became a prophetess (139:5.11, 139:5.12).

high-commissioners.name: Altos Comisionados
high-commissioners.meaning: Spirit-fused ascendant mortals who begin as race commissioners on the planets and rise to serve the local universe (37:5.6).
high-commissioners.note: 29:4.2 uses "high commissioners of power" in lowercase for another group (Council of Equilibrium). Translators must not confuse the two.

high-son-assistants.name: Asistentes de los Altos Hijos
high-son-assistants.meaning: Twice-trinitized sons, each the embodiment of one concept, who serve as personal aids and private secretaries to the high sons of the governments of the Ancients of Days (22:10.1, 22:1.12, 22:10.4).

rejected.reason: Reads as if the assistants are themselves high sons; they assist the high sons.
"ayudantes" is reserved for adjutant (espíritus ayudantes de la mente).

high-son-assistants.note: The English is ambiguous in form ("High Son Assistants"); 22:10.1 shows they serve the high sons, so the Spanish says "de los Altos Hijos".

high-spirit-personalities-of-circuit-con.name: altas personalidades espirituales del control de circuitos (no reveladas)
high-spirit-personalities-of-circuit-con.meaning: Unrevealed high spirit personalities who help the circuit supervisors direct the circuits for spirit messages and the transit of personalities (Paper 24).

rejected.form: altas personalidades de espíritu del control de circuitos
rejected.reason: Awkward; 'de espíritu' reads as 'spirited'.
'Superiores' is reserved for 'higher' (Personalidades Superiores del Espíritu Infinito).

higher-personalities-of-the-infinite-spi.name: Personalidades Superiores del Espíritu Infinito
higher-personalities-of-the-infinite-spi.meaning: The seven orders of higher personalities of the Infinite Spirit (Solitary Messengers, Universe Circuit Supervisors, Census Directors, Personal Aids, Associate Inspectors, Assigned Sentinels, Graduate Guides) (Paper 24, 45:1.8).

rejected.reason: 'Alta' is used for 'high' elsewhere in the papers; 'Higher' is a comparative and needs 'Superiores'.

himalayas.name: Himalaya
himalayas.meaning: The great Asian mountain range, among the greatest crustal upheavals, begun 290 million years ago (59:3.3).

rejected.reason: Spanish uses the singular.

hinduism.name: hinduismo
hinduism.meaning: The oldest and most adaptable of the major religions, an integral part of the social life of India (94:4).

hippos.name: Hipos
hippos.meaning: A Decapolis city where the apostles worked (138:9.3).

hittites.name: hititas
hittites.meaning: An ancient people of Andonite stock with pale skins and broad heads (80:8.2).

holy-area.name: Área Santa
holy-area.meaning: The outlying residential region of upper Paradise, divided into seven concentric zones, the 'Father's Paradise mansions', where Paradise Citizens, Havona natives, and ascenders dwell (11:3.1, 11:3.3).

rejected.reason: The name of Palestine in Spanish.
'zona' names the seven concentric parts inside the Holy Area.

holy-area.note: The English alias 'area of the Most Holy' is odd next to the separate 'Most Holy Sphere'; a reviewer can check it.

holy-of-holies.name: lugar santísimo
holy-of-holies.meaning: The innermost sanctuary of the Jerusalem temple behind the veil, entered only by high priests and lifelong Nazarites (135:1.2, 125:2.5).

rejected.reason: Latin, and in common use it also means a private retreat.
Reads as a person, the holiest of saints.

holy-spirit.name: Espíritu Santo
holy-spirit.meaning: The spiritual circuit of the local universe Creative Spirit (Divine Minister), confined to the local universe, distinct from the omnipresent Infinite Spirit (8:5.3, 34:5.5, 194:2.17).

rejected.reason: Not natural Spanish for this name; 'Espíritu Santo' is the plain form and matches the scriptural phrase the papers quote.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) third person of the Christian Trinity
rejected.reason: The reader must not identify it with the Infinite Spirit; the papers define it as the circuit of the local universe Mother Spirit (8:5.3).

honan.name: Honán
honan.meaning: The region of China east of Kansu where the most progressive Chinese settlements lay and where Andite infiltration stimulated advanced civilization (79:7.1, 79:7.5).

rejected.reason: The modern romanization; the English uses the older name.

honen-shonin.name: Honen Shonin
honen-shonin.meaning: A Japanese Buddhist teacher in whose teaching, with Ryonin's and Shinran's, the God concept came to the belief in Amida Buddha (94:12.2).

hosea.name: Oseas
hosea.meaning: The Hebrew prophet after Amos who preached forgiveness through repentance and a God of love (97:4.5).

hudson-bay.name: bahía de Hudson
hudson-bay.meaning: The bay of northeastern Canada with the most remnants of preocean rock, and where an Indian tribe met an Eskimo group (57:8.12, 64:7.19).

hudson-river.name: río Hudson
hudson-river.meaning: The North American river along whose west bank stand the Catskill Mountains, a geologic monument of the Devonian floods (59:4.15).

i-am.name: YO SOY
i-am.meaning: The philosophic concept of the Universal Father as the infinite, eternal, and absolute primal cause before any differentiation of reality (105:1.1, 105:2.1).

rejected.reason: the English keeps full capitals; keep them

iceland.name: Islandia
iceland.meaning: The northern island that in one epoch, with Greenland, connected North America and Europe (61:1.12).

idealism.name: idealismo
idealism.meaning: Devotion to high spiritual concepts and values above material ends, which in the papers must also be practical.
forcedChoices: 'idealismo': The reader must not bring the philosophical school (mind over matter) where the papers mean devotion to ideals.

identity.name: identidad
identity.meaning: The continuing sameness of a self or of an energy system, which personality can unify; in man it is at first material and temporary, and its seat can pass to the morontia soul (112:0.7, 112:5.4, 112:2.20, 112:3.7).

rejected.form: identidad (sense of a document or social group)
rejected.reason: Ordinary senses the reader must not bring: a national or social identity, or an ID card. Here it is the continuing sameness of the self.

idumea.name: Idumea
idumea.meaning: A region south of Judea, governed with Judea and Samaria by Pilate (185:0.1, 149:1.2).

ikhnaton.name: Akenatón
ikhnaton.meaning: The young Egyptian king who kept alive the doctrine of El Elyon, the One God, in Egypt (95:5.2).

rejected.reason: An older English spelling; rule 2 asks for the standard Spanish form of a historical person.

ikhnaton.note: Spanish spellings vary (Akenatón, Ajenatón, Akhenatón). A human can choose one for the whole book.

illinois.name: Illinois
illinois.meaning: The North American state whose ten coal layers show how often the land fell and rose, and which the fourth ice sheet reached (59:5.17, 61:7.2).

immanence-of-the-projected-incomplete.name: Inmanencia de lo Incompleto Proyectado
immanence-of-the-projected-incomplete.meaning: The living presence of the evolving Supreme, seen in a fortuitous co-ordination of unrelated events, which may be a forecast of the Supreme reflected back to the created levels (4:1.10, 117:7.6).

rejected.reason: The masculine reads as a person; the English names a thing or state.
Makes "incomplete" a quality of the projection; the English noun is "the Incomplete".

immanence-of-the-projected-incomplete.note: 117:7.6 says "It may be that..."; translators must keep that tentative wording.
forcedChoices: Spanish forces a gender for "Incomplete"; the neuter "lo" keeps it impersonal, as the English is.

immanuel.name: Immanuel
immanuel.meaning: The Union of Days assigned to Nebadon, ambassador of the Paradise Trinity to Michael, whose name means 'God with us' (33:4).

rejected.reason: The usual Spanish form of the biblical name; but here it names a particular being of this book, so the English spelling stays to keep the person distinct from the prophecy.

impersonal.name: impersonal
impersonal.meaning: Without personality; the impersonal never transmutes directly into the personal (0:5.4, 0:1.17, 56:9.5).

rejected.reason: 'Nonpersonal' is a separate English word in the papers (0:5.2, 0:5.5).
The reader must not read it as a lack of warmth.

imports-of-time.name: Alcances del Tiempo
imports-of-time.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim who evaluate time: they show how much time an undertaking requires, are consulted to forecast events, and testify that every being had time to choose (28:6.10, 28:6.11).

rejected.reason: "significados" already renders "meanings", and "Significances of Origins" is a sister order.
Unnatural plural, and it reads as "how important time is".
"importe" means an amount of money.
"time evaluators" is the papers' description (28:6.11), not the name.

imports-of-time.note: English "import" here means the bearing or significance of time. No Spanish noun matches it well. A human must choose.

india.name: India
india.meaning: The land of India, home of a very mixed population of all the races (79:2.1).

rejected.reason: Refers to the religion; 'indio' is the gentilic. Note that 'indio' can also mean a native American in Latin America; context decides.

indian-ocean.name: océano Índico
indian-ocean.meaning: The ocean to which the Mediterranean was once connected (61:3.8, 64:1.1).

indigo-race.name: raza índigo
indigo-race.meaning: The sixth of the Sangik colored races, which migrated to Africa and stayed there (64:6).

rejected.reason: 'añil' is correct but less known for the color in all countries; 'índigo' matches the English.

indo-china.name: Indochina
indo-china.meaning: The southeast Asian peninsula where the cultures of India and China blended and where the green race persisted most; a Hinayana Buddhist region (79:6.2, 94:9.4).

rejected.reason: English spelling; Spanish writes one word.

indra.name: Indra
indra.meaning: The Vedic Aryan god, 'the tempestuous lord of the atmosphere', later a secondary Hindu deity (94:1.3, 94:4.6).

indus.name: Indo
indus.meaning: The river of India whose valley drew the Andites about 8000 B.C. (79:1.3, 79:2.4).

infinite.name: Infinito
infinite.meaning: The fullness, the finality, implied by the primacy of the First Source and Center; an actual value-level of the free will of the Universal Father, also called the Father-Infinite (0:3.24, 0:3.25).

rejected.reason: Done as the word for 'infinity'; the Foreword keeps 'the Infinite' and 'infinity' apart (0:3.24).
Adds 'being', which the English does not say.

infinite.note: Same letters as the done adjective 'infinite: infinito'; only the capital and the article 'el' mark the noun. The reader must not take it as the plain adjective.

infinite-mind.name: Mente Infinita
infinite-mind.meaning: The mind of the Infinite Spirit, present throughout creation through the intelligence circuits.

infinite-spirit.name: Espíritu Infinito
infinite-spirit.meaning: The Third Person of Deity, the agent of the combined action of the Father and the Son, the God of Action and source of mind (8:0.1, 8:1.1, 23:0.1).

rejected.reason: 'Agente' can read as a representative or a police agent; 'Actor' keeps the sense of the one who acts, as in the English.
'Manipulador' carries a sense of deceit in Spanish, as 'manipulator' does in English; kept because the English uses this word for the handling of energies. Reviewer can check.

infinity.name: infinitud
infinity.meaning: The quality and level of the infinite: the unqualified reality of the I AM, potential infinity being absolute and inseparable from eternity (0:3.21, 0:11.1, 0:11.12).

rejected.reason: Common Spanish for 'a huge number' (una infinidad de cosas); it loses the quality sense.
Reserved for 'the Infinite' (0:3.24), a different English term.

iniquity.name: iniquidad
iniquity.meaning: The willful, determined, and persistent transgression of divine law, indicative of vanishing personality control (67:1.4, 67:1.5).

rejected.reason: Too general; does not carry the persistent, willful sense.
Only injustice.

inquiring-greeks.name: griegos inquisitivos
inquiring-greeks.meaning: The Greeks who came to Philip in Jerusalem asking to see Jesus and were brought to him by Philip and Andrew (139:5.9).

rejected.reason: Calls up the Inquisition.
Suggests an investigation, not a request.

inquiring-greeks.note: 'inquiring' here means 'asking' (they asked to see Jesus). 'inquisitivos' can read as 'nosy'; a reviewer can prefer 'griegos que preguntaban'.

inspired-trinity-spirits.name: Espíritus Inspirados de la Trinidad
aliases: Espíritus Inspirados de la Trinidad del Paraíso
inspired-trinity-spirits.meaning: A somewhat impersonal, largely secret order of Trinity-origin beings whose ministry is superconscious (19:0.1).

rejected.reason: Word order can read as 'Spirits of the inspired Trinity'.
Closes a reading the English leaves open: the English does not say the Trinity inspires them.

instigators-of-rest.name: iniciadores del descanso
instigators-of-rest.meaning: Primary supernaphim, inspectors of Paradise on the inner Havona circuit, who make pilgrims ready for the last transition sleep and their introduction to eternity (27:1.1, 26:11.6).

rejected.reason: 'instigador' in Spanish suggests inciting a wrong act.
'promotor' has a commercial or event sense.
Possible; 'descanso' is the plainer word for the 'divine rest' of 27:1.1.

instigators-of-rest.note: The partner order 'complements of rest' must use the same word for 'rest' (descanso).

intelligence-co-ordinators-seraphic-corp.name: coordinadores de información (Cuerpo Seráfico de Culminación)
intelligence-co-ordinators-seraphic-corp.meaning: Glorified completion seraphim who coordinate the exchange of news and information with the broadcasters (26:3.8 for the Havona order; 39:2.9).

rejected.reason: 'inteligencia' reads as intellect or espionage; here 'intelligence' is news

intelligence-co-ordinators-tertiary-supe.name: coordinadores de información (supernafines terciarios)
intelligence-co-ordinators-tertiary-supe.meaning: Tertiary supernaphim, the 'living newspapers' of Havona, who keep ascenders informed of the affairs of the universe of universes and promote fellowship between ascending and descending pilgrims (26:3.8).

rejected.reason: 'inteligencia' means intellect or espionage; the glossary already uses 'información' for the seraphic order of the same name.

interpreters-and-translators.name: intérpretes y traductores
interpreters-and-translators.meaning: A group of the Morontia Companions who know all the tongues of a local universe and serve ascending mortals as linguists and language teachers on the mansion worlds (48:3.12, 48:3.13, 47:3.11).

rejected.reason: 'translators' is already a separate term (traductores); this order needs both words.

interpreters-of-cosmic-citizenship.name: intérpretes de la ciudadanía cósmica
interpreters-of-cosmic-citizenship.meaning: Administrator seraphim who guide new citizens of the system capitals and quicken their appreciation of the responsibilities of universe government (39:4.7, 39:4.9).

interpreters-of-ethics.name: intérpretes de la ética
interpreters-of-ethics.meaning: Primary supernaphim who help Paradise arrivals adjust to the many groups of majestic beings before entry into the Corps of Mortal Finaliters (27:0.8, 27:3.3).

rejected.reason: Says the interpreters are ethical, not that they interpret ethics.

iran.name: Irán
iran.meaning: The Iranian plateau and its peoples, a corridor of Andite migration and land of Zoroaster (79:1, 95:6).

iron-city.name: Irón (ciudad)
iron-city.meaning: A Galilean town with mineral mines where Jesus worked with the miners and taught in the synagogue on the first preaching tour (146:0.1, 146:4.1, 146:4.2, 173:1.6).

rejected.reason: Translates the English homograph; the town name is Hebrew, not the metal.
Reads as the English word; the standard Spanish biblical form of this place is Irón.

iron-city.note: Check that Irón is the accepted Spanish form for this Galilean town.

iroquois.name: iroqueses
iroquois.meaning: The federation of six nations of northern American red men, their nearest approach to a state (71:1.3).

isaac-old-testament.name: Isaac (Antiguo Testamento)
isaac-old-testament.meaning: The son of Abraham and Sarah, born after Melchizedek's promise (93:6.5, 93:9.8).

isador.name: Isador
isador.meaning: A disciple of Matthew who wrote the Gospel of Matthew in Greek (121:8.5).

isaiah-first.name: Isaías (el primero)
isaiah-first.meaning: The first of the two Hebrew prophets named Isaiah; he appeared after an awakening of conscience in the Hebrew nations and preached a God of universal creation and upholding (97:5.1, 97:7.6).

rejected.reason: A term of biblical scholarship; the papers say 'the first Isaiah', a plain ordinal.

isaiah-second.name: Isaías (el segundo)
isaiah-second.meaning: The young prophet of the Babylonian captivity whose writings are chapters 40 to 55 of the book of Isaiah (97:7.4).

ishtar.name: Ishtar
ishtar.meaning: The Mesopotamian mother of gods and spirit of sex fertility, whose cult the Salem teachers never overcame (95:1.5, 95:1.7).

isis.name: Isis
isis.meaning: The Egyptian form of the goddess Ishtar (95:1.7).

islam.name: islam
islam.meaning: The monotheistic religion of the followers of Mohammed (also called Mohammedanism), the religio-cultural connective of North Africa, the Levant, and southeastern Asia (92:6.19, 5:4.5).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes religion names in lowercase, as in 'budismo' and 'cristianismo' in this glossary.

isle-of-paradise.name: Isla del Paraíso
isle-of-paradise.meaning: The stationary Isle at the heart of the central universe, the geographic center of infinity and the dwelling place of the eternal God (0:0.5).

rejected.reason: Reads as a resort name; Spanish needs the "de" link.

isle-of-patmos.name: isla de Patmos
isle-of-patmos.meaning: The Greek island where the apostle John was banished for four years and wrote the Book of Revelation (historical place).

rejected.reason: The capital on the generic noun is not the standard Spanish form for this historical place.

forcedChoices: lowercase "isla": Standard Spanish writes the generic geographic noun in lowercase before a historical place name.

israel.name: Israel
israel.meaning: The northern Hebrew kingdom (Ephraim), dispersed after it refused tribute to Assyria (97:9.21).

israelites.name: israelitas
israelites.meaning: The northern Hebrew tribes (only three or four settled in Palestine) whose union with the Canaanites formed the Hebrew nation; their consciousness arose in Ephraim (97:9.1, 97:9.2).

italy.name: Italia
italy.meaning: The land to which Andites came from the Aegean islands (80:7.11).

jacob-old-testament.name: Jacob (Antiguo Testamento)
jacob-old-testament.meaning: The patriarch who slept on a stone because he venerated it and anointed it (85:1.1).

jacob-s-well.name: pozo de Jacob
jacob-s-well.meaning: The well in Samaria on the route that Jews often avoided (124:6.1).

jacob-the-stone-mason-father.name: Jacob el cantero (padre)
jacob-the-stone-mason-father.meaning: A Nazareth neighbor and adviser of Joseph's family, a stone mason, whose son was Jesus' favorite playmate (123:6.9, 128:2.2).

rejected.reason: 'albañil' is a bricklayer, not a stone mason.

jacob-the-stone-mason-father.note: The done term 'Jacob (hijo del cantero)' uses 'cantero'; this form follows it.

jacob-the-stone-mason-son.name: Jacob (hijo del cantero)
jacob-the-stone-mason-son.meaning: The neighbor boy, son of the stone mason, who appointed himself Jesus' defender in childhood (124:2.4, 133:1.5).

rejected.reason: Also a Spanish form, but 'Jacob' is the plain form of the Hebrew name.
'albañil' is a bricklayer, not a stone mason.

jainism.name: jainismo
jainism.meaning: One of the composite religions that the papers list (92:6.10).

jairus.name: Jairo
jairus.meaning: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum whose only daughter Jesus went to heal (152:0.1, 153:1.7).

james-brother-of-jesus.name: Santiago (hermano de Jesús)
james-brother-of-jesus.meaning: James, the second-born brother of Jesus, later head of the church at Jerusalem.

rejected.reason: Also used in Spanish, but 'Santiago' matches the done term 'Santiago Zebedeo'.

james-of-safed.name: Santiago de Safed
james-of-safed.meaning: A citizen of Tiberias whose epileptic, demon-possessed son Jesus healed; he said 'Lord, I believe. I pray you help my unbelief' (158:4.2, 158:5.2).

rejected.reason: 'James' is Santiago in the terms already done.

james-zebedee.name: Santiago Zebedeo
james-zebedee.meaning: James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, one of the twelve and the first apostle martyred (139:3.1).

rejected.reason: Used in some Bibles, but 'Santiago' is the common Spanish name of this apostle across countries.

japan.name: Japón
japan.meaning: The island country of eastern Asia, named among regions of great crustal change (60:3.6).

java.name: Java
java.meaning: The island in the east reached by Andonic migrants over a land path from Europe and Asia, and where Buddhism later became established (64:1.6, 64:1.5, 94:9.1).

jebus.name: Jebús
jebus.meaning: The strong-walled city of the Jebusites that David made his capital, Jerusalem (97:9.11).

jehovah.name: Jehová
jehovah.meaning: A recent term for the completed Hebrew concept of Yahweh; not used until fifteen hundred years after Jesus (96:1.10, 94:12.1).

jehu.name: Jehú
jehu.meaning: The country landlord who joined Jehonadab to destroy the Baal prophets at Samaria, completing Elijah's reform (97:9.19, 124:6.3).

jeremiah.name: Jeremías
jeremiah.meaning: The Hebrew prophet of the time of the siege of Jerusalem.

jericho.name: Jericó
jericho.meaning: The ancient city near the Jordan crossing that Jesus visited several times.

jerusalem.name: Jerusalén
jerusalem.meaning: The historical city of Palestine, earlier Salem and Jebus, center of Jewish worship with its temple, where Jesus taught and was crucified (Papers 121-187).

jerusalem-temple.name: templo de Jerusalén
jerusalem-temple.meaning: The temple at Jerusalem, center of Jewish worship and sacrifice, where Jesus taught (173:1.1).

jerusalem-temple-guards.name: guardias del templo de Jerusalén
jerusalem-temple-guards.meaning: The Jewish guards of the temple, who were on duty at Jesus' tomb with the Roman guard (189:1.2).

jerusem.name: Jerusem
jerusem.meaning: The headquarters world of the local system of Satania, encircled by fifty-six worlds of transition culture (47:0.1, 46:5.27).

jesus.name: Jesús
jesus.meaning: Jesus of Nazareth, the human life on Urantia of the Creator Son Michael of Nebadon (0:0.5, 194:3.1).

jews.name: judíos
jews.meaning: The Jewish people, descendants of the Hebrews (97:0.1, 121:2.1).

jews-ancient-hebrews.name: judíos (antiguos hebreos)
jews-ancient-hebrews.meaning: The ancient Hebrew people, Abraham's descendants together with adopted nomads, from whom the Jewish nation formed (Papers 96-97).

jezreel.name: Jezreel
jezreel.meaning: The town and road junction in Palestine where Jesus' family turned east toward the Jordan valley on the journey to Jerusalem (124:6.1, 124:6.3).

joab.name: Joab
joab.meaning: A young evangelist, ringleader of the plot to make Jesus king at the feeding of the five thousand and leader of the evangelists (152:2.5, 153:5.2).

joanna.name: Juana
joanna.meaning: The wife of Chuza, steward of Herod Antipas, one of the ten women Jesus set apart for the ministering work of the kingdom (150:1.1).

job-book.name: Job (libro)
job-book.meaning: The Old Testament book that reflects the teachings of the Salem school in Mesopotamia and shows that suffering is not always punishment for sin (95:1.10, 148:6.11).

john-mark.name: Juan Marcos
john-mark.meaning: John Mark, the boy of chores for Jesus and the apostles, later the writer of the Gospel of Mark (121:8.2, 177:2.1).

john-the-baptist.name: Juan el Bautista
john-the-baptist.meaning: John, son of Zacharias and Elizabeth, who preached repentance and baptized Jesus (135:0.1).

john-zebedee.name: Juan Zebedeo
john-zebedee.meaning: John, son of Zebedee, the youngest of the twelve apostles (139:4.1).

jonah.name: Jonás
jonah.meaning: The Hebrew scriptural figure whose story Jesus used about running from duty and God's love for the so-called heathen, whether or not Jonah lived (130:1.2, 159:4.4).
forcedChoices: 'We are all Jonahs' (130:1.2): Spanish 'Jonás' is the same in the plural, so a translator writes 'todos somos Jonás' or 'todos somos como Jonás'.

joppa.name: Jope
joppa.meaning: A port town on the Mediterranean coast of Palestine where Jesus met Gadiah the Philistine interpreter (130:1.1, 134:7.4).

rejected.reason: The modern name; the papers use the ancient name.

jordan-river.name: río Jordán
jordan-river.meaning: The river of Palestine in which John baptized, and in which Jesus was baptized near Pella (135:6.4, 163:5.1).

joseph-brother-of-jesus.name: José (hermano de Jesús)
joseph-brother-of-jesus.meaning: The fourth child of the Nazareth family, born March 16, A.D. 1 (123:4.9).

joseph-father-of-jesus.name: José (padre de Jesús)
joseph-father-of-jesus.meaning: Joseph, the human father of Jesus, a carpenter and builder of Nazareth who died in an accident when Jesus was fourteen (122:1.1, 126:2.2).

joseph-of-arimathea.name: José de Arimatea
joseph-of-arimathea.meaning: A wealthy member of the Sanhedrin and a believer who gave his tomb for the body of Jesus; his daughter Rebecca joined the women's corps (150:1.1).

joseph-of-tyre.name: José de Tiro
joseph-of-tyre.meaning: A Jewish believer living south of Tyre near the tomb of Hiram, at whose home Jesus kept his headquarters while the apostles taught in Tyre (156:4.1).

joseph-old-testament.name: José (Antiguo Testamento)
joseph-old-testament.meaning: The great-grandson of Abraham, a believer in Melchizedek, who chose to serve Egypt as a civil administrator (93:9.5).

joshua-jesus.name: Josué (Jesús)
joshua-jesus.meaning: The name Gabriel told Mary to give her son, Jesus' Hebrew name, used by those around him (122:3.1, 133:2.4).

rejected.reason: Not the plain form; the English uses the common form Joshua.
Loses the point that the text gives the Hebrew name.

joshua-jesus.note: Josué is also 'Joshua (Old Testament)'; the qualifier keeps them apart. A reader can miss that Josué and Jesús are one name.

joshua-old-testament.name: Josué (Antiguo Testamento)
joshua-old-testament.meaning: The leader of Israel after Moses who kept the Mosaic tradition of God while the common people reverted to the older desert idea of Yahweh (96:6.1).

josiah-blind-beggar.name: Josías (mendigo ciego)
josiah-blind-beggar.meaning: The blind man whom Jesus healed on a Sabbath in Jerusalem by the pool of Siloam, and who became a lifelong preacher of the gospel (164:3.8, 164:5.6, 171:5.1).

josiah-king.name: Josías (rey)
josiah-king.meaning: The king of Judah whose reform era ended when he went out to intercept Necho's army and was killed, after which Judah fell under Egyptian tribute (97:9.24, 126:1.2).

jotapata.name: Jotapata
jotapata.meaning: A Galilean town where Jesus taught the believers (156:6.2).

judaism.name: judaísmo
judaism.meaning: The religion of the Jews that grew from the Hebrew faith and held the concept of one God (97:0.1, 121:2.1).

judas-iscariot.name: Judas Iscariote
judas-iscariot.meaning: The Judean apostle, treasurer of the twelve, who betrayed Jesus (139:12.1).

judas-maccabee.name: Judas Macabeo
judas-maccabee.meaning: The Jewish leader whose exploits of deliverance raised the expectation of the Messiah (121:2.7).

jude.name: Judas (hermano de Jesús)
jude.meaning: Jude, the youngest brother of Jesus, of fiery and patriotic temper (127:1.6, 128:4.6).

rejected.reason: the name of the patriarch and the tribe
not a Spanish form

forcedChoices: Judas, with the qualifier: Spanish has one name for English 'Jude' and 'Judas'; the English keeps them apart

judea.name: Judea
judea.meaning: The southern region of Palestine, with Jerusalem.

julias.name: Julias
julias.meaning: A Perean residence of Herod Antipas, with Machaerus (135:12.1); not the same as Bethsaida-Julias in Gaulanitis (138:9.3).

jupiter-god.name: Júpiter (dios)
jupiter-god.meaning: The Roman god honored, with Juno and Minerva, in the temple on the Capitolium (132:0.2).

jupiter-planet.name: Júpiter (planeta)
jupiter-planet.meaning: The giant planet of the solar system, formed with Saturn from the central portion of the matter that Angona pulled from the sun (57:5.9, 57:6.5).

justa.name: Justa
justa.meaning: Daughter of Bernice; Jesus stayed at her home north of Sidon and taught the twenty-four there each morning (156:2.2, 156:2.5).

justice-guides.name: guías de la justicia
justice-guides.meaning: Administrator seraphim who present the summary of evidence on the eternal welfare of men and angels in the tribunals and prepare the defense of doubtful survival cases (39:4.4, 39:4.5).

rejected.reason: Narrows the sense to court officials; the English names justice itself.

justus-jewish-merchant-of-corinth.name: Justo (mercader judío de Corinto)
justus-jewish-merchant-of-corinth.meaning: A devout Jewish merchant of Corinth, living beside the synagogue, who often hosted Jesus and Ganid and later the Apostle Paul (133:3.5).

rejected.reason: Spanish gives Latin personal names in their Spanish form.

justus-jewish-merchant-of-corinth.note: "Justo" is also the common adjective "just". The capital and the qualifier must show that it is a name.

kaaba-stone.name: piedra de la Kaaba
kaaba-stone.meaning: The black stone fetish in a temple at Mecca, revered by almost all Arabian tribes, which later led to Islam (95:7.5, 88:1.2).

rejected.reason: Also valid in Spanish, but Kaaba is more common and matches the English.

kansas.name: Kansas
kansas.meaning: The U.S. state that marked the southern limit of the central ice sheet in the first and last glaciers (61:5.5, 61:7.9).

karuska.name: Karuska
karuska.meaning: The woman at whose home near Sidon Jesus lodged, whose servant brought the Syrian woman Norana to him (156:1.1, 156:1.2).

kc-absolute.name: absoluto
kc-absolute.meaning: Beginningless, endless, timeless, spaceless, and unconditioned; the third level of reality after the finite and the absonite (0:1.13, 0:11.12).

rejected.reason: 'Total' and 'totality' are separate words in the papers.
The reader must not read it as a mere intensifier ('un absoluto desastre').

kc-absonite.name: absonito
kc-absonite.meaning: The level of reality between the finite and the absolute, of things and beings without beginnings or endings that transcend time and space and are eventuated, not created (0:1.12, 0:9.2).

rejected.reason: Spanish needs an agreeing adjective; "absonito" and "absonita" follow the noun's gender.

kc-actualize.name: actualizar
kc-actualize.meaning: To pass from potential to actual existence, to bring into full expression what was only a capacity (0:4.1, 115:3.16, 117:2.9).

rejected.reason: The papers use 'realize' and 'realization' as separate words (115:3.16), and 'realizar' is also 'to do'.
Breaks the family with 'actual' and 'actualidad'.
The reader must not bring 'to update, to bring up to date'. The sense is the philosophical one, 'to put into act'.

kc-actualize.note: Family root 'act-': actual, actualidad, actualizar, beside potencial, potencialidad. The common Spanish sense 'update' is a risk.

kc-ascender.name: ascendente
kc-ascender.meaning: A creature of evolutionary origin who climbs from the material worlds toward Paradise (13:1.21, 20:1.1).

rejected.reason: Means an elevator.
The reader must not bring these; the sense is one who ascends. Matches 'mortales ascendentes'.

kc-ascension-career.name: carrera de ascensión
kc-ascension-career.meaning: The whole course of a creature's ascent from the material worlds to Paradise.

rejected.reason: Breaks the family root 'ascensión'.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) 'carrera' = a race or a university degree
rejected.reason: The reader must not bring these; the sense is a course of life.

kc-associate.name: asociado
kc-associate.meaning: As noun, one who works together with another; as verb and adjective, joined in relation or function (0:1.6 'Associative Deity', 0:5.4, 8:0.4 'eternally associated persons').

rejected.reason: A business partner or a club member; a commercial sense.
Too informal and personal; loses the sense of joined function.
The reader must not bring the firm or law-office rank to it.

kc-co-ordinate.name: coordinar
kc-co-ordinate.meaning: As verb, to bring into unified and harmonious function; as adjective, equal in rank or status, as the three Paradise Deities are co-ordinate (7:7.1, 8:0.4, 42:12.13 'On Paradise the three energies are co-ordinate, in Havona co-ordinated').

rejected.reason: Mathematical 'co-ordinate' (axes); a false sense.
Explains the adjective and breaks the family with the verb, which 42:12.13 sets side by side.
As an adjective the reader must also take 'of equal rank', as in grammar ('oraciones coordinadas'), not only 'organized'.

kc-cosmic-insight.name: perspicacia cósmica
kc-cosmic-insight.meaning: A person's clear understanding of universe realities and his place among them, one of the values by which mortal progress through the cosmic circles is measured (106:0.1, 49:6.8, 100:4.2).

rejected.reason: 'Intuición' suggests knowledge without reasoning; 0:6.8 calls insight intellectual.
Collides with 'spiritual vision', which 100:4.2 sets beside cosmic insight.
Shares the root with 'Discernidores de Espíritus'.

kc-creator-creature.name: Creador-criatura
kc-creator-creature.meaning: The relationship and shared experience between Creator and created being, which the papers compare to the Father-child affection and which the Supreme personifies (3:4.7, 21:3.23, 117:1.1).

rejected.reason: 'creatura' is a Latinism, not current Spanish.

kc-enseraphimed.name: enserafinado
kc-enseraphimed.meaning: Enclosed in a transport seraphim for travel through space, in transit sleep (39:2.12, 39:5.14, 51:2.2).

rejected.reason: mixes English spelling into a Spanish verb form
plain paraphrase; the English coins one word

kc-evolutionary.name: evolutivo
kc-evolutionary.meaning: Of time-space creatures and realms that grow and progress through experience from lower to higher states, as against existential or Paradise origin (0:1.18, 0:5.1, 16:4.1).

rejected.reason: Anglicism, not standard Spanish.
Means 'a supporter of the theory of evolution', an ideological sense.

kc-existential.name: existencial
kc-existential.meaning: Eternal and without origin, existing by nature rather than through experience, as the Paradise Deities are; the opposite of experiential (0:1.14, 0:1.18, 0:4.9, 0:7.5).

rejected.reason: The reader must not bring the sense of existentialist philosophy or personal anguish ("crisis existencial").
Too broad; the Supreme is eternal in future but not existential (0:9.5).

kc-finite.name: finito
kc-finite.meaning: The level of reality of creature life and time-space limitations; finite realities always have beginnings (0:1.11).

rejected.reason: Plain 'limited'; loses the technical level set against 'absonite' and 'absolute'.

kc-guardian-of-destiny.name: guardián del destino
kc-guardian-of-destiny.meaning: The personal seraphim assigned to a mortal who reaches the third psychic circle, who keeps the life record and accompanies the survivor (110:6.14, 113:2.2, 112:4.12).

rejected.reason: carries the popular Catholic belief of a guardian from birth; the papers assign it at the third circle
the papers write 'her' for the seraphim, but the noun 'serafín' is masculine

forcedChoices: masculine 'guardián': agrees with 'serafín'; the papers use 'her', so a translator can keep feminine pronouns in the sentence

kc-indwelling.name: morada interior
kc-indwelling.meaning: The dwelling of a divine spirit (above all the Thought Adjuster) within the mind of a mortal; as adjective, 'the indwelling spirit' is the spirit that lives within (0:5.9, 0:5.10, 34:6.7).

rejected.reason: A technical term of Christian theology for the Holy Spirit in the soul; a religious sense the authors did not set.
Reads as a home address or a legal residence permit.

kc-infinite.name: infinito
kc-infinite.meaning: Without limit; the fullness implied by the primacy of the First Source and Center; 'the Infinite' (capital) is the Father-Infinite (0:3.24, 0:1).

rejected.reason: Plain 'unlimited'; loses the technical level of 'infinite' set against 'finite' and 'absolute'.

kc-isle.name: Isla
kc-isle.meaning: The Isle is Paradise as a stationary, material-like body at the center of all things, the geographic center of infinity and the dwelling place of God (0:0.5, 11:2.8, 105:3.4).

rejected.reason: Literary and archaic; the English uses the plain word.
Means a small island; the Isle is immense.

kc-mortal.name: mortal
kc-mortal.meaning: A will creature of material, evolutionary origin who is subject to physical death, and who can survive it by the soul (0:5.10, 40:9.1).

rejected.reason: Too narrow: the papers apply 'mortal' to will creatures on many worlds, not only to Urantia humans.
As an adjective Spanish 'mortal' also means 'deadly' (herida mortal, pecado mortal); the reader must not bring this sense to 'mente mortal' or 'vida mortal'.

kc-paradise-deity.name: Deidad del Paraíso
kc-paradise-deity.meaning: The existential Deity of Paradise, existing as three persons in the Paradise Trinity, as distinct from the experiential Deities that are still emerging (0:4.9, 0:7.7, 0:7.9).

rejected.reason: 'divinity' is a separate term (the quality of Deity); the two must stay distinct.

kc-perfecting.name: en perfeccionamiento
kc-perfecting.meaning: In the process of becoming perfect by evolutionary growth in time, as the superuniverses and evolutionary creatures are, in contrast to the perfect (Havona) and the perfected (32:3.14, 105:6.5, 106:1.1, 117:1.2).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'that makes something perfect' (active cause), not 'that is becoming perfect'.
Loses the idea of progress toward perfection.
Correct sense but long; kept as a possible paraphrase, not the term.

forcedChoices: adjectival phrase 'en perfeccionamiento' or relative clause 'que se perfecciona': Spanish has no one-word participle adjective with the ongoing sense of English 'perfecting'.

kc-personality-survival.name: supervivencia de la personalidad
kc-personality-survival.meaning: The survival of the personality, held by the soul and the Adjuster, past the death of the body (112:2, 112:5).

kc-prepersonal.name: prepersonal
kc-prepersonal.meaning: Of a reality that is not yet a personality but is destined to become part of one, as the Thought Adjuster (0:5.9, 0:1.3, 0:5.4).

rejected.reason: Explains and loses the term.

kc-progression.name: progresión
kc-progression.meaning: The step-by-step advance of a creature through levels of attainment, as in the circles of mortal progression and the routes of progression to Paradise (49:6.8, 40:3.1).

rejected.reason: Plainer, but reserved for the separate English word 'progress', which the papers also use (49:6.8).
The reader must not bring this.

kc-sonship.name: filiación
kc-sonship.meaning: The status of being a son of God, which a person knows and grasps by faith (140:10.9, 193:0.4, 196:3.34).

rejected.reason: Correct but long; a phrase where the English uses one word.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) 'filiación' = political membership or personal data on a record
rejected.reason: The reader must not bring these; the sense is the relation of a son to his father.

kc-spirit-born.name: nacido del espíritu
kc-spirit-born.meaning: Said of a mortal or a soul that has been born of the spirit, that is, has received and recognized the indwelling of God and lives under spirit leading (34:6.7, 34:6.13, 193:2.2, 42:12.12).

rejected.reason: Brings the evangelical 'born-again' label, a cultural sense the authors do not use.
The capital would decide that the spirit is the Spirit (a person); the English lowercase compound leaves this open, so the lowercase stays.

kc-spirit-luminosity.name: luminosidad espiritual
kc-spirit-luminosity.meaning: The 'light' that is the personality manifestation of spirit beings; a figure of speech, not related to intellectual insight or to physical light (0:6.8, 0:6.9).

rejected.reason: 'Luz' is the papers' 'light', the general word of which 'spirit luminosity' is one of three kinds (0:6.8).
Can read as the brightness of a person's mood or wit; 'espiritual' marks the spirit level better.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) the 'spiritual glow' of a saintly person
rejected.reason: The reader must not take it as a religious aura or a holy look; the papers make it a manifestation of spirit beings.

kc-spiritual.name: espiritual
kc-spiritual.meaning: Of or pertaining to spirit: that which responds to the spirit circuit of the Eternal Son and to the spirit level of reality, as against the material and the mindal (0:6.1, 0:6.2, 42:12.13).

rejected.reason: Means 'spiritist' (contact with the dead) or a philosophical school; a sense the authors do not intend.
The reader must not read it as a mood or a personal temperament; in the papers it names a level of reality.

kc-superconscious.name: superconsciente
kc-superconscious.meaning: The levels of the human mind above ordinary consciousness, the domain where the Thought Adjuster makes contact and where religious growth takes place (100:1.9, 91:2.6, 91:3.5).

rejected.reason: Also valid Spanish, but 'super-' matches 'superpersonal' and 'superuniversos'.
The papers set the superconscious against the subconscious (91:3.5).

kc-superhuman.name: sobrehumano
kc-superhuman.meaning: Above the human level, as beings, wisdom, or help from orders higher than mortals (for example the midwayers and the revelators).

rejected.reason: Less standard than "sobrehumano"; the English uses a common word.
The reader must not bring the sense "enormous effort" ("un esfuerzo sobrehumano").

kc-supermaterial.name: supermaterial
kc-supermaterial.meaning: Above the material level of reality: the morontial, mind, and spirit levels on which Deity shows its unity (0:1.2).

rejected.reason: Not a current Spanish word; "super-" follows the glossary (superpersonal, superuniversos).
Means only "not material"; loses "above".

kc-superpersonal.name: superpersonal
kc-superpersonal.meaning: Of a reality above the level of personality as creatures know it, as Deity functions superpersonally (0:1.2, 0:1.3, 0:5.4).

rejected.reason: Breaks the 'super-' family of the papers (superuniverso, superpersonal).

kc-supreme-being.name: Ser Supremo
kc-supreme-being.meaning: The evolving experiential Deity that unifies the sevenfold manifestation of Deity in the grand universe as one Lord, the eternal fusion of the finite and the infinite (0:7.7, 0:7.8, 0:7.9).

rejected.reason: Kept the form, but the reader must not take it as a generic name for God; here it names an evolving Deity distinct from the Universal Father.

kc-totality.name: totalidad
kc-totality.meaning: The whole of something taken all together, as the totality of cosmic reality or of the co-ordinated infinite nature of God (1:5.13, 10:4.6, 42:2.3).

rejected.reason: Means a set or a group; loses the sense of the complete whole.

kc-transcendental.name: trascendental
kc-transcendental.meaning: Belonging to the absonite level that transcends time and space, between finite and absolute (0:9.1, 0:9.5, 0:2.17).

rejected.reason: Valid but less common than "trascendental" in current Spanish.
The reader must not bring the sense "very important" or the sense of Kantian philosophy.

kc-triodity.name: triodidad
kc-triodity.meaning: A non-Father triune relationship, such as the triodity of actuality or of potentiality, consequent on the triunities (104:5.1, 115:3.7).

rejected.reason: Ordinary sense is an electronic valve.

kc-ultimate.name: último
kc-ultimate.meaning: In its special sense, pertaining to the absonite level of Deity and reality that transcends time and space, the second level of experiential divinity after the supreme (0:1.10, 0:1.12, 0:9.2); in many other uses it keeps its ordinary English sense of final or fundamental.

rejected.reason: Means only 'at the end'; loses the sense of a level beyond time and space and breaks the family with Ultimidad.
Not a Spanish word; reads as a coinage where the English uses a plain word.
Kept the word, but the reader must not bring the sense 'the last one'; the intended sense is the philosophical 'fundamental, beyond' as in 'realidad última'.

kenites.name: quenitas
kenites.meaning: A people with whom the line of Abraham through Isaac intermarried, the only line that long kept a clear concept of the Salem teachings (93:10.3).

rejected.reason: Also a standard Spanish form; 'quenitas' follows the -ita pattern of the done terms (Anditas, Noditas).

kentucky.name: Kentucky
kentucky.meaning: The U.S. state where a great volcano erupted 330,000,000 years ago and where Devonian coral is exposed near Louisville (59:2.5, 59:4.6).

kheresa.name: Kheresa
kheresa.meaning: The fishing village by the Sea of Galilee, home of the Alpheus twins, where Jesus called them (138:4.1).

kidron.name: Cedrón
kidron.meaning: The brook and valley beside Jerusalem near Gethsemane and the Mount of Olives (142:8.4, 176:0.2).

kingdom-of-heaven.name: reino de los cielos
kingdom-of-heaven.meaning: In Jesus' teaching, the spiritual rule of God that consists in recognizing God's sovereignty, believing in sonship with God, and having faith in the desire to do his will (140:10.9).

rejected.reason: Literal, but less natural; the plural is the ordinary Spanish phrase for this gospel term.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) a political kingdom or a place after death
rejected.reason: The reader must not bring these; the papers present a spiritual rule in human hearts.

kish.name: Kish
kish.meaning: A Mesopotamian city whose priest Sargon proclaimed himself king (78:8.8, 78:8.9).

kopet-dagh.name: Kopet Dag
kopet-dagh.meaning: A mountain range east of the southern end of the Caspian Sea; Adamson's center of the violet race was in its foothills (77:5.10).

rejected.reason: English transliteration; Spanish geography usually writes Kopet Dag.

korea.name: Corea
korea.meaning: The east Asian land where Buddhism became established and later merged with local practice (94:9.1, 94:11.1).

lake-van.name: lago Van
lake-van.meaning: The lake north of Mesopotamia where Van's followers and Adamson's descendants settled and from which Salem teachers went out to Europe and Asia (73:1.6, 93:7.2).

lanaforge.name: Lanaforge
lanaforge.meaning: The present System Sovereign of Satania, successor of Lucifer, the only primary Lanonandek in Nebadon who stayed loyal when his superior fell (45:2.2, 45:2.3).

lanonandek-sons.name: Hijos Lanonandek
lanonandek-sons.meaning: The third order of local universe Sons, created by the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit, who serve as System Sovereigns and Planetary Princes (35:8).

lao-tse.name: Lao-Tse
lao-tse.meaning: The Chinese teacher of the sixth century B.C. who envisioned more of God in Tao than Confucius did in humanity (92:5.12).

rejected.reason: Pinyin form; the papers use the older form Lao-tse.

laotta.name: Laotta
laotta.meaning: The brilliant Nodite woman, head of the Garden's western schools, whom Adam sought after Eve's default; she died giving birth to Sansa (75:5.2, 76:0.2).

lapland.name: Laponia
lapland.meaning: The northern European region where the older Andonites kept some semblance of identity (80:4.6).

lasea.name: Lasea
lasea.meaning: A port on Crete where Jesus, Gonod, and Ganid sailed from Alexandria (130:0.2, 130:4.12).

lazarus-of-bethany.name: Lázaro (de Betania)
lazarus-of-bethany.meaning: Jesus' friend at Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary, whom Jesus raised from the dead (Paper 168).

lemurs.name: lémures
lemurs.meaning: The lemur family whose early ancestors appeared in western North America and from whose types the dawn mammals came (61:2.10, 61:6.1).

rejected.reason: In Spanish 'lémures' is also the Roman spirits of the dead; the context must show the animal.

lesser-road.name: Camino Menor
lesser-road.meaning: The Hinayana division of southern Buddhism, which keeps Siddhartha's early asocial doctrine, as against the Mahayana 'Great Road' (94:9.5, 94:9.4, 94:12.2).

rejected.reason: A common rendering of Hinayana, but not what the English says; Greater Road is already Camino Mayor.
Adds a value judgment that 'lesser' does not need here.

levant.name: Levante
levant.meaning: The eastern Mediterranean lands (Syria, Palestine, Mesopotamian borders) into which Nodites and later Aryans moved (51:6.3, 78:1.4, 79:1.6).

rejected.reason: Wider region; changes the scope.

levant.note: In Spain 'Levante' also names the east of Spain and an east wind; use it with the article and capitals so context selects the eastern Mediterranean.

levites.name: levitas
levites.meaning: The hereditary temple servants of Judaism who officiated with the priests at the Jerusalem temple, chanted the Psalms, and joined in sending a delegation to John the Baptist (162:4.4, 135:6.6).

rejected.reason: The terms already done write peoples and religious groups in lowercase (fariseos, saduceos).

life-carrier-worlds.name: mundos de los Portadores de Vida
aliases: mundo de los Portadores de Vida
life-carrier-worlds.meaning: The fourth group of seven primary spheres of the Salvington circuit, overseen by the Melchizedeks and given to the study and conservation of life (36:2.1, 36:2.16, 36:6.3).

life-carriers.name: Portadores de Vida
life-carriers.meaning: Local universe Sons who design life, carry it to the planets, plant it, and foster its development (36:0.1).

rejected.reason: 'Transportador' reads as freight or a machine.
Correct, but the article makes it read less as a term; the English has no article.

light-and-life.name: luz y vida
light-and-life.meaning: The settled status of an inhabited world, the evolutionary goal of all mortal-inhabited worlds of the present age, reached after the Daynal Sons' missions (20:9.4, 36:1.4, 55:0.1).

rejected.reason: The hyphenated form is only an adjective in English; Spanish uses "de luz y vida".

livias.name: Livias
