livias.meaning: A town in southern Perea where Jesus' party camped before Jerusalem and where Simon Zelotes and Peter distributed swords (171:4.1, 165:0.1).

local-system-centers.name: centros de los sistemas locales
local-system-centers.meaning: The sixth order of Supreme Power Centers, one assigned permanently to each local system, who dispatch power circuits to the inhabited worlds and co-ordinate the physical controllers (29:2.18).

rejected.reason: "sistémico" reads as "systemic" (affecting a whole system), not "of a local system".

local-systems.name: sistemas locales
local-systems.meaning: Units of about one thousand inhabited worlds under a System Sovereign; Satania is Urantia's system (15:2.3, 32:2.11).

local-universe-centers.name: centros de los universos locales
local-universe-centers.meaning: The fourth order of Supreme Power Centers, stationed on local universe headquarters, which downstep superuniverse power for constellations and systems (29:2).

local-universe-mother-spirit-of-nebadon.name: Espíritu Madre del universo local de Nebadon
aliases: Espíritus Madre de los universos locales
local-universe-mother-spirit-of-nebadon.meaning: The Creative Spirit who is co-director with Michael of Nebadon, known as the Divine Minister of Salvington, whose personal influence is the Holy Spirit and who never leaves Salvington (34:4.7).
forcedChoices: feminine "Ministra Divina": The papers refer to the Mother Spirit as "she" (34:4.7).

local-universe-mother-spirits.name: Espíritus Madre de los universos locales
aliases: Espíritus Creativos de los Universos Locales
Espíritu Madre de un universo local
local-universe-mother-spirits.meaning: The individualized representation of the Infinite Spirit who joins each Creator Son to organize, create, and minister in a local universe; the adjutants are her children (34:0.1, 36:5.1).

rejected.reason: In Spanish a noun in apposition stays singular ('Espíritus Madre'), as in other compound names.
'Creador' is the translation of 'Creator' (Creator Sons); 'Creative' is a different English word, so it gets 'Creativo'.
The papers refer to the Mother Spirit as 'her'; the feminine 'Ministra' agrees.

local-universe-power-centers.name: centros de poder de los universos locales
local-universe-power-centers.meaning: Fourth-order Supreme Power Centers on local universe headquarters, which modify and distribute superuniverse power (29:2).

local-universe-sons-of-god.name: Hijos de Dios del Universo Local
local-universe-sons-of-god.meaning: The orders of divine sonship native to or serving in a local universe, such as Melchizedeks, Vorondadeks, and Lanonandeks (35:0).

local-universes.name: universos locales
local-universes.meaning: The creations of the Creator Sons, each of one hundred constellations of one hundred systems of inhabited worlds (32:0.1).

lord-s-prayer.name: Oración del Señor
lord-s-prayer.meaning: The prayer that Jesus first formed at fifteen for his family and later taught his apostles, which many came to call the Lord's Prayer (126:3.3, 144:3.15).

rejected.reason: The usual Spanish name, but it names the prayer by its first words; the English names it by its giver and quotes the name as a popular label (126:3.3). Kept as an alias.

lot.name: Lot
lot.meaning: Abraham's nephew, who went with him to Salem (93:5.5).

lucifer.name: Lucifer
lucifer.meaning: A primary Lanonandek Son, once System Sovereign of Satania, who led a rebellion against Michael and the Father (53:1).

rejected.reason: A traditional Spanish name with a folk-religious sense; the English uses "Lucifer".

lucifer-rebellion.name: rebelión de Lucifer
lucifer-rebellion.meaning: The revolt of Lucifer, System Sovereign of Satania, against the universe plan and the rule of Michael (53:0.1, 53:3.6).

luke.name: Lucas
luke.meaning: The physician of Antioch in Pisidia, a gentile convert of Paul, who wrote the Gospel by Luke and Acts (121:8.8).

lut.name: Lut
lut.meaning: The member of the Prince's staff who led the council of health and life, introducing sanitation and primitive hygiene (66:5.17, 66:5.21).

rejected.reason: A different person already in the glossary.

lutentia.name: Lutentia
lutentia.meaning: A rebel Lanonandek System Sovereign in Nebadon whom the Most Highs deposed and whom Michael replaced during his second bestowal (119:2.2, 119:2.4).

luz.name: Luz
luz.meaning: A place on the route from Caesarea-Philippi to the Phoenician coast; near it Jesus gave a great address on true religion (155:4.1, 155:4.2).

rejected.reason: Not a standard Spanish form.

luz.note: 'luz' is the common Spanish word for 'light'; the capital and a preposition ('cerca de Luz') must signal the place name.

lydda.name: Lida
lydda.meaning: A town on the route between Judea and Galilee through which Jesus passed on the return from Egypt and later on trips to Jerusalem (123:0.6, 127:6.4).

maccabees.name: Macabeos
maccabees.meaning: The Jewish family and movement of the Maccabean revolt, with which Mary's ancestors were identified; also the name of a book (122:5.10, 121:6.3).

macedonia.name: Macedonia
macedonia.meaning: The region north of Greece where Andrew and early missionaries proclaimed Jesus (139:1.12, 194:4.13).

machaerus-fortress-of.name: Maqueronte, fortaleza de
machaerus-fortress-of.meaning: Herod Antipas's fortress and residence in Perea, where John the Baptist was imprisoned until his execution (135:12.1, 135:12.4).

rejected.reason: A historical place has a standard Spanish form.

machiventa-melchizedek.name: Machiventa Melquisedec
machiventa-melchizedek.meaning: The Melchizedek Son who incarnated at Salem as an emergency bestowal, taught Abraham, and is now vicegerent Planetary Prince of Urantia (93:1.2, 93:9.11).

rejected.reason: The biblical name has a standard Spanish form, and 'Hijos Melquisedec' is already done.

madagascar.name: Madagascar
madagascar.meaning: The island off Africa where some tribes killed children born on unlucky days, and which the Andites did not reach (68:6.10, 78:5.5).

madon.name: Madón
madon.meaning: A Galilean town on Jesus' private tour and on the first preaching tour (134:7.5, 146:0.1).

rejected.reason: Spanish biblical usage writes the accent.

magadan-park.name: parque de Magadán
magadan-park.meaning: The park near Bethsaida-Julias where Jesus and the apostles camped and held conferences, and where the five thousand gathered (157:2.1, 152:2.4).

magdala.name: Magdala
magdala.meaning: The town by the Sea of Galilee where the women evangelists first worked and where Mary Magdalene was won for the kingdom (150:2.2).

magisterial-sons.name: Hijos Magistrales
magisterial-sons.meaning: The secondary Paradise Sons, offspring of the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit (Avonals), who judge dispensations on the worlds and also bestow themselves as mortals (20:1.11, 20:5.6, 20:6.5).

rejected.reason: 'Magisterial' in Spanish means of teachers or of a magistracy and is also a church term (magisterio); 'magistral' keeps the sense of authority and judgment.
Narrows them to judges and loses the adjective form of the English.

maine.name: Maine
maine.meaning: The U.S. state with Silurian volcanoes in the east, off whose coast icebergs slid into the Atlantic in the ice age (59:3.2, 61:5.8).

majeston.name: Majeston
majeston.meaning: The chief of reflectivity, personalized by a reaction of the Deity Absolute after the forty-ninth Reflective Spirit; the Paradise center of all reflectivity, where the mind of the Supreme focuses as a time-space experience (17:2.2, 0:3.14).

major-sectors.name: sectores mayores
major-sectors.meaning: About one tenth of a superuniverse: one hundred minor sectors and ten thousand local universes, ruled by three Perfections of Days (15:13.1).

malachi.name: Malaquías
malachi.meaning: The last Hebrew prophet before John; his promise of Elijah's return held John back (135:4.4, 97:0.2).

malaysia.name: Malasia
malaysia.meaning: The Malay lands and peoples: Mongoloid with much secondary Sangik blood; a Malay tribe claimed descent from the lemur (81:4.12, 74:8.5).

rejected.reason: Old colonial name; less known.

malaysia.note: The papers seen use only 'Malay' and 'Malayan'; in a sentence translators will mostly need 'malayo'. 'Malasia' names the modern state.

malta.name: Malta
malta.meaning: The Mediterranean island where Jesus talked with the discouraged young man Claudus on the way to Rome (130:8.1, 130:0.2).

maltese-cross.name: cruz de Malta
maltese-cross.meaning: The shape that a vertical cross section of total space slightly resembles, with horizontal arms for pervaded space and vertical arms for unpervaded space (11:7.3).

rejected.reason: Less usual; 'cruz de Malta' is the standard Spanish name.

malvorian.name: Malvorian
malvorian.meaning: The first of the Graduate Guides, who greeted the first mortal pilgrim in Havona and is now chief of their supreme council and director of their educational work (24:6.4, 24:6.6).

man-who-attacked-wife-at-tarentum.name: hombre que agredió a su esposa en Tarento
aliases: hombre que maltrataba a su esposa
man-who-attacked-wife-at-tarentum.meaning: A man at the Tarentum landing who mistreated his wife in public; Jesus took him aside kindly and he promised self-control (133:2.1).

mangus.name: Mangus
mangus.meaning: The Roman centurion at Capernaum who built the synagogue and asked Jesus to heal his servant (147:1.1, 147:1.3).

manotia.name: Manotia
manotia.meaning: A supreme seraphim who achieved all seven seraphic services, was second in command of the Satania seraphim in the Lucifer rebellion, and is now associate chief of seraphim on Urantia (39:0.9, 53:6.1).

mansant.name: Mansant
mansant.meaning: A great teacher after the Planetary Prince's fall who pointed people to 'The Great Light'; one of the twenty-four counselors (45:4.4, 64:6.29).

mansion-world-students.name: estudiantes de los mundos morada
mansion-world-students.meaning: All surviving mortals who reawaken on the mansion worlds, as one class of ascending mortals (30:4.14, 47:3.9).

mansion-world-teachers.name: Instructores de los Mundos Morada
mansion-world-teachers.meaning: Glorified cherubim and sanobim who, after the embrace of the Universe Mother Spirit, teach on the mansion worlds and higher educational spheres (48:5.2).

rejected.reason: 'Maestros' is already 'Master' (Hijos Maestros); 'Teacher' is 'Instructor' as in 'Hijos Instructores de la Trinidad'.

mansion-worlds.name: mundos morada
mansion-worlds.meaning: The seven satellites of the first transition world of Jerusem, where surviving mortals first reawaken; the name refers to Jesus' saying about 'many mansions in the Father's universe' (47:0.1, 30:4.14).

rejected.reason: Spanish 'mansión' means a luxurious house; the papers mean dwelling places, as in the saying of Jesus.
Same luxury sense, and longer.
Reads as a ranch or a short stay; loses the link to the saying.

mansions.name: moradas
mansions.meaning: The training worlds of mortal residence, of which Jesus said "In my Father's house are many mansions" (30:4.17, 47:0.1).

rejected.reason: Spanish "mansión" suggests a luxury house; "morada" also keeps the family with "mundos morada".

marduk.name: Marduk
marduk.meaning: A Babylonian god, one of the seven chief Mesopotamian deities, who perpetuated the Adam legend as a son-of-God link (92:5.6, 95:1.4, 95:1.10).

mars-planet.name: Marte (planeta)
mars-planet.meaning: Urantia's outer neighbor planet, whose thin atmosphere would class any inhabitants as subbreathers (49:2.13).

martha-sister-of-andrew-and-peter.name: Marta (hermana de Andrés y Pedro)
martha-sister-of-andrew-and-peter.meaning: The elder sister of Andrew and Peter, one of the ten women whom Jesus commissioned, who with Rachel helped win Mary Magdalene (150:1.1, 150:2.2).

rejected.form: Marta (hermana mayor de Andrés y Pedro)
rejected.reason: The English label does not include "elder"; the meaning field records it.

martha-sister-of-jesus.name: Marta (hermana de Jesús)
martha-sister-of-jesus.meaning: Jesus' second sister, born September 13 in A.D. 3, who became an expert weaver (124:1.7, 128:3.1).

martha-sister-of-lazarus.name: Marta (hermana de Lázaro)
martha-sister-of-lazarus.meaning: The sister of Lazarus and Mary of Bethany, later in Philadelphia with them (190:1.10).

martha-wife-of-justus.name: Marta (esposa de Justo)
martha-wife-of-justus.meaning: The wife of Justus in Corinth, with whom Jesus left two women to plan a new life (133:3.9).

mary-magdalene.name: María Magdalena
mary-magdalene.meaning: The woman of Magdala, leader among the women evangelists, first to see the risen Jesus (Papers 150, 189-190).

mary-mother-of-alpheus-twins.name: María (madre de los gemelos Alfeo)
aliases: María, la madre de los gemelos Alfeo
mary-mother-of-alpheus-twins.meaning: The mother of the Alpheus twins, one of the women who went to anoint Jesus' body (189:4.4, 191:0.11).

mary-mother-of-jesus.name: María (madre de Jesús)
mary-mother-of-jesus.meaning: Mary, the earthly mother of Jesus and wife of Joseph (122:1.2).

mary-sister-of-lazarus.name: María (hermana de Lázaro)
mary-sister-of-lazarus.meaning: The sister of Lazarus and Martha of Bethany, who went to Philadelphia with them (190:1.10).

mary-wife-of-clopas.name: María (esposa de Clopás)
aliases: María, la esposa de Clopás y hermana de la madre de Jesús
mary-wife-of-clopas.meaning: Sister of Jesus' mother, who stood near the cross and waited by the tomb (187:3.2, 188:1.7).

rejected.reason: Common in Spanish Bibles, but can merge Clopas with Cleopas, a different man in the papers.

master.name: Maestro
master.meaning: The title by which Jesus' associates called him, unbidden, as teacher and leader of his disciples (100:7.17, 141:3.5, 138:6.2).

rejected.reason: Translates "Lord", a different title in the text.
Means an owner of slaves or a boss, not a teacher; 138:6.2 pairs Master with pupils and disciples.

master.note: Same word as in "Espíritus Maestros" and "Hijos Maestros"; capital M and the article "el" mark the title of Jesus. The reader must not bring the sense of a schoolteacher or a master craftsman.

master-architects.name: Arquitectos Maestros
master-architects.meaning: The short name of the Architects of the Master Universe (31:9.1).

master-force-organizers.name: Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza
aliases: organizadores de la fuerza del Paraíso
master-force-organizers.meaning: Transcendental beings who work with space potency and organize the nebulae (29:5.1, 42:2.8).

master-mathematician.name: Matemático Maestro
master-mathematician.meaning: A phrase for the mind behind the mathematical order of the universe, used against materialism (195:6.8); the text does not name a specific being.

rejected.reason: breaks the 'master' family

master-michaels.name: Migueles Maestros
master-michaels.meaning: Creator Sons (Michaels) who, settled in supreme authority after their sevenfold bestowal, rule their universes with unlimited power derived from experienced association with the Paradise Trinity (21:0.3, 21:5.1).

rejected.reason: The name is already 'Miguel' in 'Miguel de Nebadon'; the family must keep one root.
Spanish puts the qualifier after the noun, as in 'Hijos Maestros'.

master-physical-controllers.name: Controladores Físicos Maestros
master-physical-controllers.meaning: The mobile subordinates of the Supreme Power Centers who control physical energies and travel fast through local space (29:4.1, 41:3.1).

rejected.reason: 'Maestro' before the noun reads as a teacher of controllers; after the noun it means principal, as in 'Espíritus Maestros'.

master-seraphim-of-planetary-supervision.name: serafines maestros de la supervisión planetaria
master-seraphim-of-planetary-supervision.meaning: Twelve corps of completion seraphim from Seraphington who supervise planetary affairs under the resident governor general (114:6.1, 39:9.2).

rejected.reason: breaks the 'master' family (Maestro)

master-sons.name: Hijos Maestros
master-sons.meaning: Creator Sons who completed their seven bestowals and so earned full sovereignty of their universe (21:4.6, 21:5.6).

rejected.reason: interprets; the English says 'Master'

master-spirit-number-five.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Cinco
master-spirit-number-five.meaning: The Master Spirit who blends the character of the Father and the Infinite Spirit (16:3.10).

master-spirit-number-four.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Cuatro
master-spirit-number-four.meaning: The Master Spirit who combines the natures of the Father and the Son (16:3.8).

master-spirit-number-one.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Uno
master-spirit-number-one.meaning: The Master Spirit who especially represents the Universal Father (16:3.2).

master-spirit-number-seven.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Siete
master-spirit-number-seven.meaning: The Master Spirit who represents the Father, Son, and Spirit together and speaks for the Supreme Being (16:3.15).

master-spirit-number-six.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Seis
master-spirit-number-six.meaning: The Master Spirit who portrays the combined character of the Son and the Spirit (16:3.12).

master-spirit-number-three.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Tres
master-spirit-number-three.meaning: The Master Spirit who especially resembles the Infinite Spirit (16:3.6).

master-spirit-number-two.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Dos
master-spirit-number-two.meaning: The Master Spirit who especially portrays the Eternal Son (16:3.4).

master-spirits-seven.name: Espíritus Maestros, Siete
master-spirits-seven.meaning: The seven primary personalities of the Infinite Spirit, one for each superuniverse, who represent all seven possible associations of the three Deities (16:0.1, 15:0.1).

rejected.reason: Adds the idea of governing; 'Master' here means primary or chief, which 'maestro' as an adjective carries (as in 'plan maestro').
Plain adjective; does not read as a term and breaks one word, one translation with Master Physical Controllers.

master-universe.name: universo maestro
master-universe.meaning: All of the creation in space: the grand universe plus the uninhabited but mobilizing universes of outer space (0:0.6, 12:1).

rejected.reason: Suggests one universe among others; loses the sense of the all-inclusive whole.
The reader must not bring the sense "teacher"; "maestro" follows "Espíritus Maestros" in the glossary.

masters-of-philosophy.name: maestros de filosofía
masters-of-philosophy.meaning: Primary supernaphim on Paradise, the "wise men of heaven", who teach philosophy and interpret the universe of universes to ascenders (27:6.2, 27:6.5, 28:5.11).

rejected.reason: Reads as an academic degree (a master's in philosophy).
Reads as ordinary school or university staff and breaks the family with "Maestro".

matadormus.name: Matadormus
matadormus.meaning: The rich young member of the Jerusalem Sanhedrin who asked Jesus for ordination and about eternal life (163:2.4).

material-sons.name: Hijos Materiales
material-sons.meaning: The order of Sons sent in pairs, as Adam and Eve, to uplift the races of an evolutionary world biologically (51:0.1).

matthew-levi.name: Mateo Leví
matthew-levi.meaning: Matthew Levi, the seventh apostle, a former customs collector of Capernaum and the apostolic treasurer (139:7.1).

matthias.name: Matías
matthias.meaning: The man chosen by lot to take the place of Judas among the apostles, who became their treasurer but had little part in later work (193:6.3, 192:0.2).

may-day.name: fiesta del primero de mayo
may-day.meaning: An old festival day when sex regulations were suspended; its rites were imitative magic aimed at the plant world (82:2.4, 88:6.4).

rejected.reason: Most readers take it as Labor Day.
Not a natural Spanish name.

meanings.name: significados
meanings.meaning: The "mind meanings" of reality, the understanding that mind adds to perception of things, set between things (energy) and values (spirit) (0:0.3, 0:1.1, 0:4.10).

rejected.reason: Also the five senses and directions; ambiguous.
Heavier "-ción" noun with no gain.

mechanical-controllers.name: controladores mecánicos
mechanical-controllers.meaning: The most powerful Master Physical Controllers on inhabited worlds, with a living antigravity endowment; ten on Urantia help seraphic transports depart (29:4.19).

mediterranean-region.name: región mediterránea
mediterranean-region.meaning: The region around the Mediterranean Sea, where races from the north, south, and east met and mixed.

mediterranean-sea.name: mar Mediterráneo
mediterranean-sea.meaning: The sea that became one with the Atlantic when an earthquake broke the Gibraltar isthmus, causing the greatest loss of life by flood in history (80:2.4).

megiddo.name: Meguido
megiddo.meaning: The international battlefield of Palestine, where Jesus recalled the victories and defeats of his people (127:6.4, 126:1.2, 123:1.7).

rejected.reason: Also used; 'Meguido' keeps the hard 'g' sound for a reader of Spanish.
A different, apocalyptic name.

mek.name: Mek
mek.meaning: Leader of the Prince's council on art and science, who improved industry and the art of the blue man (66:5.23, 66:5.26).

melchizedek-brotherhood.name: hermandad de Melquisedec
melchizedek-brotherhood.meaning: The group of believers in one God that Machiventa Melchizedek founded at Salem (93).

rejected.reason: 'Fraternidad' is used for 'brotherhood' as a quality (the brotherhood of man); 'hermandad' fits an organized body.
Ordinary sense is a Catholic lay confraternity.

forcedChoices: 'de Melquisedec' (person) rather than invariable 'Melquisedec' (order): The context is the Salem group of Machiventa.

melchizedek-college-of-administration.name: Colegio Melquisedec de Administración
melchizedek-college-of-administration.meaning: The school on Jerusem from which representatives and electors must graduate before they serve in system government (45:7).

rejected.reason: Acceptable; 'Colegio' keeps the English word, but in some countries it means a secondary school.

melchizedek-college-of-spiritual-endowme.name: Colegio Melquisedec de Dotación Espiritual
melchizedek-college-of-spiritual-endowme.meaning: A school of the Melchizedek University where Sons of God and seraphim train evangels of spiritual liberty and divine sonship.

rejected.reason: 'Dones' suggests charismatic gifts; 'endowment' is an endowing.

melchizedek-father.name: Melquisedec, Padre
melchizedek-father.meaning: The index form of Father Melchizedek, the first Melchizedek of Nebadon (93:1.2).

melchizedek-manovandet.name: Melquisedec, Manovandet
melchizedek-manovandet.meaning: A Melchizedek once attached to the receivership of Urantia, who presented Paper 53.

melchizedek-mantutia.name: Melquisedec, Mantutia
melchizedek-mantutia.meaning: The Melchizedek who directed the commission that presented Parts II and III and supervised the restatement in Paper 120.

melchizedek-receivers.name: síndicos Melquisedec
melchizedek-receivers.meaning: The twelve Melchizedeks who administered Urantia as custodians in trust after the Caligastia rebellion, until Michael's bestowal (67:6.5, 93:1.2, 93:9.11).

rejected.reason: False friend: 'receptor' means one who receives.
Loses the legal sense of receivership (custody of a forfeited estate).
Means holders of a deposit; weak sense of governing.

forcedChoices: 'síndicos': It carries the legal sense of receivership, but in some countries it also means a town official or a building manager; a human must confirm.

melchizedek-sons.name: Hijos Melquisedec
melchizedek-sons.meaning: An order of local universe Sons who serve as teachers, advisers, and emergency ministers; Machiventa Melchizedek of Salem was one of them (35:0.1, 49:0.1, 45:6.8).

rejected.reason: The name also belongs to the Melchizedek of Genesis, so the standard Spanish spelling 'Melquisedec' applies (rule for historical names). Reviewer can check this choice.
'de' makes them the children of one person; the name is the name of the order.

melchizedek-sphere.name: esfera Melquisedec
melchizedek-sphere.meaning: The pilot world of the Salvington circuit, headquarters of the Melchizedeks and site of Michael's first bestowal.

rejected.reason: Suggests one person; the English names the order.

melchizedek-university.name: Universidad Melquisedec
melchizedek-university.meaning: The training system of 490 worlds in the Salvington circuit where ascending mortals prepare for residence on Salvington.

melchizedek-worlds.name: mundos Melquisedec
melchizedek-worlds.meaning: The 490 worlds of the Salvington circuit that make up the Melchizedek University.

memories-of-mercy.name: Memorias de la Misericordia
memories-of-mercy.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim who are the living record of the mercy shown to each person, read in the courts of Uversa, and who teach ascenders to be truly merciful (28:6.6, 28:6.8).

rejected.reason: "recuerdo" is a single memory or a keepsake; the order is a living record.

memories-of-mercy.note: Plural "memorias" can also mean memoirs or a written report. The sense of a living record must come from the context.

merchant-of-damascus.name: mercader de Damasco
merchant-of-damascus.meaning: A wealthy part-Jewish merchant with caravans throughout the Roman world who befriended Jesus and later proposed that he head a school of religious philosophy at Damascus (128:3.3, 128:4.1).

rejected.reason: Also correct; "mercader" fits the period and the caravan trade.

mercury.name: Mercurio
mercury.meaning: The inner planet of the solar system, slowed by tidal friction until one face always turns to the sun (42:7.2, 57:6.2).

mesopotamia.name: Mesopotamia
mesopotamia.meaning: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, the site of the second garden and of the Andite civilization (76:0.1, 78:1.1).

mesozoic.name: Mesozoico
mesozoic.meaning: The early land-life era of one hundred million years, ending with the Cretaceous (59:0.5, 60:4.6).

messenger-corps-david-zebedee-s.name: cuerpo de mensajeros (de David Zebedeo)
messenger-corps-david-zebedee-s.meaning: The group of runners organized by David Zebedee who carried news between Jesus, the apostles, and the believers, and who later helped him run the camps (163:5.2, 163:5.3).

rejected.reason: 'mensajería' suggests a courier company.

messenger-hosts-of-space.name: Huestes Mensajeras del Espacio
messenger-hosts-of-space.meaning: The intermediate group of the family of the Infinite Spirit, linking the higher personalities with the ministering spirits (25:0.1, 26:1.1, 37:5.8).

rejected.reason: Heavier; 'messenger' here works as a modifier.

messiah.name: Mesías
messiah.meaning: The anointed deliverer that the Jews expected, a hope that Jesus did not fulfill in the temporal sense (136:1.1).

messina.name: Mesina
messina.meaning: The Sicilian port where Jesus stopped one day and spoke to a young fruit vendor (130:0.2, 130:8.3).

mexico.name: México
mexico.meaning: The region of North America where an amalgamated, mainly red, race founded one of three civilizations, and where great crustal changes took place (64:7.5, 60:3.6).

rejected.reason: Old spelling; México is the standard form.

michael-memorial-on-1st-mansion-world.name: monumento a Miguel (en el primer mundo morada)
michael-memorial-on-1st-mansion-world.meaning: A material-morontia structure in the court of the resurrection halls of the first mansion world, sealed by Gabriel, which commemorates the mortal transit of Jesus on Urantia (188:3.11, 189:1.9).

rejected.reason: Spanish 'memorial' first means a written petition or a notebook; the monument sense is secondary.
Correct but long for a name used in quotes.

michael-memorial-on-1st-mansion-world.note: The papers call the Jerusem temple and this structure by the same name. The Spanish uses one form for both.

michael-memorial-on-jerusem.name: monumento a Miguel (en Jerusem)
michael-memorial-on-jerusem.meaning: A temple at the center of the circular reservations of the Sons on Jerusem, completed some five hundred years ago, now the center of the system management changed by Michael's bestowal, with a staff of over one million (46:5.19).

rejected.reason: Spanish 'memorial' first means a written petition; the papers call it a temple.

michael-of-nebadon.name: Miguel de Nebadon
michael-of-nebadon.meaning: The Creator Son of the order of Michael who made and rules the local universe of Nebadon and who lived on Urantia as Jesus (35:0.1, 194:2.4).

rejected.reason: 'Miguel' brings in the archangel of tradition and a common personal name; the papers use Michael as the name of an order of Creator Sons, so the name is kept like the other names of this book.
replaced by a human decision

decision.note: "Miguel" is the standard Spanish form of the name, as with Jesús, Juan, and Melquisedec
"Miguel" is the standard Spanish form of the name, as with Jesús, Juan, and Melquisedec

michael-sons.name: Hijos Miguel
michael-sons.meaning: The Creator Sons of the order of Michael, the primary Paradise Sons who make the sevenfold bestowal (34:3.5, 20:5.2, 26:8.1).

rejected.reason: Reads as children of a person named Miguel; the name is an order, as in 'Hijos Melquisedec'.

michael-the-original.name: Miguel (el original)
michael-the-original.meaning: The first-born Creator Son, who made a bestowal on the seven Havona circuits and presides over the primary Paradise Sons when they assemble in conference (7:5.8, 7:5.9, 21:0.5).

rejected.reason: Reads as a regnal number (Miguel I); the papers say 'original' and 'first-born'.

midianites.name: madianitas
midianites.meaning: An ancient people raided by the Hebrews and who invaded the Jordan region in Gideon's day (70:1.15, 124:6.6).

midsonite-world.name: mundo midsonitario
midsonite-world.meaning: The special sphere of each local system where midsonite parental groups live and where Material Sons and Daughters can go to receive Adjusters (45:6.9, 55:4.27).

rejected.reason: The glossary root is 'midsonitario' (midsoniters: midsonitarios).

midsoniters.name: midsonitarios
midsoniters.meaning: Beings born of Melchizedek Life Carriers and Material Daughters who are neither clearly mortal nor immortal, never die, and gather on a finaliter world for a purpose not yet revealed (36:4.4, 36:4.8, 55:8.4).

rejected.reason: The English pairs midsoniter (noun) with midsonite (adjective), like absoniter/absonite; the done list gives absoniters = absonitarios, absonite = absonito. So the noun takes -itario and the adjective keeps -ita.
Explains instead of naming, and collides with 'seres intermedios' (midwayers).

midsoniters.note: The adjective 'midsonita' (midsonite creatures, midsonite sphere) and the noun 'midsonitarios' follow the absonito/absonitarios pattern. A reviewer can confirm that pattern.

midspace-zones.name: zonas del espacio intermedio
aliases: zonas de quiescencia del espacio intermedio
zona del espacio de relativa quietud
midspace-zones.meaning: Relatively quiet elliptical regions of quiescent space activity that separate the successive space levels and separate pervaded from unpervaded space; near Paradise they are the transition zones from time to eternity (11:7.3, 11:7.7, 12:5.4).

rejected.reason: Not a natural Spanish word.

rejected.form: zonas intermedias (alone as the main name)
rejected.reason: Too general; 'intermedio' is also in 'seres intermedios' (midwayers), so the word 'espacio' must stay.

midway-messengers.name: mensajeros intermedios
midway-messengers.meaning: A small named group of the United Midwayers who give quick and reliable personal communication service on an evolutionary world (77:8.6).

rejected.reason: Reads as messengers who serve the midwayers, not midwayers who are messengers.
'intermediario' adds a go-between sense.

midwayers.name: seres intermedios
midwayers.meaning: Beings who live on a level about midway between mortals and the angelic orders, hence called midway creatures (77:0.1).

rejected.reason: As a noun, 'intermedio' is an intermission.
Means a go-between or middleman; the papers mean a level of life, not a role.
Means a mediator or party wall; changes the idea.

midwayers-chief-of-urantia.name: jefe de los seres intermedios de Urantia
aliases: Jefe de los Seres Intermedios de Urantia
midwayers-chief-of-urantia.meaning: The leader of the midwayers of Urantia, who presented Paper 91 on prayer (91:9.9, 77:8.1).

rejected.reason: Reads as a middle-rank chief, not the chief of the midwayers.

forcedChoices: masculine 'jefe' with 'los seres': Spanish needs a gender; the English uses no gender here, and the masculine plural is the generic form.

midwayers-primary.name: seres intermedios primarios
midwayers-primary.meaning: The first order of midway creatures, derived from the corporeal staff of the Planetary Prince, nearer to angels in nature, who serve as the planetary intelligence corps (38:9.9, 38:9.10, 77:1).

rejected.reason: Go-between sense; see secondary midwayers.

midwayers-secondary.name: seres intermedios secundarios
midwayers-secondary.meaning: The second order of midway creatures, descended from the Adamic line, nearer to mortals in nature, who bridge the gap between mortal man and the primary midwayers (38:9.9, 38:9.10, 77:4).

rejected.reason: 'intermediario' is a go-between or a broker; the term names beings on a level between two levels, not agents who mediate.
'mediano' means of medium size or mediocre.

mighty-messengers.name: Mensajeros Poderosos
mighty-messengers.meaning: Trinity-embraced ascendant mortals, tested in rebellion, who serve in superuniverse administration (22:2.1).

rejected.reason: preposed adjective reads as praise, not as a name

milcha.name: Milca
milcha.meaning: A cousin of the Apostle Thomas, one of the ten women Jesus commissioned for ministry (150:1.1).

rejected.reason: Spanish 'ch' gives a wrong sound.

milcha.note: A Hebrew name, so hispanicized like Juana and Rebeca; confirm the policy.

milky-way-galaxy.name: galaxia de la Vía Láctea
milky-way-galaxy.meaning: The vast starry system that the papers call the central nucleus of the superuniverse of Orvonton (15:3.1, 15:3.2).

mind.name: mente
mind.meaning: All that responds to the mind circuit of the Conjoint Actor, an attribute of the Infinite Spirit; in personality it always intervenes between spirit and matter (0:6.1, 0:6.8).

rejected.reason: Narrower: only the reasoning faculty; the papers use mind for all levels of intelligence.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) the brain or the psyche alone
rejected.reason: The reader must not bring this; mind is a cosmic endowment of the Infinite Spirit.

mind-energy-manipulators.name: manipuladores de energía mental
mind-energy-manipulators.meaning: Celestial artisans expert in communication between morontia beings and other intelligent beings, and students of the mind circuits of the Infinite Spirit.

rejected.form: manipuladores de la energía de la mente
rejected.reason: Long; 'manipuladores de energía espiritual' sets the pattern noun + adjective.
The reader must not bring this; the sense is a skilled handler.

mind-personalities.name: personalidades de mente
mind-personalities.meaning: Unrevealed orders of beings dominated by mind but always associated with spirit, of which Majeston and his associates are an illustration (30:1.113).

rejected.reason: 'Mental' can suggest a psychological type or a mental illness.

mind-planners.name: planificadores de la mente
mind-planners.meaning: Seraphim on the mansion worlds who study the souls in transit and group them for assignment and advancement, helping survivors use morontia mind (48:6.25, 39:2.6).

rejected.reason: Reads as people who plan in their heads.
Suggests they design minds; 48:6.25 says they study and group, and do not manipulate.

mindal-and-physical-energy-personalities.name: personalidades de energía mental y física
aliases: personalidades de energía mental y de energía física
mindal-and-physical-energy-personalities.meaning: Unrevealed creatures that do not respond to spirit gravity but are true personalities within the Father's circuit (30:1.113).

rejected.reason: Drops 'energy', which is the point of the term.

forcedChoices: 'mental' for 'mindal': Spanish has no separate adjective; 'mental' is the adjective of 'mente'.

minor-sectors.name: sectores menores
minor-sectors.meaning: A division of a superuniverse of one hundred local universes, ruled by three Recents of Days and mainly concerned with physical problems (15:2.6, 18:5.4).

miriam-sister-of-jesus.name: Miriam (hermana de Jesús)
miriam-sister-of-jesus.meaning: The eldest daughter of Joseph and Mary, sister of Jesus, who later married Jacob the stone mason (127:5.1, 128:5.8).

rejected.reason: Would merge her with Mary her mother and other Marys in the text.

mississippi-river.name: río Misisipi
mississippi-river.meaning: The North American river and its valley, used as a geologic reference line (59:3.9, 59:5.20).

rejected.reason: The RAE recommends the adapted spelling Misisipi; both are understood.

mithraism.name: mitraísmo
mithraism.meaning: The greatest of the mystery cults, the worship of Mithras, spread over the Roman Empire by legions recruited in the Levant (98:5.1).

mohammed.name: Mahoma
mohammed.meaning: The founder of Islam in the sixth century after Christ, whose return his followers expect (92:5.14, 92:5.6).

rejected.reason: Common, but Mahoma is the standard Spanish historical form.

monmatia.name: Monmatia
monmatia.meaning: The name of Urantia's solar system (57:5).

monotheism.name: monoteísmo
monotheism.meaning: The belief in one God, as taught by Moses and held by the Hebrews and the Muslims (92:5.11, 104:1.9).

moon-urantia-s.name: luna (de Urantia)
moon-urantia-s.meaning: The satellite of Urantia, which in the far future will come near the earth and break into particles that form rings or fall as meteors (57:6.3).

morality.name: moralidad
morality.meaning: The recognition of duty and of right and wrong, a superanimal but subspiritual level of mind that prepares for religious experience.

rejected.reason: As a noun it also means morale (spirit of a group); kept only as an adjective alias.

morontia.name: morontia
morontia.meaning: The level of reality between the material and the spiritual, the substance of the soul and of the ascension life in the local universe (0:5.10, 103:6.7).

rejected.reason: Describes rather than names, and implies half spirit, which the papers do not say.

morontia-cherubim.name: querubines morontiales
morontia-cherubim.meaning: The 'fourth creatures' among cherubim and sanobim, who keep quasi-material traits and serve on the morontia training worlds (38:7.7, 38:8.4, 48:3.4).

morontia-companions.name: Compañeros Morontiales
morontia-companions.meaning: Beings of the local universe who act as hosts, guides, teachers of language, and interpreters for ascenders on the morontia worlds (48:3.4, 48:3.13).

morontia-counselors.name: consejeros morontiales
morontia-counselors.meaning: The seraphic transition ministers who teach mota on the mansion worlds to bring material and morontial viewpoints into focus (48:6.28).

rejected.reason: 'Asesor' reads as a technical adviser; also matches 'Consejeros Divinos'.

morontia-planners.name: planificadores morontiales
morontia-planners.meaning: Divine Builders among the celestial artisans who build for the co-ordinate association of all personalities present on a sphere (44:3.7).

rejected.reason: 'Planeador' means a glider.

morontia-power-supervisors.name: Supervisores del Poder Morontial
morontia-power-supervisors.meaning: Local universe beings who unite material and spiritual energies to organize morontia forms and supply the 570 successive morontia bodies of an ascender (48:1.5, 42:12.11).

rejected.reason: 'Power' is 'poder' in all terms (Directores Supremos del Poder).
Makes the supervisors morontial; the English qualifies the power.

forcedChoices: 'Morontia Power Supervisors' can read as 'supervisors of morontia power' or 'morontia supervisors of power'; the papers show they supervise morontia energy work (48:1.5), so 'morontial' qualifies 'Poder'.

morontia-progressors.name: progresores morontiales
morontia-progressors.meaning: Ascending mortals who move through the morontia worlds of the local universe between the mansion worlds and spirit status (48:6.28, 43:8.12).

rejected.reason: 'Progresista' is a political sense.
Long, and loses the coined agent noun.

forcedChoices: adjective 'morontial' for the attributive 'morontia': Spanish needs an adjective; the English itself uses 'morontial' (0:5.10).

morontia-recorders.name: registradores morontiales
morontia-recorders.meaning: Celestial artisans who preserve the scenes of morontia life as group records for the morontia halls of records (44).

rejected.reason: 'Grabador' can mean an engraver or a tape recorder.

morontia-synthesizers.name: sintetizadores morontiales
morontia-synthesizers.meaning: Master artisans who add the finishing touches to morontia ensembles of beauty (44).

rejected.reason: Loses the English coinage.

forcedChoices: 'sintetizadores': The reader must not bring the ordinary sense of an electronic music instrument.

morontia-temple.name: templo morontial
morontia-temple.meaning: The structure that appears on a planet entering light and life, used for planetary ceremonies and the translation of living mortals.

morontia-world.name: Mundo Morontial
morontia-world.meaning: The second transitional culture world of a system capital such as Jerusem, headquarters of the supervisors of morontia life (45:1).
forcedChoices: capitalize for the specific world: In lowercase it is the same form as the general singular of 'morontia worlds'; capitals keep them apart, as the English alias does.

morontia-world-transition-ministers.name: ministros de transición de los mundos morontiales
morontia-world-transition-ministers.meaning: The sixth order of seraphim, who help mortals pass from the life in the flesh into morontia existence on the mansion worlds (48:6.1).

rejected.reason: Shifts 'morontia' from the worlds to the ministers.

morontia-worlds.name: mundos morontiales
morontia-worlds.meaning: The transition worlds of the local universe, from the mansion worlds to the universe headquarters, where ascending mortals live the morontia life (48:6.1, 47:5.3).

rejected.reason: Acceptable, but the adjective reads more naturally and matches the family.

morontians.name: morontianos
morontians.meaning: Morontia beings, in context ascending mortals in the morontia stage, as on the Edentia training worlds (43:8.5, 43:8.12).

mortal-corps-of-the-finality.name: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios Mortales
mortal-corps-of-the-finality.meaning: The corps into which Father-fused mortals are mustered on reaching Paradise; only they take the finaliter oath (30:4.31, 31:3.3).

rejected.reason: Follows the English order, but 'cuerpo mortal' is the ordinary Spanish for 'the mortal body'.
Same 'mortal body' reading, and breaks the done form for 'Corps of the Finality'.

mortal-corps-of-the-finality.note: The form is close to the done 'Corps of Mortal Finaliters: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Mortales'. The two English names appear to refer to the same corps; a reviewer must confirm that.

mortal-mind.name: mente mortal
mortal-mind.meaning: The mind of evolutionary human beings, in whose superconscious levels the Thought Adjuster works and religious growth occurs (100:1.9, 91:2.6).

rejected.reason: 'Mind' is 'mente' in all terms; 'intellect' is a separate English word.

mortals.name: mortales
mortals.meaning: Will creatures of animal origin on the evolutionary worlds, the lowest order of personal creation, able to survive and ascend to Paradise (49:0.1, 107:0.2).

moses.name: Moisés
moses.meaning: Moses, the Hebrew leader and teacher who led the Hebrews out of Egypt and taught the worship of one God (96:3.1).

most-high.name: Altísimo
most-high.meaning: A Semitic title for Deity in scripture; the papers note that in Urantia records it can refer to the Most High Fathers of the constellation or to God (43:3.4, 4:1.4).
most-high.note: The papers state that the referent of 'Most High' is often unclear; keep it open, do not resolve it in translation.

most-high-assistants.name: Asistentes Altísimos
most-high-assistants.meaning: A corps of high spirits from outside the local universe who assist the Paradise personalities of Nebadon with advanced plans and rulings (37:4.5, 37:8.10).

rejected.reason: Decides that they assist the Most Highs; the papers say they assist Paradise personalities (37:4.5).
Collides with the 'Supreme' terms.

most-high-assistants.note: 'Most High' can be a rank adjective or a link to the Most Highs; the English does not decide. The chosen form keeps both readings.

most-high-observer-of-urantia.name: observador Altísimo de Urantia
most-high-observer-of-urantia.meaning: The Vorondadek Son resident on Urantia as observer for the Most Highs and trustee of planetary sovereignty, the twenty-third to serve, who can act as regent in a crisis (114:4.1, 114:4.4, 43:5.17).

rejected.reason: With the adjective first, "altísimo" reads as "very high", not as the title of the Most Highs.

most-high-observer-of-urantia.note: "Altísimo" after the noun works as a title, but a reader can still take it as an ordinary adjective.

most-high-observers.name: observadores Altísimos
most-high-observers.meaning: Vorondadek Sons stationed as observers on isolated worlds, who can take absolute authority as Most High regents in an emergency (35:5.6, 43:5.17, 114:4.4).
most-high-observers.note: Same problem as the singular: "Altísimos" must read as the title, not as "very high".

most-highs.name: Altísimos
most-highs.meaning: Vorondadek Sons who rule a constellation in a group of three, the senior one acting as Constellation Father (43:5, 67:6.5).

rejected.reason: Reads as a comparison ('taller ones'), not a title.

most-highs-of-norlatiadek.name: Altísimos de Norlatiadek
most-highs-of-norlatiadek.meaning: The three Vorondadek Sons who rule the constellation of Norlatiadek from Edentia (43:0.2, 67:6.5).

most-holy-sphere.name: Esfera Santísima
most-holy-sphere.meaning: The region of upper Paradise immediately around the Deity presence, reserved for worship, trinitization, and high spiritual attainment, with no material structures (11:3.1, 13:2.4).

rejected.reason: Awkward in Spanish.
'el Santísimo' in common use means the Eucharist, a sense the authors do not intend.

most-holy-sphere.note: 'Santísima' can recall 'Santísima Trinidad' for a Catholic reader; a reviewer can check the effect.

mota.name: mota
mota.meaning: Morontia wisdom, a supermaterial sensitivity to reality that reconciles science and religion, with knowledge-reason for substance and faith-insight for essence (103:6.7, 48:6.28, 45:7.6).

rejected.reason: A gloss, not the coined term; usable as an explanation.

forcedChoices: keep the coined name 'mota': Rule 3 keeps names that exist only in the book, but Spanish 'mota' means a speck or a fluff, and in Mexico it is slang for marijuana; a human must decide if a mark (italics) is needed.

mother-cult.name: culto de la madre
mother-cult.meaning: The ancient cult of the descendants of Cain that glorified Eve as the 'great mother'; it dominated the Mediterranean world, and its priests taught physical suffering (80:7.7, 89:3.4, 98:1.3).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'motherly worship', a manner of worship, not worship of a mother figure.
Clear, but breaks the pattern of the done term 'culto de la Madre de Dios'.

mother-cult.note: 'de la madre' can also read as a cult that belongs to a mother; context removes it.

mother-of-god-cult.name: culto de la Madre de Dios
aliases: secta de la Madre de Dios
mother-of-god-cult.meaning: A cult in Mexico and elsewhere that used a sacrament of cakes and wine in place of human sacrifice (89:9.2); related to the temples of the Great Mother (98:5.5).
mother-of-god-cult.note: 'Madre de Dios' is a common Catholic title for Mary. The English has the same echo, so the form keeps it; the translator must not add or remove a link to Mary.

mother-spirits.name: Espíritus Madre
mother-spirits.meaning: The local universe Mother Spirits, consorts of the Creator Sons (Paper 34).

rejected.reason: Breaks the fixed form 'Espíritus Madre de los universos locales'.

mount-ararat.name: monte Ararat
mount-ararat.meaning: The sacred mountain of northern Mesopotamia where Vanites said their seven commandments were given to Van (77:4.11, 77:4.12).

mount-assembly.name: Monte de la Asamblea
mount-assembly.meaning: The most holy mount on Edentia, residence of the Faithful of Days, where ascending mortals gather (43:4.1, 43:4.5, 43:4.6).

mount-carmel.name: monte Carmelo
mount-carmel.meaning: The long ridge in northwest Palestine running down to the sea, linked with Elijah's story against the priests of Baal (123:5.12, 128:3.2).

mount-gerizim.name: monte Gerizim
mount-gerizim.meaning: The mountain in Samaria where the Samaritans built a temple to Yahweh that John Hyrcanus destroyed (143:4.2).

rejected.reason: Older spelling, less common now.

mount-hermon.name: monte Hermón
mount-hermon.meaning: The mountain where Jesus endured his great temptation and defeated Caligastia before his baptism (136:3.1).

mount-olivet.name: monte de los Olivos
mount-olivet.meaning: The mount east of Jerusalem on whose slope lay the Gethsemane camp.

mount-sartaba.name: monte Sartaba
mount-sartaba.meaning: The highest mountain over the Jordan valley, crowned by the Alexandrian fortress where Herod imprisoned a wife and buried two strangled sons (124:6.6, 122:7.6).

mount-seraph.name: Monte Serafín
mount-seraph.meaning: The highest elevation on Jerusem, the point of departure for all transport seraphim (46:2.8).

rejected.reason: 'seraph' is an English common noun with a Spanish equivalent; the family stays visible as 'serafín'

mount-sinai.name: monte Sinaí
mount-sinai.meaning: The volcano (Mount Horeb) associated with Yahweh by the southern tribes, and a source of iron ore (96:1.3, 80:6.3).

mount-tabor.name: monte Tabor
mount-tabor.meaning: The mountain range east of Nazareth whose summit Jesus first climbed with Joseph at nine (122:6.1, 124:1.6).

mystery-monitors.name: Monitores de Misterio
mystery-monitors.meaning: Another name of the Thought Adjusters, the divine fragments of the Father that indwell mortal minds (Paper 107).

rejected.reason: Makes 'mystery' an adjective of character (secretive).
'Vigilante' is a security guard; it loses the advising sense of 'monitor'.
The reader must not bring the screen or the camp-instructor sense; it means one who watches and admonishes.

mysticism.name: misticismo
mysticism.meaning: The practice of seeking consciousness of God by withdrawal and inner communion, which can be genuine spiritual communion but can also become a technique of reality avoidance (100:5.8, 100:5.10).

rejected.reason: As a noun it often names a body of religious literature or a 'mystique'; kept only as an adjective alias.

nabon.name: Nabon
nabon.meaning: A Greek Jew, high priest of the Mithraic cult in Rome, influenced by Jesus' talk on truth and faith (132:3.1, 132:3.11).

naboths.name: los Nabot
naboths.meaning: Naboth and his sons, executed in Ahab's intrigue to take their land; Elijah denounced the murder (97:9.19).
forcedChoices: Spanish does not pluralize a surname: 'los Nabot' for 'the Naboths'.

nahor-old-testament.name: Nacor (Antiguo Testamento)
nahor-old-testament.meaning: Abraham's brother, who did not wholly accept the Melchizedek gospel, stayed behind, and built a city-state that bore his name (93:5.5).

rejected.reason: Also a standard Spanish form; both exist in Spanish Bibles. Chose the older, more widespread one.

nahor-old-testament.note: Distinct from Nahor the Jerusalem teacher who visited Jesus (123:6.8). A reviewer can confirm Nacor against Najor.

nahor-rabbi.name: Nacor (rabino)
nahor-rabbi.meaning: A teacher in a Jerusalem rabbinical academy who came to observe Jesus at Nazareth and proposed taking him to Jerusalem (123:6.8, 123:6.9).
nahor-rabbi.note: Another Nahor, a young evangelist, appears at 150:9.3; keep them separate.

nain.name: Naín
nain.meaning: A hill town of southern Galilee where Joseph worked and where Jesus restored the widow's son, who was not really dead (122:6.1, 123:3.8, 146:6.2).

rejected.reason: The standard Spanish form carries the accent.

nalda.name: Nalda
nalda.meaning: The woman of Sychar at Jacob's well to whom Jesus offered the living water (143:5.2, 143:5.4).

naples.name: Nápoles
naples.meaning: The Italian port city where Jesus, Gonod, and Ganid stayed on the way to Rome (130:0.2, 130:8.4).

nasanta.name: Nasanta
nasanta.meaning: Daughter of Elman the Syrian physician, one of the ten women commissioned by Jesus (150:1.1).

nathan-of-caesarea.name: Natán de Cesarea
nathan-of-caesarea.meaning: A Greek Jew from Caesarea, associate of the apostle John, who wrote the Gospel of John under John's direction (121:8.10).

nathan-of-cana.name: Natán de Caná
nathan-of-cana.meaning: The father of Johab, the bridegroom at the Cana wedding (137:3.6).

nathan-of-nazareth.name: Natán de Nazaret
nathan-of-nazareth.meaning: A Nazareth potter by the spring who befriended young Jesus and Jacob and gave them clay (123:5.15).

nathaniel-apostle.name: Natanael (apóstol)
nathaniel-apostle.meaning: Nathaniel of Cana, the sixth apostle, brought to Jesus by Philip (139:6.1).

national-council-of-defense.name: Consejo Nacional de Defensa
national-council-of-defense.meaning: On a neighboring planet, the council of twenty-five members that commissions 'guardians of civilization' and in war can assess the states for money, men, and materials (72:11.1, 72:7.7).

nazareth.name: Nazaret
nazareth.meaning: The town in Galilee where Jesus grew up (Papers 122-126).

nazarites.name: nazareos
nazarites.meaning: A brotherhood with headquarters at Engedi whose life vows were to abstain from intoxicating drink, let the hair grow, and not touch the dead (135:1.1, 135:1.2).

rejected.reason: Means people from Nazareth or followers of Jesus.

neanderthalers.name: neandertales
neanderthalers.meaning: The people descended from the improved Badonite stock who spread from northwest India to France, China, and northern Africa and dominated the world for almost half a million years (64:3.5, 64:4.1, 64:4.2).

rejected.reason: Not natural Spanish; 'neandertal' is the common form.

neanderthalers.note: A reviewer can decide between lowercase 'neandertales' and a capital, for consistency with 'Andonitas' and 'Noditas'.
forcedChoices: Lowercase, as Spanish writes the names of peoples; the English capital is kept for book-only peoples such as Andonitas, but this is a real-world term.

nebadon.name: Nebadon
nebadon.meaning: The local universe in which Urantia is, the creation of Michael (0:0.5, 35:0.1).

nebadon-corps-of-perfection.name: Cuerpo de Perfección de Nebadon
nebadon-corps-of-perfection.meaning: The local-universe corps of Spirit-fused ascenders; members may become Universe Aids and are associated with the Susatia (37:5.4, 37:9.7).

nebadon-corps-of-the-finality.name: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios de Nebadon
nebadon-corps-of-the-finality.meaning: The finality corps of Nebadon, whose leadership some in the universe hold that Jesus' soul-identity will later take in outer space (188:3.8).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de la Finalidad de Nebadon
rejected.reason: Follows the English word, but rule 4 requires the done form 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'.

nebadon-corps-of-the-finality.note: The papers mention this corps once, as an opinion held by 'those in the universe'; the translation must keep it as an opinion.

nebadon-revelatory-corps.name: Cuerpo Revelador de Nebadon
nebadon-revelatory-corps.meaning: A Nebadon group that requested and sponsored papers of this revelation (56:10.22).

rejected.reason: Reads as a body of revealed text, not a group of beings.

nebadon-revelatory-corps.note: The summary's details (twelve members, Mantutia's direction, Part II in 1934) were not checked in this task.

nebuchadnezzar.name: Nabucodonosor
nebuchadnezzar.meaning: The king of Babylon who overthrew Necho, besieged and took Jerusalem, and put Judah under Babylon (97:9.25, 97:6.4).

nebulae.name: nebulosas
nebulae.meaning: Cyclones of force started by the Paradise force organizers; they are the mother wheels of suns and their systems (15:4.4).

rejected.reason: Rare in Spanish; 'nebulosas' is the usual word in astronomy.

necho.name: Necao
necho.meaning: The Egyptian pharaoh whose army killed Josiah and who was later overthrown by Nebuchadnezzar (97:9.24, 97:9.25).

neighboring-planet.name: planeta vecino
neighboring-planet.meaning: The inhabited world near Urantia whose government the papers describe by special permission (72:12.3).

nether-paradise.name: Paraíso inferior
nether-paradise.meaning: The under side of the Isle of Paradise, the impersonal plane where the space presence of the Unqualified Absolute is focused and below which space seems to originate (11:2.8, 11:2.11, 15:4.1).

rejected.reason: "bajo" also means "base" or "low" in value and reads as a lesser Paradise.
Too colloquial for a term.
The reader must take "inferior" as "lower in position" (the opposite of "Paraíso superior"), not "lower in worth".

new-jerusalem.name: Nueva Jerusalén
new-jerusalem.meaning: The holy city the Jews expected the Messiah to set up as world capital, and the city John saw coming down from God (176:1.6, 52:7.11).

new-stone-age.name: Nueva Edad de Piedra
new-stone-age.meaning: The period in Europe overlapping the Bronze Age, with sun worship and roofless sun temples; its charms survive in Brittany (80:9.13, 80:9.14).

rejected.reason: Technical term; the English uses a plain phrase, and 'Edad de Piedra (Antigua)' is already set.

new-testament.name: Nuevo Testamento
new-testament.meaning: The Christian scriptures, mostly devoted to Paul's religious experience and convictions rather than to the religious life of Jesus (196:2.1).

niagara-falls.name: cataratas del Niágara
niagara-falls.meaning: The falls over Niagara limestone; the Great Lakes have emptied by this route for 37,000 years (59:3.9, 61:7.10).

nicodemus.name: Nicodemo
nicodemus.meaning: A wealthy, elderly member of the Sanhedrin who visited Jesus privately at night (142:6.1).

nicopolis.name: Nicópolis
nicopolis.meaning: The Greek 'city of victory' founded by Augustus after Actium; Jesus lodged there with Jeramy (133:2.5, 130:0.3).

nile-god.name: dios del Nilo
nile-god.meaning: The legendary Egyptian god who died and rose again, behind the Isis and Osiris rites; shown holding the infant prince with his ka (98:4.8, 111:0.5).

nile-valley.name: valle del Nilo
nile-valley.meaning: The valley of the Nile river in Egypt.

nirvana.name: Nirvana
nirvana.meaning: In Buddhism, a condition of supreme enlightenment and bliss with freedom from the desires of mortal life and from incarnation, which Siddhartha never clearly defined (94:8.16, 94:12.3).

rejected.reason: The English capitalizes the word.

noah-wine-maker-of-aram.name: Noé (vinicultor de Aram)
noah-wine-maker-of-aram.meaning: The real Noah, a wine maker of Aram, a river settlement near Erech, who recorded the river floods and urged boat-like houses; he and his family survived a great flood (78:7.5).

rejected.reason: Often means a wine seller, not a maker.
Aram here is a settlement near Erech, not the biblical land of Aram.

noah-wine-maker-of-aram.note: Aram is a river settlement near Erech (78:7.5); readers can confuse it with biblical Aram (Syria).

nod-land-of.name: Nod (tierra de)
nod-land-of.meaning: The dwelling place of the Nodites, descendants of the disloyal staff led by Nod, east of the second Eden, where Cain went (67:4.2, 74:8.8, 76:2.9).

rejected.reason: 'país' suggests a modern state.

nod-prince-s-corporeal-staff.name: Nod (del personal corpóreo del Príncipe)
nod-prince-s-corporeal-staff.meaning: The leader of the Dalamatia commission on industry and trade among the Prince's staff, first leader of the rebels, from whom the Nodites take their name (66:5.11, 73:1.3).

rejected.reason: Matches the earlier "Van (del cuerpo del Príncipe)", but "cuerpo" can read as the Prince's physical body; "personal corpóreo" follows the done term "corporeal staffs of Planetary Princes".

nod-prince-s-corporeal-staff.note: The terms already done use two forms for "Prince's staff": "personal corpóreo" and "cuerpo" (Van). A reviewer must unify them.

nodites.name: Noditas
nodites.meaning: The descendants of the rebel members of Caligastia's staff, named after Nod, the eighth race on Urantia (73:1.3, 77:2.1).

norlatiadek.name: Norlatiadek
norlatiadek.meaning: Constellation number seventy of Nebadon, with one hundred local systems including Satania and its headquarters on Edentia (15:14.6, 46:8.3).

north-america.name: América del Norte
north-america.meaning: The continent that the red man and later the Eskimos entered (64:7.18).

rejected.reason: Also correct; 'América del Norte' matches 'América del Sur' in the done list.

north-pole.name: Polo Norte
north-pole.meaning: The northern pole of the earth, which marine fossils reach (59:3.7).

ohio-river.name: río Ohio
ohio-river.meaning: The river whose banks near Louisville expose thick Devonian coral deposits (59:4.6).

old-testament.name: Antiguo Testamento
old-testament.meaning: The Hebrew scriptures, which Jesus treated as human writings that contain truth and error (159:4.1).

omniaphim.name: omniafines
omniaphim.meaning: Ministering spirits of the superuniverses created by the Infinite Spirit with the Seven Supreme Executives, who are their exclusive servants and messengers in the oversight of the superuniverses (26:1.13, 28:2.1, 28:2.2).

rejected.reason: Keeps the Hebrew-style plural; the done list uses -afines (seconafines, supernafines).

onagar.name: Onagar
onagar.meaning: The first truth teacher of early mankind, who led his fellows in the worship of "The Breath Giver" and now serves among the four and twenty counselors (63:6.7, 45:4.3).

onamonalonton.name: Onamonalonton
onamonalonton.meaning: A leader and spiritual deliverer of the red men about 65 000 years ago who turned them to the worship of the Great Spirit (64:6.7, 45:4.5).

one-truth.name: Verdad Única
one-truth.meaning: The object of worship that Singlangton taught the yellow race about one hundred thousand years ago, one truth instead of many (64:6.15, 45:4.8).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'a truth' (indefinite), which loses the contrast with many.
Philosophical and unusual in plain Spanish.

orange-race.name: raza anaranjada
orange-race.meaning: One of the six Sangik races; after a long struggle with the green men in Egypt it ceased to exist as a race about one hundred thousand years ago (64:6.13).

rejected.reason: Correct, but 'anaranjada' agrees in gender and reads better as an adjective.

original.name: Original
original.meaning: The I AM considered as the source reality that always is, in which the Actual and the Potential are both encircuited (115:3.11, 115:3.16, 0:3.22).

rejected.reason: The masculine reads as a person or as "the original copy" of a document.
Means "native of" or "derived from", which reverses the sense of a source.

forcedChoices: Spanish needs an article for the nominalized adjective; chose the neuter "lo" to match the done term "Actual, lo" and the triad Original, Actual, Potential (115:3.9).

orlandof.name: Orlandof
orlandof.meaning: A prince and teacher of the blue race who led tribes back to the true God as the 'Supreme Chief'; one of the twenty-four counselors (64:6.23, 45:4.6).

orvonon.name: Orvonon
orvonon.meaning: The enlightener of the indigo race who proclaimed 'The God of Gods'; one of the twenty-four counselors (64:6.26, 45:4.10).

orvonton-paradise-satellite.name: Orvonton (satélite del Paraíso)
orvonton-paradise-satellite.meaning: The seventh of the executive spheres of the Infinite Spirit near Paradise, named for and dedicated to the administration of the seventh superuniverse (13:4).

rejected.reason: "luna" names a natural moon; the English says "satellite".

orvonton-superuniverse.name: Orvonton (superuniverso)
orvonton-superuniverse.meaning: The seventh superuniverse, which contains the local universe of Nebadon and Urantia; its capital is Uversa (0:0.5, 15:14).

osiris.name: Osiris
osiris.meaning: The Egyptian god in whose judgment hall the soul of the dead was weighed for admission to bliss or consignment to hell (95:2.9).

outer-space.name: espacio exterior
outer-space.meaning: The space levels beyond the seven superuniverses, where uninhabited universes now mobilize (0:0.6, 12:1, 12:2.4).

rejected.reason: The reader must not bring the astronaut sense "space beyond Earth's atmosphere".
Means "later" more than "farther".

overcontrol.name: supercontrol
overcontrol.meaning: Control exercised from a higher level over all within a domain, as by the Ultimate over the master universe or by the Unqualified Absolute in infinity (0:1.10, 0:11.8, 118:2.4, 1:2.10).

rejected.reason: Spanish 'sobre-' often means excess, as in sobrecarga; reads as too much control.
Loses the coined single term and the family link.

overcontrol.note: Readers must not take 'super-' as colloquial 'very great'; it names control from a level above, as in Superalma for Oversoul. Family root: control (controladores).

pacific-ocean.name: océano Pacífico
pacific-ocean.meaning: The ocean that formed from the early world ocean and once covered nine tenths of the earth's surface (57:8.20, 57:8.21).

paleozoic.name: Paleozoico
paleozoic.meaning: The marine-life era of 250 million years, ending with the Permian (59:0.4, 59:6.11).

palestine.name: Palestina
palestine.meaning: The land of the eastern Mediterranean where Jesus lived.

palonia.name: Palonia
palonia.meaning: A local system of Nebadon where Lutentia rebelled and where Michael ruled for more than seventeen years as the Savior Sovereign (119:2.5, 119:2.6).

panama-isthmus.name: istmo de Panamá
panama-isthmus.meaning: The isthmus that rose and sank twice in the Cenozoic, joining or separating the Atlantic and Pacific (61:0.2, 61:1.12).

panoptia.name: Panoptia
panoptia.meaning: The only Satania world whose people stayed loyal in the Lucifer rebellion, under Ellanora; Panoptians now care for the Father's world on Jerusem (53:7.1, 53:9.1).

panorama-exhibit-jerusem.name: panorama de exposiciones (Jerusem)
panorama-exhibit-jerusem.meaning: The vast exhibit wall, five thousand miles around the Jerusem circles, that portrays the current status of every peopled world of Satania (46:5.23, 46:5.24).

rejected.reason: "exhibición" can suggest a show or performance in some regions; "exposición" is the plain museum word.
Loses "panorama" as the head noun of the English name.

pantheism.name: panteísmo
pantheism.meaning: The philosophy that denies the personality of God because God has no body; the papers name it, with materialism, as an extreme to avoid (1:5.11, 1:5.12, 103:8.6).

paradise.name: Paraíso
paradise.meaning: The stationary Isle at the geographic center of infinity and the dwelling place of the eternal God (0:0.5, 11:0.1).

rejected.reason: Lowercase reads as the general idea of heaven or the garden; the papers mean a specific place.

paradise-arrivals.name: Llegados al Paraíso
paradise-arrivals.meaning: The seventh stage of ascending mortals: those who reach Paradise with residential status, begin the course in divinity and absonity, and are to be mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality (30:4.31).

rejected.reason: "llegadas" as a noun is the act of arrival, not the persons who arrive.
Adds "newly", which the English does not say.

paradise-central-shining.name: Resplandor Central del Paraíso
paradise-central-shining.meaning: The central shining of the spiritual glory of the Universal Father and the eternal Deities at the center of Paradise, with which a servital can have "personal contact" (11:1.3, 13:0.3, 24:7.2); the papers do not say if it is a being or a manifestation.

rejected.reason: "brillo" is ordinary gloss or shine of a surface; too small for divine glory.
The English says "Shining", not "Light"; also near "luminosidad espiritual" already in the glossary.

paradise-citizens.name: Ciudadanos del Paraíso
paradise-citizens.meaning: Native resident beings of Paradise, of more than three thousand orders, who are not directly concerned with the ascent of will creatures (30:1, 11:2.11).

rejected.reason: Loses the status sense of "citizens".

forcedChoices: masculine generic "Ciudadanos": Spanish requires a gender; the masculine plural is the neutral generic for a mixed or sexless group.

paradise-companions.name: Compañeros del Paraíso
paradise-companions.meaning: A composite group of angels drawn from several seraphic and supernaphic orders, assigned to keep company with beings, chiefly ascendant mortals, who arrive alone on Paradise (25:8).

rejected.reason: Reads as an escort or attendant role, weaker than companionship.

forcedChoices: masculine generic "Compañeros": Spanish requires a gender; the group is mixed angels, so the generic masculine plural is the neutral form.

paradise-corps-of-the-finality.name: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios del Paraíso
aliases: Cuerpos de los Finalitarios del Paraíso
paradise-corps-of-the-finality.meaning: The general name for the seven finality corps mustered on Paradise, of which the Corps of Trinitized Finaliters is one (22:8.6, 26:11.2, 31:10.20).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de la Finalidad del Paraíso
rejected.reason: Closer to the English 'Finality', but the done term 'Corps of the Finality' is 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'; rule 4 requires that form.
That form is kept for 'Corps of Paradise Finaliters', one specific corps (31:10.3); the general name must differ.

Because 'Corps of the Finality' became 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios', the general 'Paradise Corps of the Finality' and the specific 'Corps of Paradise Finaliters' differ in Spanish only by the article 'los'. 'Cuerpo de la Finalidad' for the done term would keep the two apart.

paradise-corps-of-the-finality.note: Near-collision with corps-of-paradise-finaliters. A reviewer must decide whether to revisit 'Corps of the Finality: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'.

paradise-creator-sons.name: Hijos Creadores del Paraíso
paradise-creator-sons.meaning: The Creator Sons (Michaels), who originate on Paradise from the Father and the Son and go out to make and rule local universes (21:0.1, 5:3.6).

paradise-deities.name: Deidades del Paraíso
paradise-deities.meaning: The three existential Deities of Paradise: the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit (0:4.9, 0:12.12).

rejected.reason: Suggests polytheism; the English uses "Deities", already "Deidad" in the glossary.

paradise-energy.name: energía del Paraíso
paradise-energy.meaning: Energy that takes origin from, or is grasped by, the Isle of Paradise, the source of all cosmic force and the center of absolute gravity (11:8, 105:3.4).

rejected.reason: "paradisíaco" means "delightful" in ordinary Spanish.

paradise-force-organizers.name: organizadores de la fuerza del Paraíso
paradise-force-organizers.meaning: The Master Force Organizers of Paradise origin, who transmute space potency into primordial force and evolve it into the primary and secondary energies of physical reality (15:4.2, 12:2.4).

rejected.reason: Kept in line with "Directores del Poder del Universo", which uses the article.
The plural turns the cosmic force into a list of forces.

paradise-gravity.name: gravedad del Paraíso
paradise-gravity.meaning: The absolute, circular gravity grasp of the Isle of Paradise on all physical energy and matter of the master universe (11:8, 12:3, 42:2.12).

rejected.reason: Correct physics but less common; "gravedad" is the plain term in the sciences across Spanish countries.
The reader must not bring the sense "seriousness".

paradise-havona-system.name: sistema Paraíso-Havona
paradise-havona-system.meaning: The eternal central aggregation of Paradise, its satellites, and the Havona spheres, which forms the nucleus around which the superuniverses and outer space revolve (12:1, 14:1).

rejected.reason: Loses the compound name that the English hyphen makes.

paradise-havona-trinitized-sons.name: Hijos trinitizados por seres del Paraíso y Havona
paradise-havona-trinitized-sons.meaning: Sons trinitized by Paradise citizens and Havona natives acting together, held in reserve for future universe ages (22:7.8 context, 31:9).

rejected.reason: Calque of the English compound; not readable Spanish.

forcedChoices: spell out 'por seres del Paraíso y Havona': Spanish cannot stack the compound modifier; the short alias 'Hijos trinitizados Paraíso-Havona' is offered for tight sentences.

paradise-incarnation-commission.name: comisión de encarnación del Paraíso
paradise-incarnation-commission.meaning: A commission of seven unidentified Paradise personalities who arrived at the tomb before Jesus' morontia resurrection on April 9, A.D. 30 (189:1.1).

rejected.form: comisión del Paraíso para la encarnación
rejected.reason: Closes the English: it decides that the commission is from Paradise and exists for the incarnation.
"paradisíaco" means "delightful" in ordinary Spanish.

paradise-master-spirits.name: Espíritus Maestros del Paraíso
paradise-master-spirits.meaning: The Seven Master Spirits of Paradise, who express the combinations of the three Paradise Deities (16:0.1, 16:1.1).

paradise-sons-of-god.name: Hijos de Dios del Paraíso
paradise-sons-of-god.meaning: The Sons of God of Paradise origin: Creator Sons, Magisterial Sons, and Trinity Teacher Sons (20:0.1, 35:0.1).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'Sons of God's Paradise'.
'Paradisíaco' reads as 'idyllic'.

paradise-source-and-center.name: Fuente y Centro del Paraíso
paradise-source-and-center.meaning: The eternal Isle of Paradise as the second nondeity pattern among the Seven Absolutes of Infinity, the absolute of patterns and the foundation of gravity control (105:3.4); the packet summary ("the Universal Father") is not what 105:3.4 says, although 19:1.12 uses the phrase more broadly.

rejected.reason: The English uses "and", not a hyphen.
"paradisíaco" means "delightful" in ordinary Spanish.

paradise-trinity.name: Trinidad del Paraíso
paradise-trinity.meaning: The eternal union of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit (10:0.1, 15:0.1).

rejected.reason: The adjective reads as 'idyllic' in common use.

parsees.name: parsis
parsees.meaning: The followers of Zoroastrianism in India, for whom the dog is the sacred animal and in whose symbolism the fire myth persists (88:1.4, 69:6.6).

rejected.reason: Less usual plural.
Spanish writes the names of religious groups in lowercase, as with 'fariseos'.

parthia.name: Partia
parthia.meaning: The ancient Parthian kingdom, one of the powers whose trade and armies swept over Palestine (121:2.2).

patmos-isle-of.name: Patmos, isla de
patmos-isle-of.meaning: Index form of the island where the apostle John was banished for four years and wrote the Book of Revelation (historical place).

rejected.reason: Kept in line with "isla de Patmos"; the generic noun stays lowercase.

paul.name: Pablo
paul.meaning: Paul of Tarsus, missionary to the gentiles and founder of much of early Christian theology (194:4.0, 196:2.1).

pella.name: Pella
pella.meaning: The place by the Jordan where John baptized Jesus and where Jesus later had a camp in Perea.
pella.note: Meaning taken from the packet summary; I did not open a paragraph for it.

pennsylvania.name: Pensilvania
pennsylvania.meaning: The North American state, used as a geologic reference point for ancient rock layers (58:7.4).

pentecost-bestowal-of-spirit-of-truth.name: Pentecostés (otorgamiento del Espíritu de la Verdad)
pentecost-bestowal-of-spirit-of-truth.meaning: The day on which the Spirit of Truth was poured out upon all flesh after Jesus' ascension, which transformed the apostles and the believers (Paper 194, 194:2.17, 34:5.5).

rejected.form: Pentecostés (donación del Espíritu de la Verdad)
rejected.reason: 'Donación' reads as a charitable or legal donation; 'otorgamiento' keeps the sense of a gift that is conferred.

rejected.form: Pentecostés (efusión del Espíritu de la Verdad)
rejected.reason: Translates 'outpouring', not 'bestowal'; it is a different English word in the papers.

perea.name: Perea
perea.meaning: The province east of the Jordan, about equally gentile and Jewish, called 'the land beyond the Jordan', where Jesus kept his last headquarters near Pella (165:0.3, 163:5.1).

perfection.name: perfección
perfection.meaning: The state of being complete in divine quality, existential in Paradise-Havona and experiential (attained by growth) for evolutionary creatures; the papers contrast the perfect, the perfected, and the perfecting (32:3.14, 56:4.3, 106:1.1).

rejected.reason: Means fullness, not the quality of being perfect; breaks the family perfect/perfected/perfecting.
Ordinary sense is a psychological trait; the reader must not bring that sense to 'perfección'.

perfections-of-days.name: Perfecciones de Días
perfections-of-days.meaning: The 210 Trinity personalities who rule the ten major sectors of each superuniverse as personal vicegerents of the Ancients of Days (18:4.1, 18:5.4).

perfectors-of-wisdom.name: Perfeccionadores de la Sabiduría
perfectors-of-wisdom.meaning: Trinity-created beings who personify the wisdom of divinity in the superuniverses and counsel the Ancients of Days (19:2.1).

rejected.reason: says they are perfect, not that they bring wisdom to perfection
'perfeccionista' is a personal trait

perpetua.name: Perpetua
perpetua.meaning: Simon Peter's wife, a leader of the enlarged women's corps, who went with Peter on his missions and died in the arena at Rome (163:7.3).

persian-gulf.name: golfo Pérsico
persian-gulf.meaning: The body of water by whose ancient region the Planetary Prince's headquarters, Dalamatia, stood (66:3.1).

persians.name: persas
persians.meaning: The people who freed the Jews from Babylon and whose Zoroastrian ideas shaped Jewish heaven, hell, and devils (97:10.2, 95:6.6).

personal-aids-of-the-infinite-spirit.name: Auxiliares Personales del Espíritu Infinito
personal-aids-of-the-infinite-spirit.meaning: Beings, numbered in trillions, who serve only the Paradise presence of the Infinite Spirit and flash through the universes to execute his bidding, without a discoverable personality form (Paper 24, 24:4).

rejected.reason: 'Ayudantes' is already the fixed form for 'adjutant' (espíritus ayudantes de la mente); using it here would merge two different English words.
Reads as an office job title (personal assistant).

personality.name: personalidad
personality.meaning: The unique gift of the Universal Father, the one changeless reality in creature experience, which unifies body, mind, spirit, and soul without being any of them (0:5.11, 0:5.4, 1:5.13).

rejected.reason: 'Person' is a different English word in the papers.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) personalidad = 'character traits, temperament' or 'a celebrity'
rejected.reason: The reader must not read it as psychological character or as 'a famous person'; it is a bestowed reality.

personalized-adjusters.name: Ajustadores Personalizados
personalized-adjusters.meaning: Thought Adjusters who have received personality from the Father, usually after indwelling an incarnated Paradise Son or after unusual service (Paper 109, Paper 136).

rejected.reason: Loses the sense of an act of personalization.
The reader must not read it as 'custom-made'; it means 'given personality'.

pharisee-and-publican.name: fariseo y publicano
aliases: parábola del fariseo y el publicano
historia del fariseo y el publicano
