pharisee-and-publican.meaning: Jesus' parable of two men praying in the temple, a self-righteous Pharisee and a humble publican (tax collector), used to contrast bad and good religion and to show that salvation comes by faith, not works (167:5.1, 167:5.2, 140:5.7).

rejected.reason: The terms already done write 'fariseos' in lowercase; a common noun for a group stays lowercase in Spanish.
Explains the word instead of naming the parable; the papers keep 'publican' and gloss it once (167:5.1).

pharisees.name: fariseos
pharisees.meaning: The Jewish sect of strict observers of the law and tradition who often opposed Jesus (137:7.5).

phasaelis.name: Fasaelis
phasaelis.meaning: A new Greek city near the Jordan where the apostles first preached to mostly gentile hearers (143:0.2, 143:1.1).

rejected.reason: Spanish does not keep 'ph'.

philadelphia.name: Filadelfia
philadelphia.meaning: The city in Perea where Abner led the believers (Paper 166, 171).

philip-apostle.name: Felipe (apóstol)
philip-apostle.meaning: Philip, one of the twelve apostles and their steward, who invited others with 'Come and see' (139:5.1).

philip-tetrarch.name: Filipo (tetrarca)
philip-tetrarch.meaning: The tetrarch Philip, ruler of the domain whose capital was Caesarea-Philippi (157:3.1).

rejected.reason: 'Felipe' is the done form for the apostle; 'Filipo' is the usual Spanish form for the tetrarch and keeps them apart.

philistines.name: filisteos
philistines.meaning: The coastal people of Palestine who fought the Hebrews and defeated Saul (97:9.5, 97:9.13).

rejected.reason: Spanish has this figurative sense too; the context makes the people clear.

philo-of-alexandria.name: Filón de Alejandría
philo-of-alexandria.meaning: The Jewish philosopher of Alexandria whose religious experience, with that of Jesus and Paul, shaped early Christian doctrine (5:4.14).

philosopher-in-ephesus.name: filósofo de Éfeso
philosopher-in-ephesus.meaning: A progressive thinker of the local school of philosophy at Ephesus who asked Jesus what he meant by "soul" (133:6.4).

rejected.reason: Literal but does not read as a name in Spanish.

forcedChoices: "de Éfeso" can imply he was born there; the English says only that he was in Ephesus. The context (local school) supports "de".

phoenicians.name: fenicios
phoenicians.meaning: The ancient seafaring Semitic people of the Mediterranean coast north of Palestine.

phrygian-mystery-cults.name: cultos mistéricos frigios
phrygian-mystery-cults.meaning: The mystery cult of Phrygia centered on Cybele and her son Attis, whose imposing but degrading ceremonies celebrated the death and resurrection of Attis (98:4.3, 98:4.6, 98:4.7).

rejected.reason: Reads as cults that are a mystery; 'mistéricos' is the plain term for mystery religions.
'misterioso' means strange or secret, not a cult of initiation.

pilgrim-helpers.name: asistentes de los peregrinos
pilgrim-helpers.meaning: The first group of secondary supernaphim, who welcome the ascenders on the seventh (outer) circle of Havona and teach them an outline of every Paradise requirement (26:5.1, 26:5.2, 26:5.6).

rejected.reason: 'ayudantes' is taken by 'adjutant' (espíritus ayudantes de la mente); 'helper' is 'asistente' in 'serafines asistentes planetarios'.
'auxiliar' is taken by 'Aids' (Auxiliares Personales, Auxiliares del Universo).

pilgrim-helpers.note: 'asistente' now carries both 'helper' (planetary helper seraphim) and 'assistant' (administrative assistants, High Son Assistants) in the done terms. A reviewer must decide if the two English words need two Spanish words.

pilgrim-receivers-and-free-associators.name: receptores de peregrinos y asociadores libres
aliases: Receptores de Peregrinos y Asociadores Libres
pilgrim-receivers-and-free-associators.meaning: An order of Morontia Companions who are the social companions of new arrivals on the mansion worlds, welcome them on awakening, and stay with them until they leave the local universe as first-stage spirits (48:3.8).

rejected.reason: 'recibidor' is an entrance hall in much of the Spanish-speaking world.
'acogedor' is mainly an adjective (cozy); it does not read as a noun of office.
Changes the word; 'associator' is 'asociador' in 'asociadores primarios'.

pilgrim-receivers-and-free-associators.note: 'receptor' also means a receiving device (receptores de difusiones). In this term it means one who receives guests; the context must carry that.

planetary-custodians.name: custodios planetarios
planetary-custodians.meaning: The council of seventy guardians on each morontia world, the local authority in morontia affairs, who grant morontia form material and authorize the changes of form between spheres (48:2.18, 30:2.111).

rejected.reason: 'guardián' is used for 'guardian'; 'custodian' is 'custodio' in Custodians of Records.

planetary-helper-seraphim.name: serafines asistentes planetarios
planetary-helper-seraphim.meaning: The fifth order of seraphim, who come with the Planetary Adams and help the material uplift of the races (39:5.1).

rejected.reason: 'ayudante' is already 'adjutant' (espíritus ayudantes de la mente)
'Auxiliares' is already 'Aids' (Auxiliares Personales)

planetary-prince-of-urantia.name: Príncipe Planetario de Urantia
planetary-prince-of-urantia.meaning: The title first held by Caligastia; after Jesus defeated him on Mount Hermon, the title passed to Jesus (Christ Michael), with Machiventa Melchizedek a possible vicegerent (136:3.1, 93:10.6).

planetary-princes.name: Príncipes Planetarios
planetary-princes.meaning: Secondary Lanonandek Sons who rule the evolutionary worlds in the early ages (35:9.1, 50:1.1).

rejected.reason: longer; the English uses an adjective

planetary-sovereigns.name: Soberanos Planetarios
planetary-sovereigns.meaning: The title of a Planetary Prince after the bestowal Son proclaims his world settled in light and life (55:1.1).

planets.name: planetas
planets.meaning: Material spheres that circle suns, some of them inhabited by evolutionary mortals (15:6.11, 49:0.1).

plato.name: Platón
plato.meaning: The Greek philosopher of idealism, successor of Socrates, whom the papers rank as a philosopher rather than a religious teacher (92:5.12, 98:2.6, 130:4.1).

platonism.name: platonismo
platonism.meaning: The philosophy of Plato, which with Stoic doctrine shaped Hellenized Jewish thought (121:6.3).

poles-of-space-communication.name: polos de comunicación del espacio
aliases: polo planetario de comunicación del espacio
poles-of-space-communication.meaning: The planetary place where messages over the mind circuit are received, linked to the point of spiritual polarity (62:7.2, 17:3.1).

rejected.reason: 'comunicación espacial' suggests satellite technology.

polynesia.name: Polinesia
polynesia.meaning: The island region of the Pacific, whose islands were once more numerous and larger, crossed by Andite sailors from Japan (78:5.7, 79:5.9, 82:6.9).

polytheism.name: politeísmo
polytheism.meaning: The worship of many gods, which the papers call a relative unification of the deity concept and 'monotheism in the making' (5:4.2, 5:4.9, 104:1.9).

rejected.reason: Not a standard Spanish word.

pontius-pilate.name: Poncio Pilato
pontius-pilate.meaning: Pontius Pilate, the Roman procurator of Judea who presided at the trial of Jesus and ordered his crucifixion (185:1.1).

porshunta.name: Porshunta
porshunta.meaning: The oracle and master mind of the extinct orange race, who led a revival of higher living at Armageddon about 300 000 years ago and is one of the four and twenty counselors (45:4.7, 64:6.12).

potential.name: Potencial
potential.meaning: Reality that carries undisclosed capacity for growth; capitalized, the triodity of the Deity, Unqualified, and Universal Absolutes (0:4.7, 115:3.8, 115:3.16).

rejected.reason: A possibility is not a capacity for growth, and it breaks the family 'potencialidad'.

power.name: poder
power.meaning: Ordinarily the electronic level of material, linear-gravity-responsive matter; the papers also use it for sovereignty (0:6.2, 0:6.7).

rejected.reason: Covers only the physical sense and loses sovereignty; 'Poder' is used in 'Directores del Poder del Universo'.

powers-of-paradise.name: Poderes del Paraíso
powers-of-paradise.meaning: The divine presences on Paradise into whose presence ascending angels and mortals come at last, in context the Paradise Deities (27:7.6).

rejected.reason: "Potestades" names a rank of angels in Christian tradition, a sense the authors do not intend.
"fuerza" is a technical term for physical force in the papers.

praetorium.name: pretorio
praetorium.meaning: The addition to the fortress of Antonia where Pilate stayed in Jerusalem and before which he tried Jesus (185:0.2, 185:0.3).

primary-associators.name: asociadores primarios
primary-associators.meaning: Master Physical Controllers who store and conserve energy and act as living catalysts that convert space energies into physical states (29:4.32).

rejected.reason: "asociado" is reserved for "associate".

primary-associators.note: "asociador" is a rare word in Spanish but it reads as a term, as the English does.

primary-eventuated-master-force-organize.name: Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza Primarios Eventuados
primary-eventuated-master-force-organize.meaning: The first order of Master Force Organizers, whose space presence makes passive force active (29:5.2, 42:2.8).

rejected.reason: 'eventual' means possible or temporary
loses the special sense of 'eventuate' (absonite emergence)

primates.name: Primates
primates.meaning: The particular species, sprung from the mid-mammals, that were the direct animal ancestors of the human race and soon died out (62:4.2, 62:4.7).

rejected.reason: In Spanish it is the whole zoological order (monkeys, apes, humans); the papers name one species, so the capital stays.

primates.note: A reader can take "Primates" as the zoological order; only the capital marks the difference.

primitive-mortals.name: mortales primitivos
primitive-mortals.meaning: Mortals in the early stages of evolution on a world, before advanced civilization (e.g. 39:5.7 'primitive men').

rejected.reason: 'Primigenio' means 'original, first of all', which changes the idea from 'early stage' to 'origin'.

prince-of-peace.name: Príncipe de Paz
prince-of-peace.meaning: A title of the bestowal Son, who on normal worlds brings an age of peace; the papers apply it to Jesus and deny it to the Planetary Prince (52:6.1, 52:2.5, 68:3.5).

rejected.reason: Also used in Spanish, but the English has no article; both are natural.

prison-worlds.name: mundos prisión
prison-worlds.meaning: The seven satellites around the Father's world of Jerusem used as detention spheres for Lucifer and his followers (45:1.10, 45:1.11).

rejected.reason: Suggests a penal system for correction, which the text does not state.

probationary-nursery.name: guardería probatoria
probationary-nursery.meaning: The system finaliter world where Adjuster-indwelt children who die before they choose the Paradise career are raised; parents can serve there (49:6.11, 45:6.8).

rejected.reason: 'Probación' also means a religious novitiate.
'Vivero' is a plant nursery or fish farm.
Reads as a trial or test daycare.

probationary-nursery.note: 'Probatorio' in common Spanish leans to legal proof ('periodo probatorio'). A reviewer can prefer a form that says 'a period before the choice'.

proterozoic.name: Proterozoico
proterozoic.meaning: The life-dawn era of geologic history, between the prelife age and the era of developed marine life (59:0.3, 58:7.1).

protozoa.name: Protozoos
protozoa.meaning: The primitive single-celled animal organisms, such as the ameba, that survive from the first steps of life differentiation (58:7.2, 65:2.4).

rejected.reason: Correct but less common than 'protozoos' in neutral Spanish.

proverbs.name: Proverbios
proverbs.meaning: The Hebrew Book of Proverbs of the Old Testament, parts of which the papers say are taken almost verbatim from Amenemope's Book of Wisdom (95:4.5, 95:4.3).

rejected.reason: Ordinary word for sayings; loses the reference to the biblical book.

psalms.name: Salmos
psalms.meaning: The Book of Psalms, a collection of hymns that records varying concepts of God from Amenemope to Isaiah; Jesus recited psalms on the cross (96:7.3, 187:5.2).

ptolemais.name: Tolemaida
ptolemais.meaning: A coastal city of Palestine on Jesus' routes (128:3.2, 156:6.2).

public-builders.name: constructores públicos
public-builders.meaning: The seventh group of divine builders among the celestial artisans, who plan and construct the places of assembly other than those of worship (44:3.8).

rejected.reason: Adds a sense of civil engineering that the English does not have.

public-builders.note: 'constructores públicos' can read as builders employed by a government. The English has the same weakness.

punjab.name: Punyab
punjab.meaning: The region of northwestern India that received a continuous infiltration of Andite and Aryan blood (79:1.1, 79:4.3).

rejected.reason: Also accepted, but less common.
English spelling; Spanish usage adapts 'j' to 'y'.

pygmies.name: pigmeos
pygmies.meaning: The Pygmies of Africa, cited as surviving backward, nonsocial peoples without a marriage institution (68:1.6, 82:2.2).

qualified-absolute.name: Absoluto Condicionado
qualified-absolute.meaning: The Deity Absolute, the absolute potential segregated by the Father's choice, in contrast to the Unqualified Absolute (0:11.6, 0:10.1).

rejected.reason: 'Cualificado' means 'skilled, trained'.
'Calificado' means 'graded' or 'skilled'.

qualified-vicegerents-of-the-ultimate.name: Vicegerentes Condicionados del Último
qualified-vicegerents-of-the-ultimate.meaning: Beings who represent the Ultimate, influential in the superuniverse governments and represented by Reflective Image Aids, whose present whereabouts and function the papers do not reveal (15:10.21, 106:4.3, 117:7.4).

rejected.reason: 'Calificado' means skilled or graded; 'Qualified' is 'Condicionado' in 'Absoluto Condicionado', so it stays 'Condicionado'.
Loses the sense of a deputy who holds the authority of another.

quickeners-of-morality.name: vivificadores de la moralidad
quickeners-of-morality.meaning: Administrator seraphim who quicken the appreciation of cosmic morality, the interactions of liberty and loyalty, and portray mortal life as an unbroken chain (39:4.10, 39:4.13).

rejected.reason: 'quicken' here is to enliven, not to make faster.
Reads as a technical or chemical stimulus.

quickeners-of-morality.note: 'vivificar' also means to give life; the sense here is to make more alive and keen.

race-commissioners.name: comisionados de las razas
race-commissioners.meaning: High Commissioners in their first planetary service, who interpret and speak for the needs of the human races (37:5.5, 48:6.22).

rejected.reason: "racial" in Spanish can suggest racial policy or discrimination.

races.name: razas
races.meaning: The human races of Urantia: the Andonites, the six Sangik races, and later blends with Nodites and Adamites (63:4.1, 64:6.1, 78:4.3).

rachel-sister-in-law-of-jude.name: Raquel (cuñada de Judas, hermano de Jesús)
rachel-sister-in-law-of-jude.meaning: The sister-in-law of Jude, Jesus' brother, one of the ten women whom Jesus set apart for the ministry of the kingdom (150:1.1, 154:6.1).

racial-interpreters.name: intérpretes raciales
racial-interpreters.meaning: A group of seraphic transition ministers who help the race commissioners harmonize the differing viewpoints of the races on the inhabited worlds and the mansion worlds; 'sociologists and ethnic advisers of the first heaven' (48:6.22, 39:6.3).

rejected.reason: Suggests translation of languages; these beings interpret viewpoints, not words.
Acceptable, but longer and reads less as a term.

ragaba.name: Ragaba
ragaba.meaning: A town of Perea in the final mission, where the Pharisee Nathaniel gave a Sabbath breakfast for Jesus (165:0.1, 166:1.1).

ramah.name: Ramá
ramah.meaning: A Galilean town where the apostles worked and where Jesus talked with an aged Greek philosopher (146:3.1, 138:9.3, 156:6.2).

rantulia.name: Rantulia
rantulia.meaning: A local system of Norlatiadek next to Satania, through which the loyal intelligence corps sent calls for help to Edentia in the Lucifer rebellion (41:2.1, 53:6.5).

ratta.name: Ratta
ratta.meaning: Adamson's Nodite wife; with him she had sixty-seven children, among them the origin of the secondary midwayers (77:5.6).

reality.name: realidad
reality.meaning: All that exists on every universe level, originating in the infinite volition of the Universal Father and actualizing differentially in primal phases on many levels (0:4.1, 0:6.11).

rejected.reason: False friend: means the present time; the papers keep 'actual' and 'reality' apart.

rebecca-daughter-of-ezra.name: Rebeca (hija de Esdras)
rebecca-daughter-of-ezra.meaning: The eldest daughter of Ezra, a merchant of Nazareth, who fell in love with Jesus (127:5.1).

rebecca-daughter-of-joseph-of-arimathea.name: Rebeca (hija de José de Arimatea)
rebecca-daughter-of-joseph-of-arimathea.meaning: The daughter of Joseph of Arimathea, added by Jesus to the women's corps; she heard the women's report of the resurrection (150:1.1, 190:1.2).

rejected.reason: The terms already done use the standard Spanish 'Rebeca' (Rebecca, daughter of Ezra).

recents-of-days.name: Recientes de Días
recents-of-days.meaning: The youngest supreme Trinity directors of the superuniverses, 21,000 in number, who rule the minor sectors in groups of three, co-ordinate in nature with the Perfections of Days but subordinate in authority (18:5.1, 18:5.4, 15:13.6).

rejected.reason: The done list has 'Ancianos de Días' and 'Uniones de Días' without the article.

recorder-teachers.name: registradores-instructores
recorder-teachers.meaning: The sixth order of transition ministers: seraphim who record borderland transactions of the spiritual and the physical and teach techniques of fact recording (39:6.7, 48:6.30).

rejected.reason: 'Teachers' is 'Instructores' in the done terms; 'maestro' is reserved for 'Master'.

recorders.name: registradores
recorders.meaning: The beings who keep and forward the records of time and space, as on Uversa (25:6.4).

red-race.name: raza roja
red-race.meaning: The first of the six Sangik races, which went to the Americas (64:6.2).

reflective-image-aids.name: Auxiliares de Imagen Reflectivos
reflective-image-aids.meaning: Forty-nine beings created by the Reflective Spirits, seven on each superuniverse headquarters, true images of their Spirit ancestors minus reflectivity, who serve as their channel of communication (17:4.1, 15:10.2).

rejected.reason: 'Aids' is 'Auxiliares' in 'Auxiliares Personales'; and 'Reflectiva' ties the adjective to the image only.

forcedChoices: 'Reflectivos' agrees with 'Auxiliares': Spanish forces the adjective onto one noun; it marks the order as that of the Reflective Spirits, since the Aids themselves lack reflectivity (17:4.1).

reflective-mother-spirits.name: Espíritus Madre Reflectivos
reflective-mother-spirits.meaning: The Reflective Spirits in their role as mothers of the Reflective Image Aids and the seconaphim (Paper 17, Paper 28).

rejected.reason: 'Reflexivo' means 'thoughtful'; see Reflective Spirits.

reflective-spirits.name: Espíritus Reflectivos
reflective-spirits.meaning: Forty-nine Spirits of Trinity origin on the superuniverse capitals, seven of each Master Spirit type, who operate universe reflectivity and are the mothers of the seconaphim (28:0, 40:10.2, 13:1.10).

rejected.reason: 'Reflexivo' means 'thoughtful' or grammatical 'reflexive'; the term names the reflection (reflectivity) of images and information, not thought.
'Reflector' reads as a device (a spotlight, a mirror) rather than a quality.

religion.name: religión
religion.meaning: Religion is the personal experience of divinity in the consciousness of a moral being, a faith and assurance, not a system of belief (101:1.1, 101:0.3, 101:2.13).

rejected.reason: Means ritual worship or a sect; the papers contrast religion with mere ritual and dogma.

religious-leaders-in-rome.name: líderes religiosos de Roma
religious-leaders-in-rome.meaning: The Stoic, Cynic, and mystery-cult leaders in Rome whom Jesus taught for almost six months, preparing them for the later gospel (132:0.4).

rejected.reason: Also correct; "líderes" is more common in all regions.

remembrance-supper.name: Cena del Recuerdo
remembrance-supper.meaning: The supper Jesus established at the Last Supper, without ecclesiastical sanction, as the believer's symbolic meeting with Michael, in which the Master is really present (179:5.6, 179:5.8).

rejected.reason: A church term; the papers say the supper had no ecclesiastical sanction.
Good sense, but loses the plain word 'remembrance'.

reserve-corps.name: cuerpo de reserva
reserve-corps.meaning: Vast reserves of beings mobilized on Uversa, Salvington, and other capitals, sent on active service at the request of their group directors (30:3.10); also the mortal reserve corps of destiny (114:7.9).

reserve-corps-of-destiny.name: cuerpos de reserva del destino
reserve-corps-of-destiny.meaning: Groups of living mortals held in reserve to serve the superhuman government of a world in emergencies; Urantia has twelve such corps (114:7.7, 114:7.9).

reservists.name: reservistas
reservists.meaning: Mortals of the reserve corps of destiny, little known to their fellows, who act in emergencies to prevent the breakdown of culture or the extinction of truth (114:7.9, 114:7.7).
reservists.note: Spanish 'reservista' first means a military reservist; the context gives the special sense.

resident-governors-general.name: gobernadores generales residentes
resident-governors-general.meaning: The representatives of the twenty-four Jerusem counselors who co-ordinate superhuman administration on Urantia, without personal authority of their own (114:3.2, 114:6.2).

resurrection-halls.name: salas de resurrección
resurrection-halls.meaning: The halls on the mansion worlds and other receiving worlds where sleeping survivors are repersonalized in morontia form.

rejected.reason: 'Hall' here is a large room, not a corridor.

revelations-book-of.name: Apocalipsis, libro del
revelations-book-of.meaning: The book John wrote in exile on Patmos; the papers say it holds surviving fragments of a great revelation in an abridged and distorted form (139:4.14).

rejected.reason: Literal, but Spanish readers do not know the book by this name.
The plural English title is a common error; no Spanish reader knows this form.

revelations-book-of.note: The standard name 'Apocalipsis' loses the English link between 'Book of Revelation' and 'a great revelation' in 139:4.14. In common speech 'apocalipsis' also means a catastrophe; the reader must not bring that sense to the title.

reversion-directors.name: directores de reversión
reversion-directors.meaning: Beings who promote relaxation and humor by a return to past memories, ministers of exalted humor in the morontia and spirit realms (30:3.7, 48:4.3, 48:3.11).

rejected.reason: Loses the coined word "reversion" (a return), and the papers use the word itself.
"regresión" brings a psychological (hypnosis) or statistical sense.

reversion-directors.note: "reversión" also has a legal sense (return of property); the context removes it, but a reader can stop at it.

rhodes.name: Rodas
rhodes.meaning: The Greek island where Jesus and his companions stopped on the voyage from Ephesus to Cyprus (130:0.3, 133:7.1).

rich-man-of-rome.name: hombre rico de Roma
rich-man-of-rome.meaning: A wealthy Roman citizen and Stoic whom Jesus counseled to administer wealth as a wise trustee for later generations (132:5.1).

rig-veda.name: Rig-Veda
rig-veda.meaning: The oldest of the Vedas, a compilation of sacred writings made by the Brahmans to combat the Salem teachers; it contains some of the highest and lowest deity concepts (94:1.7, 96:0.1, 111:0.7).

rejected.reason: Also correct in Spanish; the hyphenated form keeps the English spelling that the papers use.

road-of-robbers.name: camino de los salteadores
road-of-robbers.meaning: The road up from Jericho to Bethany, called the "road of robbers", that Jesus took to the Passover (171:6.4); Barabbas was taken for robbery and murder on the Jericho road (185:5.3).

rejected.reason: 'ladrones' is taken by 'thieves' (ladrones crucificados con Jesús).
'bandido' is broader (outlaw); 'salteador' is a robber on the road.

road-of-robbers.note: 'salteador' is a little literary in some regions.

rocky-mountains.name: Montañas Rocosas
rocky-mountains.meaning: The mountain range of western North America.

rodan-of-alexandria.name: Rodan de Alejandría
rodan-of-alexandria.meaning: A Greek philosopher of Alexandria, taught Jesus' teachings by a former apostle of John, who discussed philosophy with Nathaniel and Thomas at Magadan (161:0.2).

rejected.reason: The name exists only in this book; the English spelling stays.

roman-catholic-church.name: Iglesia católica romana
roman-catholic-church.meaning: The Roman church that grew from early Christianity, whose medieval control helped cause the secular revolt (entity record roman-catholic-church; see 195:8.6).
roman-catholic-church.note: A full-text search for 'Catholic church' gives no result. The entity aliases 'world religion' and 'one religion' do not look like names of this church; a human must check them.

roman-centurion-of-jerusalem.name: centurión romano de Jerusalén
roman-centurion-of-jerusalem.meaning: The Roman officer at the crucifixion who, when he saw how Jesus died, said he must have been a Son of God and began to believe (187:5.5, 183:5.1).

roman-empire.name: Imperio romano
roman-empire.meaning: The Roman Empire of Jesus' time and after (195:3.1).

roman-soldiers-in-jerusalem.name: soldados romanos en Jerusalén
roman-soldiers-in-jerusalem.meaning: The Roman soldiers at Jerusalem, among them those who saw the stone roll from the tomb and fled to the fortress of Antonia (189:2.4).

rome.name: Roma
rome.meaning: The capital of the Roman Empire, a city of two million where Jesus spent time on his Mediterranean journey (132:0.2).

ruffians-at-nazareth.name: matones de Nazaret
ruffians-at-nazareth.meaning: The rough men, led by hirelings of Jesus' enemies, who seized Jesus at the Nazareth synagogue and tried to push him over a cliff (150:9.3).

rejected.reason: False friend: Spanish 'rufián' also means a pimp.
Implies habitual criminals, more than the English says.

rufus.name: Rufo
rufus.meaning: The son of Simon of Cyrene, whom Jesus and Ganid helped after an oxcart accident, and who later taught the gospel in Africa (130:6.6, 187:1.10).

russia.name: Rusia
russia.meaning: The present land named among places with Devonian red sandstone (59:4.7).

ruth-daughter-of-matthew.name: Rut (hija de Mateo)
ruth-daughter-of-matthew.meaning: Ruth, the eldest daughter of Matthew Levi, one of the ten women Jesus set apart for the ministering work of the kingdom (150:1.1).

ruth-sister-of-jesus.name: Rut (hermana de Jesús)
ruth-sister-of-jesus.meaning: Jesus' youngest sister, who married David Zebedee and went to Philadelphia (190:1.10).

ryonin.name: Ryonin
ryonin.meaning: A Japanese Buddhist teacher whose teachings, with those of Honen Shonin and Shinran, brought the God concept of Buddhism to the belief in Amida Buddha (94:12.2).

sabbath.name: sábado
sabbath.meaning: The seventh day of the week as a day of rest and worship, from its origin in Eden to its later Jewish rules (74:7, 147:6, 153:3).

rejected.reason: A loanword; plain Spanish names the day 'sábado'.
Descriptive phrase; loses the name of the day.

forcedChoices: lowercase 'sábado': Spanish writes days in lowercase; the English capital is the convention for a day name, not a coined term.
'sábado' is also the plain weekday Saturday: The context must show the day of rest; English 'Sabbath' is narrower than Spanish 'sábado'.

sacred-spheres-of-paradise.name: esferas sagradas del Paraíso
sacred-spheres-of-paradise.meaning: The three circuits of seven worlds each that circle Paradise inside Havona: the secret spheres of the Father, the luminous worlds of the Son, and the executive spheres of the Spirit (13:0.1-0.3).

rejected.reason: "santo" adds a sense of holiness of persons; the English says "sacred" and "spheres".

sadducees.name: saduceos
sadducees.meaning: The Jewish party of the priesthood and wealthy Jews who denied the resurrection and questioned Jesus in the temple (174:3.3).

sagittarius.name: Sagitario
sagittarius.meaning: The dense star cloud that is the rotational center of our minor sector (15:3.5).

sahara.name: Sahara
sahara.meaning: The region of North Africa, once open grazing land of an indigo-black people, later the great Sahara desert (78:1.10, 80:1.4).

rejected.reason: Also accepted by the RAE, but less used in Latin America.

saharans.name: saharianos
saharans.meaning: The people of the Sahara when it was open land, who met blue men, Nodites, and Adamites in the Mediterranean basin (78:1.11, 80:1.1).

rejected.reason: The name of a modern people of Western Sahara.

forcedChoices: Lowercase, as Spanish writes names of peoples.

salem.name: Salem
salem.meaning: The community of Melchizedek in Palestine, later Jebus and then Jerusalem, and the center of his teaching (93:2.4, 93:5.4).

salem-teachings.name: enseñanzas de Salem
aliases: mandamientos de la religión de Salem
salem-teachings.meaning: The teaching of one God that Machiventa Melchizedek gave at Salem and that his missionaries spread (93:4.16, 95:3.5).

salome-wife-of-zebedee.name: Salomé (esposa de Zebedeo)
salome-wife-of-zebedee.meaning: The wife of Zebedee and mother of the apostles James and John (Papers 125, 189).

salsatia.name: Salsatia
salsatia.meaning: The Census Director of Nebadon on Salvington, who is automatically aware of the birth and death of will in the local universe (37:8.4).

salvation.name: salvación
salvation.meaning: The free gift of God, received by faith, by which a person recognizes sonship with God and enters on eternal survival; it is not earned by works (150:5.3, 150:5.5, 193:1.2).

rejected.reason: Plain sense of physical rescue or ransom; changes the idea.
Brings a theology of payment for sin that the papers do not attach to the word.

salvington.name: Salvington
salvington.meaning: The headquarters world of the local universe of Nebadon (32:2, 41:1.3).

samaria.name: Samaria
samaria.meaning: The region of Palestine between Judea and Galilee whose people the Jews avoided (124:6.1, 162:0.1).

samaritans.name: samaritanos
samaritans.meaning: The people of Samaria in central Palestine, long at enmity with the Jews.

samuel.name: Samuel
samuel.meaning: The Hebrew prophet, a life Nazarite, whom the later record shows as crowning Saul (97:9.4, 135:1.2).

sanctities-of-service.name: Santidades del Servicio
sanctities-of-service.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim, the service indicators, who reveal the real nature and hidden motives of any service by man or angel (28:6.16, 28:6.19).

rejected.reason: Rare and abstract; not a natural word.

sanctities-of-service.note: 'Su Santidad' is the title of the pope; the reader must not bring that title to this order.

sangik-family.name: familia Sangik
sangik-family.meaning: The family of unusually intelligent children born suddenly to Badonite parents, the ancestors of all six colored races of Urantia (64:5.2, 64:7.1).

sangiks.name: Sangiks
sangiks.meaning: The six colored races, all descendants of the Sangik family that appeared among the highland Badonites (64:5.2, 64:6.17).

rejected.reason: Changes a name that exists only in this book.

sangiks.note: The Spanish plural of a word that ends in -k is not fixed. 'Sangiks' keeps the English; a reviewer can choose an invariable 'los Sangik'.

sanhedrin.name: Sanedrín
sanhedrin.meaning: The supreme Jewish council and court at Jerusalem that opposed Jesus and brought about his trial (184:0.1, 172:2.1).

sanobim.name: sanobines
sanobim.meaning: The energy-negative partner of the cherubim, the complement of being (38:7.2).

rejected.reason: the family plural follows serafines and querubines

sarah.name: Sara
sarah.meaning: The status wife of Abraham, mother of Isaac; brilliant and much younger than the Hebrew records say (93:9.3, 93:9.8).

rejected.reason: The standard Spanish form of the biblical name is 'Sara'.

sargon-king-of-assyria.name: Sargón (rey de Asiria)
sargon-king-of-assyria.meaning: The king of Assyria who, about 700 B.C., took more than 25 000 Jews of the northern kingdom into captivity and put other peoples in their place, a source of the Jewish-Samaritan enmity (143:4.1).
sargon-king-of-assyria.note: The papers also name an earlier Sargon, the priest of Kish who made himself king in Mesopotamia (78:8.8). Keep the two apart.

satan.name: Satanás
satan.meaning: A primary Lanonandek Son, Lucifer's first assistant, who represented the rebellion on Urantia (53:1, 53:5).

rejected.reason: Less common in neutral Spanish.
The reader must not bring the popular image of the devil as ruler of hell; in the papers Satan is a personal being of a defined order.

satania.name: Satania
satania.meaning: The local system of Urantia, with its capital on Jerusem, the site of the Lucifer rebellion (32:2.11, 53:0.1).

satisfactions-of-service.name: Satisfacciones del Servicio
satisfactions-of-service.meaning: A group of secondary seconaphim attached to the Divine Counselors, who promote the value of unselfish service and the satisfactions that come from it (28:5.4).

sato.name: Sato
sato.meaning: A direct descendant of Adamson and Ratta who led the tall Adamsonite progenitors of the Greeks westward to Greece (80:7.3).

saturn.name: Saturno
saturn.meaning: The planet that, with Jupiter, formed from the massive central part of the matter pulled from the sun by Angona (57:5.9).

saul-king.name: Saúl (rey)
saul-king.meaning: The first king of Israel, made king by the election of his troops after the defeat of the Ammonites, and defeated by the Philistines at Gilboa (97:9.4, 97:9.5, 97:9.13).

rejected.reason: Spanish uses Saulo for Paul of Tarsus; the king is Saúl.

scandinavians.name: escandinavos
scandinavians.meaning: The Scandinavian peoples, cited among those who had triad gods (104:0.3).

scotland.name: Escocia
scotland.meaning: The northern part of Great Britain, named in the geologic history as a site of the Caledonian Mountains, earthquakes, and volcanic activity (59:3.3, 59:3.6).

scythopolis.name: Escitópolis
scythopolis.meaning: The Greek, gentile city of marble buildings near Gilboa on the road from Nazareth to Jerusalem (124:6.4).

sea-of-galilee.name: mar de Galilea
sea-of-galilee.meaning: The lake of Galilee, about seven hundred feet below sea level and subject to sudden windstorms (151:5.2).

seas-of-glass.name: mares de cristal
seas-of-glass.meaning: Enormous crystal fields on headquarters worlds such as Edentia that serve as receiving fields for transport seraphim (43:1.10, 47:10.2).

rejected.reason: Literal, but 43:1.10 calls it a crystal, and "cristal" is the natural word for glass in this sense.

seas-of-glass.note: 47:10.2 quotes the Revelation of John. A translator must keep the same form inside that quotation.

seconaphim.name: seconafines
seconaphim.meaning: The ministering spirits of the superuniverses, offspring of the Reflective Spirits, in primary, secondary, and tertiary orders (28:3.1).

rejected.reason: the family plural follows serafines

second-experiential-trinity.name: segunda Trinidad experiencial
second-experiential-trinity.meaning: The second post-Havona Trinity, the Trinity Absolute, which cannot be infinite because it embraces derived Deities (0:12.3).

rejected.reason: 'Experimental' means 'trial' or 'test'.

second-garden.name: segundo jardín
second-garden.meaning: The home of Adam and Eve in Mesopotamia after they left the first garden (76:3.4, 76:3.7).

secondary-circuit-supervisors.name: Supervisores Secundarios de los Circuitos
secondary-circuit-supervisors.meaning: Universe Circuit Supervisors stationed on the superuniverse headquarters who supervise the spirit-energy circuits of the local universes; 84 691 are on Uversa (24:1.5, 24:1.9).

secondary-dissociators.name: disociadores secundarios
secondary-dissociators.meaning: Master Physical Controllers of great antigravity endowment, the reverse of the primary associators, who evolve limitless supplies of energy from little-known matter (29:4.10, 29:4.35).

rejected.reason: Loses the visible pair with 'asociadores primarios'.

secrets-of-greatness.name: Secretos de la Grandeza
secrets-of-greatness.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim who reflect the measure of greatness, which is unselfish service and self-control, working always with the Soul of Goodness (28:6.20, 28:6.21).

secularism.name: secularismo
secularism.meaning: The revolt from ecclesiastical control that brought liberties but then turned against God; it cannot bring peace to mankind (195:8.6).

rejected.reason: In Spanish it means mainly a political doctrine of a state free of church; the papers mean a wider godless revolt.

selective-assorters.name: clasificadores selectivos
selective-assorters.meaning: Morontia Power Supervisors who re-key ascenders as they pass from one morontia class or phase to another and who group morontia personalities for study and projects (48:2.21, 48:2.24).

rejected.reason: Stresses choice only; 'assort' is to sort into groups.

self-acting-adjusters.name: Ajustadores autoactuantes
self-acting-adjusters.meaning: A functional class of experienced Adjusters able to act on their own initiative, to leave the body, and to communicate with others of their kind (109:2.1, 109:2.9, 108:4.4).

rejected.reason: 'Autónomo' commonly means 'self-employed' or 'regional government'.

rejected.form: Ajustadores que actúan por sí mismos
rejected.reason: Explains and loses the form of a class name.

self-consciousness.name: conciencia de sí
self-consciousness.meaning: Awareness of oneself as a self, which implies the recognition of other selves and a mutual awareness (16:9.4, 133:6.6, 117:3.3).

rejected.reason: The English everyday sense "self-conscious" (shy); the papers do not mean it.
Forces a gender; "conciencia de sí" keeps it open.
Natural in philosophy but less clear to a general reader; kept as an alias.

self-consciousness.note: Family "self": root "sí" / "mismo" (conciencia de sí, mismidad). Check that "conciencia" is not read as "moral conscience"; 133:6.6 joins the two ideas, so the context helps.

selfhood.name: mismidad
selfhood.meaning: The state of being a self, which persists through the change of all its parts and which can transfer its seat of identity to the morontia soul (112:5.20, 112:2.20, 5:6.4, 6:5.5).

rejected.reason: Natural, but it stresses separateness from others, not being a self; kept as an alias.
Too technical for the general reader.
Same form as the term "personality"; 112:5.20 links them but they are not one word.
Not a standard Spanish word.

selfhood.note: "mismidad" is in the dictionary with the sense "the condition of being oneself", which matches, but it is rare. A reviewer can prefer "individualidad".

semites.name: semitas
semites.meaning: Peoples of the fertile crescent, among the most blended of Urantia peoples, including Chaldeans and Phoenicians (96:2.1).

sepphoris.name: Séforis
sepphoris.meaning: The town near Nazareth where Joseph died from an accident while at work on the governor's residence; capital of Galilee before Tiberias (126:2.1, 129:1.2).

serapatatia.name: Serapatatia
serapatatia.meaning: The brown-tinted, brilliant leader of the western or Syrian confederation of the Nodite tribes in the days of Adam (75:3.1).

seraphic-corps-of-completion.name: Cuerpo Seráfico de Culminación
seraphic-corps-of-completion.meaning: The same corps as the Corps of Seraphic Completion: seraphim who attained Paradise and the embrace of the Eternal Son (39:9.1, 39:9.2).

seraphic-evangels.name: evangelistas seráficos
seraphic-evangels.meaning: The first group of transition ministers, who guide new mansion world arrivals and proclaim the gospel of eternal progression (48:6.4).

rejected.reason: 'evangelio' is the message, not the messenger
loses the link to 'evangelio' (gospel)
the reader must not bring the sense of a Gospel writer or a sect preacher

seraphic-guardians-of-destiny.name: guardianes seráficos del destino
seraphic-guardians-of-destiny.meaning: The personal seraphim assigned to individual mortals who reach the third circle (113:0.1, 113:2.2).

seraphic-hosts.name: huestes seráficas
seraphic-hosts.meaning: The seraphim taken together as an organized body of ministry (Paper 39 title, 39:0.1).

rejected.reason: adds a military sense

seraphic-secoraphic-and-superaphic-trans.name: transporte seráfico, secoráfico y superáfico
seraphic-secoraphic-and-superaphic-trans.meaning: The carrying of personalities through space by seraphim, seconaphim, and supernaphim, in which the traveler is enseraphimed and sleeps in transit (39:2.12, 51:2.2, 23:2.22).

rejected.reason: the English writes 'secoraphic', not 'seconaphic'; keep its shape
the English writes 'superaphic'; keep its shape

seraphim.name: serafines
seraphim.meaning: The angels of the local universes, offspring of the Infinite Spirit as personalized on the local universe headquarters, who minister to mortals (39:0.1).

rejected.reason: The Spanish plural 'serafines' is the plain, standard word, and the English also uses the plain word.

seraphim-of-the-future.name: serafines del futuro
seraphim-of-the-future.meaning: Seraphim held in reserve for the ages of light and life and for mortals of modified ascension (39:0.8, 39:5.1).

seraphington.name: Seraphington
seraphington.meaning: The Paradise sphere that is the destiny world of the angels, the 'bosom of the Son and the Spirit' (13:1.22, 39:9.2).

rejected.reason: names unique to the book keep the English spelling, as Spiritington does

sermon-on-the-mount.name: Sermón de la Montaña
sermon-on-the-mount.meaning: The so-called Sermon on the Mount, which the papers say was Jesus' ordination charge to the twelve apostles and not the gospel itself (140:4.1, 140:5.1).

rejected.reason: Less common; 'Sermón' is the established form.

set.name: Set
set.meaning: The Egyptian god of darkness and evil, believed to have killed Osiris (95:5.12).

sethites.name: setitas
sethites.meaning: The priesthood that descended from Seth, noble teachers of health, religion, and education with advanced concepts of Deity (76:3.10).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes a group of people in lowercase; the done list has both uses, so a reviewer can align it.

seven-absolutes-of-infinity.name: Siete Absolutos de la Infinitud
seven-absolutes-of-infinity.meaning: The seven eternal premises of reality: Universal Father, Eternal Son, Infinite Spirit, Isle of Paradise, Deity Absolute, Universal Absolute, Unqualified Absolute (Paper 105).

rejected.reason: 'Infinidad' means 'a huge number'; 'infinity' is 'infinitud' in every term.

seven-spirits-of-god.name: siete espíritus de Dios
seven-spirits-of-god.meaning: The seven spirits that the prophet saw in vision 'like lamps burning before the throne'; elsewhere the papers apply 'the Seven Spirits of God' to the Seven Master Spirits (16:4.1).

rejected.reason: Keep the English case of each passage: capitals where the papers capitalize (16:4.1), lowercase in the vision passage.

seven-spirits-of-havona-circuits.name: Siete Espíritus de los Circuitos de Havona
seven-spirits-of-havona-circuits.meaning: The joint impersonal representation of the Infinite Spirit and the Seven Master Spirits to the seven circuits of Havona, one Spirit pervading each circuit (Paper 24, 24:1).

rejected.form: Siete Espíritus de los Circuitos havonianos
rejected.reason: Turns the coined place name into an adjective; the name Havona must stay in its English form.

seven-superuniverses.name: siete superuniversos
seven-superuniverses.meaning: The seven evolving superuniverses that circle Havona and, with it, form the grand universe (0:0.5, 0:0.6).

seven-supreme-executives.name: Siete Ejecutivos Supremos
seven-supreme-executives.meaning: Seven beings trinitized by the Father, Son, and Spirit who coordinate the administration of the grand universe as representatives of the Seven Master Spirits.

rejected.reason: 'Ejecutor' suggests one who carries out a sentence.

seven-supreme-power-directors.name: siete Directores Supremos del Poder
seven-supreme-power-directors.meaning: Seven beings created by the Seven Master Spirits who regulate physical power and energy in the grand universe and produce the Supreme Power Centers.

rejected.reason: Makes 'Supreme' modify the power, not the Directors.

seven-supreme-spirit-groups.name: siete grupos de Espíritus Supremos
seven-supreme-spirit-groups.meaning: The seven groups that make up the Supreme Spirits, the coordinating directors of the grand universe.

seven-worlds-of-infinite-spirit.name: siete mundos del Espíritu Infinito
seven-worlds-of-infinite-spirit.meaning: The seven sacred spheres of the Infinite Spirit that circle Paradise (Paper 13).

rejected.reason: 'Esfera' translates 'sphere', a different English word.

sevenfold-controllers.name: controladores séptuples
sevenfold-controllers.meaning: The controllers of the grand universe that God the Sevenfold encompasses together with its creators (116:5.1).

rejected.reason: Adds a genitive that the English does not state.

sevenfold-controllers.note: 'séptuple' follows 'Dios el Séptuple'. A reader can take 'controladores séptuples' as each controller being sevenfold; the English permits the same reading.

shang-ti.name: Shang-ti
shang-ti.meaning: The God of Heaven of Chinese belief, in which the teachings of Singlangton persisted and which preserved vestiges of a real God concept (94:5.3, 79:8.7).

shechem.name: Siquem
shechem.meaning: An ancient city of central Palestine on Jesus' route north in A.D. 25 and one of the places to which David Zebedee's runners carried news of the crucifixion (134:7.5, 186:3.2).

rejected.reason: The standard Spanish biblical form is 'Siquem'.

shensi.name: Shensi
shensi.meaning: A province of China where Andite immigrants stimulated advanced civilization and irrigation problems promoted co-operation (79:7.5, 79:8.6).

rejected.reason: Modern spelling; the English text uses the older form.

shiloh.name: Silo
shiloh.meaning: The place of an early temple of Yahweh, later discredited (97:9.17, 153:2.2).

rejected.reason: Also used, but less common in Spanish Bibles.

shiloh.note: 'silo' is also a grain silo; the capital letter and context separate them.

shinran.name: Shinran
shinran.meaning: A Japanese Buddhist teacher who, with Ryonin and Honen Shonin, brought the Buddhist God concept to the belief in Amida Buddha (94:12.2).

shinto.name: sintoísmo
shinto.meaning: The religion revered in Japan, listed by the papers among the composite religions (92:6.9, 92:6.15).

rejected.reason: Spanish uses the adapted form "sintoísmo" for the religion.

shunem.name: Sunem
shunem.meaning: An ancient village near Jezreel, known for the beautiful maiden and the works of Elisha, where Jesus later taught the evangelists and women about salvation (124:6.3, 150:5.1).

siberia.name: Siberia
siberia.meaning: The vast northern region of Asia.

sicilian-land-bridge.name: puente terrestre siciliano
sicilian-land-bridge.meaning: The land connection between Africa and Europe by Sicily, used by animals and peoples; its submergence went with the sinking of the eastern Mediterranean floor (64:1.5, 64:4.7, 73:7.1).

rejected.reason: A geographic claim the English does not make.

sicily.name: Sicilia
sicily.meaning: The Mediterranean island where Thomas preached; its ancient bay was a refuge for marine life (139:8.13, 59:6.9).

siddim.name: Sidim
siddim.meaning: The place of the battle after which Abraham led a confederation of eleven tribes and met Melchizedek (93:5.14, 93:9.9).

sidon.name: Sidón
sidon.meaning: The Phoenician city where Jesus and his associates spent almost two and a half weeks (156:0.1).

sierras.name: Sierras
sierras.meaning: The mountain range of the Pacific coast of North America near California, which began to form in the modern mountain-building stage and has risen ever since (60:3.3, 61:3.3).

rejected.reason: In lowercase it is the common Spanish noun for any mountain ranges.
Adds a name that the papers do not give; kept only as an alias for clarity.

sierras.note: In Spanish 'Sierras' is also a common noun; only the capital letter and the context mark it as a proper name.

significances-of-origins.name: Significaciones de los Orígenes
significances-of-origins.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim who are living ready-reference genealogies of the beings of the superuniverses and teach ascenders how to apply spirit ethics (28:6.4, 28:6.8).

rejected.reason: 'significados' is the done form for 'meanings'; 'significances' here carries importance as well as meaning.
Unnatural plural and drops the sense of meaning.

sikhism.name: sijismo
sikhism.meaning: The religion formed in the fifteenth century by Nanak and his followers from the teachings of Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism; the most recent of the composite religions (92:5.15, 92:6.13).

rejected.reason: Not the RAE spelling.

siloam-pool.name: Siloé (estanque)
siloam-pool.meaning: The pool in Jerusalem where Josiah washed the clay from his eyes and received his sight (164:3.8).

simeon-reputed-holy-man.name: Simeón (reputado hombre santo)
simeon-reputed-holy-man.meaning: A man of Israel reputed to be holy, whose tomb stood on the hill near Nazareth (once a high place of Baal) where Jesus went to look over the land (126:1.2).

rejected.reason: Asserts holiness; the English says only that he was reputed to be holy.
'supuesto' adds doubt that the English does not express.

simeon-reputed-holy-man.note: 'reputado' keeps the sense 'considered to be'; the reader must not take it as 'famous' only.

simeon-singer.name: Simeón (cantor)
simeon-singer.meaning: The Judean singer who, with Anna, greeted the infant Jesus in the temple (122:9).

rejected.reason: 'cantante' suggests a modern performer; 'cantor' fits a temple singer.

simians.name: simios
simians.meaning: The modern apes, which spring from the same mid-mammal tribe as man but from its most inferior couple (62:3.13).

simon-assistant-of-david-zebedee.name: Simón (asistente de David Zebedeo)
simon-assistant-of-david-zebedee.meaning: One of David Zebedee's assistants who, after the draught of fishes, fell at Jesus' knees and then left his nets to follow him (145:1.2).

simon-boat.name: Simón (barca)
simon-boat.meaning: The boat named "Simon", the former fishing boat of Simon Peter, built by Jesus' own hands, from which he taught the crowd (145:1.1).

rejected.reason: 'barco' suggests a larger vessel; 'barca' fits a lake fishing boat.

simon-brother-of-jesus.name: Simón (hermano de Jesús)
simon-brother-of-jesus.meaning: A younger brother of Jesus, the third son of Joseph and Mary.

simon-brother-of-jesus-mother.name: Simón (hermano de la madre de Jesús)
simon-brother-of-jesus-mother.meaning: Mary's brother Simon, who joined the Zealots and became an officer of the Galilean division, which caused an estrangement with Jesus (127:2.4).

simon-father-of-lazarus.name: Simón (padre de Lázaro)
simon-father-of-lazarus.meaning: The man of Bethany with three children, Mary, Martha, and Lazarus, whose home began a lifelong friendship with Jesus' family (124:6.9).
simon-father-of-lazarus.note: Other men named Simon in Bethany appear later (152:7.1, 172:0.1); they are not this Simon.

simon-of-bethany.name: Simón de Betania
simon-of-bethany.meaning: The man of Bethany whose family received the Nazareth families for the Passover in the youth of Jesus (125:2.1).

simon-of-bethphage.name: Simón de Betfagé
simon-of-bethphage.meaning: A man of Bethphage (spelled 'Bethpage' in the papers) at whose home Thomas stayed alone for a week after the crucifixion (191:0.13, 183:4.3).

rejected.reason: Follows the papers' spelling but is not the standard Spanish name of the village.

simon-of-bethphage.note: The papers spell the village 'Bethpage'; the standard Spanish 'Betfagé' is the same place.

simon-of-cyrene.name: Simón de Cirene
simon-of-cyrene.meaning: A Passover visitor from Cyrene in northern Africa who was made to carry Jesus' crossbeam; he became a believer and never knew that Jesus had once helped his son Rufus (187:1.10, 130:6.6).

simon-peter.name: Simón Pedro
simon-peter.meaning: Simon Peter, fisherman and spokesman of the twelve apostles (139:2.1).

simon-the-tanner.name: Simón el curtidor
simon-the-tanner.meaning: A tanner of Joppa who employed the Philistine interpreter Gadiah and did business with Gonod's agents (130:1.1).

simon-zelotes.name: Simón Zelotes
simon-zelotes.meaning: Simon Zelotes, the eleventh apostle, a former Zealot agitator of Capernaum (139:11.1).

rejected.reason: the English uses a surname-like form, not 'the Zealot'

sin.name: pecado
sin.meaning: The conscious, knowing, and deliberate transgression of divine law, a purposeful resistance to reality; distinguished from error and evil (67:1.4, 67:1.5, 89:10.2).

rejected.reason: Also a minor fault or absence; too weak.

singlangton.name: Singlangton
singlangton.meaning: The first of the yellow men to teach and lead his people in the worship of 'One Truth'; a member of the four and twenty counselors (45:4.8, 94:5.3).

sinkiang.name: Sinkiang
sinkiang.meaning: The region of central Asia through which Andite culture reached eastward from Mesopotamia (78:5.2).

rejected.reason: The present spelling; it changes the historical form that the English uses.

siva.name: Siva
siva.meaning: A member of the Hindu Trimurti: lord of life and death, god of fertility, and master of destruction (94:4.5, 104:1.5).

rejected.reason: Common in Spanish, but the English text uses 'Siva', which is also a standard Spanish form.

skepticism-philosophy.name: escepticismo (filosofía)
skepticism-philosophy.meaning: The Gentile philosophy that held knowledge to be fallacious and conviction and assurance impossible, a purely negative attitude (121:4.5); also doubt in general (102:6.4).

social-architects.name: arquitectos sociales
social-architects.meaning: Supervisor seraphim who further sincere social contacts and the social evolution of creatures, removing artificiality from associations; any group of three or more falls under them (39:3.4, 39:3.6).

rejected.reason: Loses the word 'architect', which the papers use in other terms (Master Architects).

socrates.name: Sócrates
socrates.meaning: The Greek philosopher who, with Plato and Aristotle, taught that virtue is knowledge and that it is better to suffer injustice than to be guilty of it (98:2.6, 98:0.1).

sodom.name: Sodoma
sodom.meaning: The city where Lot went to trade; its king joined Abraham's Hebron confederation (93:5.9, 93:5.14).

solemnities-of-trust.name: Solemnidades de la Confianza
solemnities-of-trust.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim who show all will creatures the solemnity of trust and reflect to the governing authorities the trustworthiness of any candidate (28:6.13).

rejected.reason: "fe" is faith, a different term.

solemnities-of-trust.note: "solemnidad" is also a liturgical feast rank in Spanish; the reader must take it as gravity or sacredness.

solitarington.name: Solitarington
solitarington.meaning: The fifth sacred world of the Father on Paradise, the 'bosom of the Father and the Spirit', rendezvous of unrevealed beings of the Father and the Infinite Spirit (13:1.15, 13:1.18).

solitary-messengers.name: Mensajeros Solitarios
solitary-messengers.meaning: The personal and universal messenger corps of the Infinite Spirit, the first order of the Higher Personalities of the Infinite Spirit, who function alone (23:0.1).

solomon.name: Salomón
solomon.meaning: The Hebrew king, son of David, who continued his father's tyranny and bankrupted the nation by his court and building program (97:9.16).

solomon-s-porch.name: Pórtico de Salomón
solomon-s-porch.meaning: A colonnade in the temple courts at Jerusalem where Jesus taught at the feast of tabernacles and made the formal announcement of his divinity (162:1.9, 162:7.1).

rejected.reason: Spanish 'porche' suggests the porch of a house.

solonia.name: Solonia
solonia.meaning: The seraphic chief of the planetary helpers, the 'voice in the Garden', who proclaimed the miscarriage of the divine plan after the Adamic default (51:3.5, 73:7.5).

somme-river.name: río Somme
somme-river.meaning: The French river, unchanged by the glaciers, along which Andonic tribes lived for tens of thousands of years (63:5.3).

son-fused-mortals.name: mortales fusionados con el Hijo
son-fused-mortals.meaning: Mortals who fuse with an individualized spirit of the Creator Son rather than with an Adjuster, and serve mostly in their superuniverse (40:9.1, 40:10.10, 22:6.1).

son-of-god.name: Hijo de Dios
son-of-god.meaning: In Jewish Messianic expectation, the latest name for the expected deliverer, after "servant of the Lord", "son of David", and "Son of Man" (136:1.1).
son-of-god.note: Same Spanish words as 'Sons of God' (Hijos de Dios), an order of beings. Only the number and the context separate them, as in English.

son-of-man.name: Hijo del Hombre
son-of-man.meaning: The title Jesus took from the Book of Enoch, for a being who left heavenly glory with the Father to bring salvation to mankind; Jesus adopted it as his inaugural title (126:3.8).

son-seizure.name: arrebatamiento por el Hijo
son-seizure.meaning: The way Adjuster-fused mortals of the primary modified order escape death: they are translated from among the living to the presence of the Sovereign Son (49:6.18).

rejected.reason: Reads as the Son being captured.
'rapto' commonly means a kidnapping.
Loses the sudden taking that 'seizure' carries.

son-seizure.note: 'arrebatamiento' has a Christian 'rapture' sense in Spanish; a reviewer must decide if that echo is acceptable.
forcedChoices: 'Son seizure' does not say who seizes; 'por el Hijo' names the Son as the agent, which the context of appearing before the Sovereign Son supports best.

son-spirit-ministers.name: ministros Hijo-Espíritu
son-spirit-ministers.meaning: The first group of supreme seraphim, who serve the high Sons and the Spirit-origin beings of the local universe, the Universe Son and the Universe Spirit (39:1.2).

rejected.form: ministros del Hijo y del Espíritu
rejected.reason: Explains the compound and loses its form as a name.
Breaks the 'minister/ministry' family (ministerio) that the papers use for angelic service.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) ministro = government minister or clergyman
rejected.reason: The reader must not bring the cabinet or the church office to it; it means one who ministers.

sonarington.name: Sonarington
sonarington.meaning: The sacred sphere of Paradise that holds the secret of the incarnation of the divine Sons (13:1.8).

sons-of-god.name: Hijos de Dios
sons-of-god.meaning: All the orders of divine sonship, classified as descending, ascending, and trinitized Sons (20:0.1, 35:0.1).

sons-of-thunder.name: hijos del trueno
sons-of-thunder.meaning: The nickname Jesus gave James and John, the sons of Zebedee (139:3.1).

sontad.name: Sontad
sontad.meaning: The first child of Andon and Fonta, the first creature born on Urantia wrapped in protective coverings; he led the clan after his parents died (63:3.1, 63:3.5).

soul.name: alma
soul.meaning: The morontial, evolving self that the mind and the indwelling Adjuster create together through moral choices, which can survive death (111:0-111:2, 0:5.10).

rejected.reason: Literary or theological; suggests the souls of the dead in folk religion.
Already the glossary form for "spirit", a different concept.
The reader must not bring the common sense of an immortal soul given at birth; the papers' soul is created and grows.

souls-of-goodness.name: Almas de la Bondad
souls-of-goodness.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim who reflect goodness and work inseparably with the Secret of Greatness (28:6.20, 28:6.21).

souls-of-peace.name: almas de la paz
souls-of-peace.meaning: The third order of planetary helper seraphim, whose ministry brings "peace on earth and good will among men"; their chief Vevona heralded Michael's birth (39:5.5).

south-africa.name: África del Sur
south-africa.meaning: The southern part of Africa as a landmass, joined in past ages by land bridges to Antarctica, South America, and Australia (61:2.3).

rejected.reason: Names only the modern country; the geologic context can mean the whole southern region.

south-africa.note: "África del Sur" keeps both readings open and matches "América del Sur".

south-america.name: América del Sur
south-america.meaning: The continent of the western hemisphere, peopled mainly by the red race with later admixtures (Papers 57-64, 79:5).

rejected.reason: Regional variant; 'América del Sur' is neutral.

sovereign-michaels.name: Migueles Soberanos
sovereign-michaels.meaning: Creator Sons who completed the sevenfold bestowal and hold full sovereignty over their local universes (21:0.5, 20:6.9).

rejected.reason: The family root is 'Miguel'.

space-levels.name: niveles del espacio
space-levels.meaning: The concentric elliptical paths of the master universe around Paradise, separated by relatively quiet zones (12:1.1, 11:7.7).

rejected.reason: Correct, but 'espacial' often reads as spaceflight; 'del espacio' is plainer.

spain.name: España
spain.meaning: The present European country; the papers name it in the geology of the Mediterranean and in the migrations of the indigo and Andite peoples (61:3.8, 80:2.2).

spirit.name: espíritu
spirit.meaning: That which responds to the spirit circuit of the Eternal Son; a level of reality distinct from matter and mind, and in man the divine spirit that indwells the mind (0:6.1, 0:5.9, 0:6.8).

rejected.reason: 'Soul' is a separate term in the papers (0:5.10); 'alma' must stay for it.
Archaic, and carries the sense of a soul in purgatory.
The reader must not bring the ghost, the mood, or the distilled-liquor senses to the term.

spirit-advocate.name: Espíritu-Abogado
spirit-advocate.meaning: The member of a conciliating commission, appointed by the judge-arbiter, who presents evidence and safeguards the rights of all personalities involved (25:2.7).

rejected.reason: Closes the compound to 'an advocate of spiritual type'; the English leaves open whether 'Spirit' names the nature of the being or its domain.
Reads as 'the Spirit's lawyer', which changes the idea.

spirit-co-ordinators.name: coordinadores del espíritu
spirit-co-ordinators.meaning: The third group of superior seraphim, based on Salvington, who prepare ascenders for the transition from the highest morontia level to newborn spirit status (39:2.6).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'religious coordinators' (a parish role).
Implies they coordinate spirit beings; their work is the transition to spirit status.

spirit-fused-mortals.name: mortales fusionados con el Espíritu
spirit-fused-mortals.meaning: Ascending mortals who fuse, after death and at reawakening on the mansion worlds, with an individualization of the premind spirit of the Third Source (the local universe Mother Spirit) rather than with an Adjuster; they normally remain in their local universe (40:9.1, 40:10.2).

rejected.reason: 'Fundido' also means 'melted' and colloquially 'burnt out, broken'.
'Por' makes the Spirit the agent of the fusion instead of the partner in it.

spirit-mortals.name: mortales espíritu
spirit-mortals.meaning: Mortals of origin who have attained spirit status in the ascension (cf. 39:2.6 'newborn spirit beings').

rejected.reason: Reads as 'spiritually minded mortals' on earth, the opposite of the intended status.
Reads as 'spirited mortals'.

spirit-mother.name: Madre Espíritu
spirit-mother.meaning: The local universe Mother Spirit (Divine Minister) seen as the mother of the local creation (Paper 34).

rejected.reason: That is the fixed form of 'Mother Spirit'; the English inverts the order here, so the Spanish does too.

spirit-of-god.name: espíritu de Dios
spirit-of-god.meaning: The liaison of all spiritual ministry, the union of the spirits of the Father, the Son, the Spirit, and God the Sevenfold; in scripture also used for the Infinite Spirit or the local Creative Spirit (8:5.3, 8:5.6, 34:6.7).

rejected.reason: The capital would close the reading to one person; the English lowercase keeps the wider sense of 8:5.6. Use the capital only where the English has it (8:5.3).

spirit-of-truth.name: Espíritu de la Verdad
spirit-of-truth.meaning: The spirit of the Creator Son, also of the Father, poured out at Pentecost as the new teacher that leads believers into all truth (194:2.3, 194:2.11, 194:3.8).

rejected.reason: Without the article it reads as a quality ('a truthful spirit'); 'de la Verdad' names the one spirit.

spiritington.name: Spiritington
spiritington.meaning: The third of the seven sacred worlds of the Father around Paradise, the 'bosom of the Spirit', home of the high beings that represent the Infinite Spirit; its secrets involve reflectivity (13:1.9, 13:1.10).

rejected.reason: Rule 3: a name that exists only in this book keeps its English spelling.

spirits-of-brotherhood.name: espíritus de la fraternidad
spirits-of-brotherhood.meaning: Planetary helper seraphim who work for racial harmony and social co-operation among the races (39:5).

rejected.reason: 'Hermandad' also names a religious confraternity or a guild.

spirits-of-the-havona-circuits.name: Espíritus de los Circuitos de Havona
spirits-of-the-havona-circuits.meaning: The Seven Spirits of the Havona Circuits considered as an order (Paper 24).

rejected.reason: Turns the name Havona into an adjective.

spirits-of-trust.name: espíritus de la confianza
spirits-of-trust.meaning: Planetary helper seraphim of the Adamic regime who inculcate trust into the minds of evolving men (39:5.7).

rejected.reason: Without the article it reads as 'trustworthy spirits' (de confianza = reliable), which changes the idea.

spiritual-energy-manipulators.name: manipuladores de energía espiritual
spiritual-energy-manipulators.meaning: Celestial artisans who study the laws of spiritual energy and develop improved techniques for its intake by morontia and other beings (44:5.4).

rejected.reason: Loses the match with the other 'energy manipulators' of 44:5.
The reader must not bring the sense of deceit; it means one who handles energy.

spironga.name: spironga
spironga.meaning: Spirit offspring of the Bright and Morning Star and the Father Melchizedek; spirit helpers of the local universe who do the routine spirit tasks of Nebadon (37:10.2, 43:0.4).

rejected.reason: Coined name; keep the English spelling, as with 'spornagia'.

splandon.name: Splandon
splandon.meaning: The fifth major sector of Orvonton, with headquarters at Umajor the fifth, which contains the minor sector of Ensa (15:14.7).

spornagia.name: spornagia
spornagia.meaning: Animal creatures, neither spirits nor persons, who care for the material phases of the architectural headquarters worlds from Jerusem to Salvington (37:10.3).

st-lawrence-river.name: río San Lorenzo
st-lawrence-river.meaning: The river and valley of eastern North America, named in the geologic history for volcanic activity and glacial advance (59:4.16, 61:7.5).

rejected.reason: The standard Spanish name is 'San Lorenzo'.

stars.name: estrellas
stars.meaning: The suns of space; early peoples deified them, and in India they were held to be the glorified souls of great men (85:5.1).

stationary-sons-of-the-trinity.name: Hijos Estacionarios de la Trinidad
stationary-sons-of-the-trinity.meaning: The Trinity-origin administrators of Havona and the superuniverses, of fixed number, including the Ancients of Days and the Universal Censors (22:1.13 'stationary numbers').

rejected.reason: 'Fijo' can read as permanent in post; 'estacionario' keeps the coined English word.
Means 'posted' or 'parked'; changes the idea.

forcedChoices: 'Estacionarios': The English does not say whether 'stationary' refers to fixed numbers or fixed posts; 'estacionario' keeps both readings, but its ordinary sense (seasonal or stalled) must not be brought to it.

stephen.name: Esteban
stephen.meaning: The Greek believer in Jerusalem who talked with Jesus years before, was stoned for his preaching, and became the first martyr of the Christian faith (128:3.6).

stoicism-religion.name: estoicismo
stoicism-religion.meaning: The Greek philosophy of a controlling Reason-Fate and virtue as its own reward, which reached a sublime morality but remained a philosophy and never became a religion (121:4.3).

stone-age-old.name: Edad de Piedra (Antigua)
stone-age-old.meaning: The period 'commonly regarded as the Old Stone Age', which the papers equate roughly with the latter half of human history from the arrival of the Planetary Prince; Europe's research on it concerns the blue men (64:0.2, 64:6.24).

rejected.reason: A technical term with its own dating; the papers use the popular name with 'commonly regarded'.
'Vieja' reads as colloquial in this compound.

student-visitors.name: estudiantes visitantes
student-visitors.meaning: Celestial beings of many types who visit headquarters and other worlds as observers, exchange pupils, and student helpers; a courtesy colony registered on Uversa, allowed on all inhabited planets (30:3.11, 48:3.10).

rejected.reason: Keeps the English word order but reads unnaturally in Spanish.

sumerians.name: sumerios
sumerians.meaning: The people who appeared in Mesopotamia with a full-grown culture; they began two hundred thousand years ago after the submergence of Dalamatia (77:4.7).

sun-urantia-s.name: sol (de Urantia)
sun-urantia-s.meaning: The sun of Urantia's solar system, an offspring of the Andronover nebula (41:9.4, 57:5.1).

suns.name: soles
suns.meaning: The stars of space, which also serve as way stations for energy circuits (41:3.1).

superior-seraphim.name: serafines superiores
superior-seraphim.meaning: The second order of seraphim, who serve in the local universe administration, including transporters and recorders (39:2.1).

supernaphim.name: supernafines
supernaphim.meaning: The angelic ministering spirits of the central universe and Paradise, in primary, secondary, and tertiary orders, who serve the pilgrims of Havona and the Paradise residents (Paper 26:1, 27:0).

rejected.reason: The terms already done give 'seraphim' as 'serafines'; the same -im to -ines pattern keeps the angelic family visible.
Not a natural Spanish plural; mixes the Hebrew plural with Spanish spelling.

superuniverse-centers.name: Centros de los Superuniversos
superuniverse-centers.meaning: The third order of Supreme Power Centers, a thousand on the capital of each superuniverse, which send out the specialized power circuits (29:2).

superuniverse-wards.name: pupilos del superuniverso
superuniverse-wards.meaning: Ascending mortals as first-stage spirits on the training worlds of a superuniverse, placed under the guardianship of the Ancients of Days (30:4).

rejected.reason: Suggests favor or patronage rather than legal guardianship.
The reader must take "pupilo" as a person under guardianship, not only as a school pupil.

superuniverses.name: superuniversos
superuniverses.meaning: The seven evolutionary universes of time and space that circle Havona (0:0.5, 15:0.1).

supervisor-seraphim.name: serafines supervisores
supervisor-seraphim.meaning: The third order of seraphim, assigned to constellation service (39:3.1).

supremacy.name: Supremacía
supremacy.meaning: The first level of experiential divinity, in which Paradise Deity evolves experientially in two phases that unify in the Supreme Being (0:7.7, 0:3.22).

rejected.reason: Rare in Spanish; the plain noun is 'supremacía'.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) dominance of one group over another
rejected.reason: The reader must not bring this; the sense is a level of Deity.

supremacy-guides.name: guías de la supremacía
supremacy-guides.meaning: The secondary supernaphim who teach the "spiritual graduates" on the sixth circle of Havona, distinct from the Graduate Guides (26:6.1, 26:6.4).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'supreme guides', a rank, not guides in Supremacy.

supreme.name: Supremo
supreme.meaning: God the Supreme, the evolving Deity of time and space, who becomes the highest finite manifestation of the total will of God (117:0.1).

rejected.reason: Is a separate alias of the Supreme in the papers ('Supreme Being'); the term here is the bare 'Supreme'.

supreme-center-supervisors.name: Supervisores Supremos de los Centros
supreme-center-supervisors.meaning: Seven beings who coordinate the master energy circuits of the grand universe, each on a world of the Seven Supreme Executives.

rejected.reason: Implies one Supreme Center, which the papers do not say.

supreme-chief.name: Jefe Supremo
supreme-chief.meaning: The name under which Orlandof led the blue race back to the worship of the true God (64:6.23, 45:4.6).

rejected.reason: Carries a modern political sense.

supreme-circuit-supervisors.name: Supervisores Supremos de los Circuitos
supreme-circuit-supervisors.meaning: Seven beings created by the Infinite Spirit who regulate the circuits of Havona from the pilot worlds.

rejected.reason: Ambiguous: 'Supremos' can attach to the circuit.

supreme-council-of-destiny.name: Consejo Supremo del Destino
supreme-council-of-destiny.meaning: The Paradise council of the presiding heads of the finaliter corps, with Grandfanda as chief.

rejected.reason: Without the article it reads as a council that assigns destinations.

supreme-council-of-salvington.name: consejo supremo de Salvington
supreme-council-of-salvington.meaning: The supreme council of the local universe at Salvington, made up of three members from each system and seven from each constellation (33:8.3, 45:3.22, 188:3.12).

supreme-council-of-universe-adjustments.name: Consejo Supremo de Ajustes del Universo
supreme-council-of-universe-adjustments.meaning: The Paradise body formed by the reserve corps of Unions of Days, which handles adjustments in universe affairs.

rejected.reason: 'Universe' as a noun phrase follows 'del Universo' in 'Directores del Poder del Universo'.

supreme-council-of-unlimited-authority.name: consejo supremo de autoridad ilimitada
supreme-council-of-unlimited-authority.meaning: The governing body proclaimed by the Ancients of Days when a local universe is settled in light and life: one hundred Faithfuls of Days presided over by the Union of Days (55:10.1, 55:10.6).

rejected.reason: 'Absoluta' has a special sense in the papers (the Absolutes).

supreme-creators.name: Creadores Supremos
supreme-creators.meaning: The Creators of time and space who, in association with Paradise Deity, contribute to the evolution of the Supreme Being (0:7.9).

rejected.reason: Adjective first reads as praise, not a name.

supreme-executive-7-of-orvonton.name: Ejecutivo Supremo n.º 7 (de Orvonton)
supreme-executive-7-of-orvonton.meaning: The one of the Seven Supreme Executives who acts from executive sphere number seven and directs the affairs of Orvonton, the seventh superuniverse.

rejected.reason: '#' is not the normal Spanish sign for a number; 'n.º' is.

supreme-executives.name: Ejecutivos Supremos
supreme-executives.meaning: The Seven Supreme Executives, one group of the Supreme Spirits, who coordinate the grand universe administration.

supreme-lanonandek-councils.name: consejos supremos Lanonandek
supreme-lanonandek-councils.meaning: Councils on the constellation headquarters, presided over by the senior Most High associate of the Constellation Father, that select System Sovereigns from the Lanonandek reserves (35:9.4).

rejected.reason: Capitalizes 'councils', which the text does not; and 'de los' makes the Lanonandeks the owners, not the order the councils serve.

forcedChoices: lowercase 'consejos supremos': The text writes 'supreme Lanonandek councils' in lowercase (35:9.4); only the name Lanonandek keeps its capital.

supreme-mind.name: Mente Suprema
supreme-mind.meaning: The mind of the Supreme Being, given by the Infinite Spirit, which unifies the spirit person of God the Supreme with the power of the Almighty Supreme.

rejected.reason: 'Mind' is 'mente' in all terms.

supreme-power-centers.name: Centros Supremos del Poder
supreme-power-centers.meaning: Living beings created by the Supreme Power Directors that control and direct the physical energies of space in the grand universe.

rejected.reason: 'Power' is 'Poder' in 'Directores del Poder del Universo'; one word for one meaning.

supreme-power-directors.name: Directores Supremos del Poder
supreme-power-directors.meaning: The seven beings created by the Seven Master Spirits who regulate physical power in the grand universe and are the progenitors of the Supreme Power Centers.

rejected.reason: 'Power' is 'Poder' in 'Directores del Poder del Universo'.

supreme-rulers.name: Gobernantes Supremos
supreme-rulers.meaning: The highest rulers of the universe, named without saying which beings they are; the context does not decide whether it means the superuniverse authorities or Deity (43:3.4, 54:4.5, 18:3.8).

rejected.reason: 'Sovereign' is a separate English word in the papers (System Sovereigns).

supreme-seraphim.name: serafines supremos
supreme-seraphim.meaning: The first order of local universe seraphim, associated with the Seraphic Corps of Completion (39:1.1).

rejected.reason: 'Supremo' capitalized is God the Supreme; this adjective stays lowercase

supreme-spirits.name: Espíritus Supremos
supreme-spirits.meaning: The seven groups of spirit beings that act as coordinating directors of the grand universe administration, including the Master Spirits, the Supreme Executives, and the Reflective Spirits.

supreme-trinity-personalities.name: Personalidades Supremas de la Trinidad
supreme-trinity-personalities.meaning: Beings created by the Paradise Trinity in fixed numbers who carry out its administrative policies and justice in the grand universe; the Ancients of Days are among them (18:3.8).

rejected.reason: Makes 'Supreme' modify the Trinity, as if it were a different Trinity.

supreme-ultimate.name: Supremo-Último
supreme-ultimate.meaning: A future Deity reality related to both the Supreme and the Ultimate; the papers name its secrets and spirits but leave its nature open (13:1.18, 13:2.10, 0:9.5).

rejected.reason: Without the hyphen, 'Último' reads as an adjective: 'the last Supreme'.

survival-of-mortal-death.name: supervivencia (a la muerte mortal)
survival-of-mortal-death.meaning: The continuation of the personality beyond physical death through the immortal soul in partnership with the Adjuster, which depends on the choice to do the Father's will (112:2, 112:3, 5:5).

rejected.reason: Regional variant; "supervivencia" is the neutral standard.
The reader must not bring the sense of only getting through physical danger.

susa.name: Susa
susa.meaning: The Mesopotamian city that prospered in flood times; Jesus and his companions visited it before Charax (78:8.2, 130:0.3).

susanna-daughter-of-ezra-of-alexandria.name: Susana (hija de Esdras de Alejandría)
susanna-daughter-of-ezra-of-alexandria.meaning: One of the five women who went to anoint Jesus' body and found the empty tomb (189:4.4).

rejected.reason: Both are common biblical names with standard Spanish forms.

susanna-daughter-of-ezra-of-alexandria.note: "Ezra" is rendered "Esdras", the usual Spanish form of the name; a reviewer can check that it fits a person who is not the biblical scribe.

susanna-daughter-of-nazareth-chazan.name: Susana (hija del jazán de Nazaret)
